children.title: Working-Face Representation
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral faces represented through provisional active constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Face Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral face induced by provisional active inequalities, allowing additional active constraints under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The associated working-face representation is \[F_W:=\{x\in P:A_Wx=b_W\}.\] If \(F_W\ne\varnothing\), then \(F_W\) is a face of \(P\). Define \(I(F_W):=\{i:A_ix=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F_W\}\). Then \(W\subseteq I(F_W)\), and the direction space parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(F_W)\) is \[\{p\in\mathbb R^n:Ep=0,\ A_{I(F_W)}p=0\}.\] Thus provisional working constraints represent a candidate face, while additional inequalities may be active because of degeneracy or redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected inequalities imposed as equalities represent a nonempty face, but the face may have additional active inequalities. Its affine direction space is determined by the original equalities and all inequalities active throughout the face.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_W=P\cap\{x:A_Wx=b_W\}\) is a face, and its complete active-index set \(I(F_W)\) may strictly contain \(W\).

notation.meaning: Rows and right-hand sides indexed by the working set
Indices active at every point of the represented face

children.title: Primal-Dual KKT Representation
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal and dual quantities organized for numerical solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual KKT Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex quadratic program with affine equality and greater-than inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ex=d,\quad Ax\ge b,\] where \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and suppose the feasible set is nonempty. A feasible point \(x\) is a global minimizer if and only if there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \[Hx+c-E^Ty-A^Tz=0,\qquad z_i(A_ix-b_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Together with \(Ex=d\), \(Ax-b\ge0\), and \(z\ge0\), these conditions give the coupled primal-dual KKT representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic objective over a nonempty polyhedron, a feasible point is globally optimal exactly when equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfy stationarity and componentwise complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The feasible set \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible \(x\) is globally optimal if and only if some \((y,z)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies stationarity and complementarity.

children.title: Slack-Multiplier Complementarity Representation
children.top_down_role: Inequality structure represented through slack and multiplier pairs.

assumptions_latex: \(s,z\in\mathbb R^m\) correspond componentwise to the inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality KKT conditions are \(Ax-b-s=0\), \(s\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(SZe=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise slack-multiplier form used by primal-dual interior-point systems.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(s:=Ax-b\) and diagonal matrices \(S:=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\) and \(Z:=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\). The inequality part of the KKT system is then represented by \[Ax-b-s=0,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad SZe=0,\] where \(e\) is the all-ones vector. Exact complementarity means \(s_i z_i=0\) for every index. A primal-dual interior-point perturbation replaces the last equation by \(SZe=\mu e\) with \(\mu>0\), together with \(s>0\) and \(z>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inequality is represented by a nonnegative slack and multiplier whose product is zero; interior-point methods replace zero products by a common positive barrier parameter.

children.title: Full-Space KKT Factorizations
children.top_down_role: Coupled symmetric-indefinite factorization families.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space KKT Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct symmetric-indefinite solution of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the equality-constrained system \[K\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\r\end{bmatrix},\qquad K:=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^T\\E&0\end{bmatrix},\] assume that \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and that \(p^THp>0\) for every nonzero \(p\in\ker E\). Then \(K\) is nonsingular. A full-space direct method selects a symmetric permutation \(P\), computes \[P^TKP=LDL^T,\] where \(L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) has nonsingular symmetric one-by-one or two-by-two pivot blocks, and recovers \((p,y)\) by permutation and triangular, block-diagonal, and backward substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space direct method solves the nonsingular coupled KKT system using a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization followed by substitutions.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(H\in\mathbb S^n\) is positive definite on \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT matrix \(K\) is nonsingular and can be solved through a symmetric-indefinite factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\).

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage cost of the pivoted full KKT factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=n+m\) be the order of the dense KKT matrix. A dense pivoted symmetric-indefinite \(LDL^T\) factorization requires \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(N^2)\) factor storage; each subsequent triangular and block-diagonal solve costs \(O(N^2)\). Sparse costs instead depend on ordering and fill and admit no dimension-only refinement at this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense full-space KKT factorization is cubic in system order with quadratic factor storage; sparse costs depend on fill and ordering.
assumptions_latex: The KKT matrix is treated as dense and has order \(N=n+m\).
A stable symmetric pivoting strategy using one-by-one or two-by-two pivots is employed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{factor\ work}=O(N^3),\quad\operatorname{storage}=O(N^2),\quad\operatorname{solve\ work}=O(N^2).

children.title: Range-Space Schur-Complement Methods
children.top_down_role: Constraint-space elimination and multiplier-centered solution families.

children.title: Range-Space Reductions
children.top_down_role: Constraint-space elimination organized around multiplier-sized reduced systems.

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating the primal step reduces the KKT equations to an \(m\)-dimensional range-space equation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal elimination for equality-constrained QP systems with positive-definite Hessian.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Hp+E^Ty=-g\) and \(Ep=r\). Because \(H\) is invertible, stationarity gives \(p=-H^{-1}(g+E^Ty)\). Substitution into feasibility yields the range-space reduction \[Sy=-r-EH^{-1}g,\qquad S:=EH^{-1}E^T.\] After solving this \(m\)-dimensional system, the primal step is recovered from \(p=-H^{-1}(g+E^Ty)\). The reduction requires applications of \(H^{-1}\), normally realized by linear solves, and is especially appropriate when the number of equality constraints is smaller than the primal dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step produces a multiplier system in the constraint range; solving it and one Hessian system recovers the full KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: Linear systems with nonsingular \(H\) can be solved without explicitly forming \(H^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\), \(Sv=Ew\) where \(Hw=E^{\mathsf T}v\); each implicit product uses one solve with \(H\), while column assembly uses \(m\) right-hand-side solves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free implementation and solve count for the range-space reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit product with \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) is evaluated by forming \(t=E^{\mathsf T}v\), solving \(Hw=t\), and returning \(Ew\); neither \(H^{-1}\) nor a dense Schur matrix need be formed. Explicit column assembly requires solving with \(H\) for the \(m\) columns of \(E^{\mathsf T}\), after which a factorization of \(S\) may be reused for multiple multiplier right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the range-space operator with one Hessian solve per product, or solve for all constraint right-hand sides to assemble it for reuse.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Range-Space Reduction

assumptions_latex: The classical range-space reduction attempts to eliminate the primal variable through \(H^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H\) is singular, the classical formula is undefined even though the full KKT matrix may remain nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact applicability boundary of primal-block range-space elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formula \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) requires nonsingular \(H\). Singularity of \(H\) invalidates this classical primal-block elimination but does not imply singularity of \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^{\mathsf T}\\E&0\end{bmatrix}\): for \(H=[0]\) and \(E=[1]\), the KKT matrix is nonsingular. Such cases require another elimination, a null-space method, or a full-space factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular Hessian blocks classical range-space elimination but need not make the coupled KKT problem singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Primal-Block Boundary

children.title: Schur-Complement Systems
children.top_down_role: Reduced linear systems formed through block elimination of primal variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite range-space Schur complement of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The range-space Schur complement \[S:=EH^{-1}E^T\] belongs to \(\mathbb S_{++}^m\). Consequently, for every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^m\), the system \[Sy=-r-EH^{-1}g\] has a unique solution \(y\in\mathbb R^m\). The system may be treated by a positive-definite direct factorization or by conjugate gradients using products with \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite Hessian and independent equality constraints, the range-space Schur complement is symmetric positive definite and uniquely determines the multiplier step.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=EH^{-1}E^T\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), so the Schur-complement equation has a unique multiplier solution.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) may be row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T})=\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T})=\operatorname{rank}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank and null-space structure of the Schur matrix under positive-definite primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) with \(H\succ0\), \(y^{\mathsf T}Sy=\|H^{-1/2}E^{\mathsf T}y\|_2^2\). Consequently, \(\ker S=\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\operatorname{rank}S=\operatorname{rank}E\). Thus \(S\) is positive definite exactly when \(E\) has full row rank; redundant equality rows make it positive semidefinite and singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite H, the Schur matrix loses rank exactly when the equality matrix loses row rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur Rank Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range-space Schur-complement solution of a KKT system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eliminates primal variables through a positive-definite leading block, identifies the full-row-rank condition for a positive-definite multiplier system, and records the associated block inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad G\in\mathbb{S}^n,\qquad G\succ0,\] and define \(S=AG^{-1}A^T\). Then \(S\succeq0\), and \(S\succ0\) if and only if \(A\) has full row rank. Under \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), the KKT equations \[K\begin{bmatrix}-p\\\lambda^*\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\h\end{bmatrix}\] can be solved by \[S\lambda^*=AG^{-1}g-h,\qquad Gp=A^T\lambda^*-g.\] Moreover, \[K^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}G^{-1}-G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}AG^{-1}&G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}\\S^{-1}AG^{-1}&-S^{-1}\end{bmatrix}.\] The method is especially useful when systems with \(G\) are well conditioned and inexpensive to solve, such as when \(G\) is diagonal or block diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite primal block G, block elimination produces S=A G-inverse A-transpose. This matrix is positive semidefinite in general and positive definite exactly when A has full row rank. In the full-row-rank case, solve the multiplier system, recover the primal step with G, and obtain the stated block inverse. The method is attractive when solves with G are easy and well conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)=m\ \text{for the unique reduced solve and inverse formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S:=AG^{-1}A^T\succeq0,\qquad S\succ0\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{rank}(A)=m;\qquad S\lambda^*=AG^{-1}g-h,\qquad Gp=A^T\lambda^*-g,\qquad K^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}G^{-1}-G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}AG^{-1}&G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}\\S^{-1}AG^{-1}&-S^{-1}\end{bmatrix}\ \text{when }\operatorname{rank}(A)=m.

children.title: Multiplier Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Recovery quality, conditioning, and reuse considerations for multiplier-centered solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent multiplier-recovery procedures for an exact equality-constrained KKT step with a positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and suppose \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(Ep=r\) and \(Hp+g\in\operatorname{range}(E^T)\). A primal-first recovery computes the unique multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) from \[(EE^T)y=-E(Hp+g).\] A range-space recovery instead computes it from \[(EH^{-1}E^T)y=-r-EH^{-1}g.\] For an exact KKT step, both procedures return the same multiplier satisfying \(E^Ty=-(Hp+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact KKT step with a positive-definite Hessian and independent constraints, the multiplier can be recovered either from stationarity after the primal solve or from the range-space Schur system, and the results agree.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The systems \((EE^T)y=-E(Hp+g)\) and \((EH^{-1}E^T)y=-r-EH^{-1}g\) recover the same unique multiplier for an exact KKT step.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The computed primal vector \(\widehat p\) need not satisfy stationarity exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique least-squares multiplier solves \((EE^{\mathsf T})\widehat y=-E(H\widehat p+g)\), and the remaining residual is the orthogonal projection of \(H\widehat p+g\) onto \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier recovery and residual diagnosis for an inexact primal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact primal vector \(\widehat p\), define \(\widehat y\in\arg\min_y\|H\widehat p+g+E^{\mathsf T}y\|_2\). Full row rank makes this multiplier unique, and it satisfies \((EE^{\mathsf T})\widehat y=-E(H\widehat p+g)\). The residual \(\rho=H\widehat p+g+E^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\) satisfies \(E\rho=0\) and is the component of \(H\widehat p+g\) in \(\ker E\); its norm measures stationarity error that no equality multiplier can remove.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inexact primal solution, recover the least-squares multiplier and use the remaining null-space component as the irreducible stationarity defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Multiplier Recovery

assumptions_latex: The stationarity equation \(E^{\mathsf T}y=-w\) is considered for a specified vector \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A multiplier exists exactly when \(w\in\operatorname{range}(E^{\mathsf T})\); when one exists, all are \(y_0+\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\), and uniqueness holds exactly when \(E\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundary for equality-multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=Hp+g\), the equation \(E^{\mathsf T}y=-w\) is solvable if and only if \(w\in\operatorname{range}(E^{\mathsf T})\). If \(y_0\) is one solution, every solution is \(y_0+v\) with \(v\in\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\). Thus a consistent multiplier is unique if and only if \(E\) has full row rank; redundant constraints permit distinct multipliers representing the same stationarity vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency need not prevent multiplier recovery, but it destroys uniqueness; inconsistency occurs when the stationarity vector lies outside the constraint-transpose range.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Recovery Rank Boundary

children.title: Null-Space Basis Construction
children.top_down_role: Explicit, implicit, sparse, and orthogonal representations of feasible directions.

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank with \(m<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete orthogonal factorization of \(E^T\) constructs an orthonormal basis \(Z\) of \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense orthogonal construction of an explicit null-space basis.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a full-row-rank matrix \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Compute a complete orthogonal factorization \[E^T=[Y\ Z]\begin{bmatrix}R\\0\end{bmatrix},\] where \([Y\ Z]\) is orthogonal, \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), and \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular upper triangular. Output \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\). It satisfies \(EZ=0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker E\). Householder QR may store the orthogonal factors implicitly when explicit formation of \(Z\) is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete orthogonal factorization of the constraint transpose yields orthonormal range and null-space bases; the null-space columns are the algorithm's output.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Construction

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthonormal null-space construction for possibly rank-deficient constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E=U\Sigma V^T\) has rank \(r\), then \[Z:=V_{(:,r+1:n)}\] satisfies \(EZ=0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and \(\operatorname{range}Z=\ker E\). In floating-point arithmetic the selected dimension depends on a numerical-rank threshold; singular values near that threshold make the computed nullity sensitive to perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right singular vectors associated with zero singular values form an orthonormal null-space basis, including for rank-deficient constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z=V_{(:,r+1:n)}\text{ is an orthonormal basis of }\ker E.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing SVD Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic construction from a nonsingular constraint column block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a column permutation, write \(E=[E_B\ E_N]\) with \(E_B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) nonsingular. Solve \(E_BD=-E_N\) and form, in the permuted coordinates, \[N=\begin{bmatrix}D\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-E_B^{-1}E_N\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(EN=0\), \(N\) has full column rank, and \(\operatorname{range}N=\ker E\). The construction can exploit a sparse factorization of \(E_B\), but fails for a singular selected block and need not be orthogonal or well conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular constraint column block yields a fundamental null-space basis by solving for basic variables in terms of the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: After a column permutation, \(E=[E_B\ E_N]\) with square nonsingular \(E_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N=\begin{bmatrix}-E_B^{-1}E_N\\I\end{bmatrix}\text{ is a full-rank basis of }\ker E.
knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental Null-Space Basis Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense storage and arithmetic regimes for explicit and implicit null-space representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rank \(r\), an explicit dense basis \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) requires \(\Theta(n(n-r))\) storage. When \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank with \(m\le n\), Householder factorization of \(E^T\) costs \(O(nm^2)\), stores its reflectors in \(O(nm)\) space, and applies the represented orthogonal transformation to a vector in \(O(nm)\) work. Explicit formation of all null-space columns incurs additional work and storage, so implicit factors are preferable when nullity is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit bases store every null-space column, whereas compact Householder factors have quadratic-in-rank construction cost and avoid nullity-sized storage.
assumptions_latex: For the QR bounds, \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(m\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage}(Z)=\Theta(n(n-r));\quad\operatorname{QR\ work}=O(nm^2),\quad\operatorname{reflector\ storage}=O(nm).

notation.meaning: Number of independent equality rows in the full-row-rank QR regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit and Implicit Construction Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit feasible-direction representation without explicit basis columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\) has full row rank, then \[P=I-E^T(EE^T)^{-1}E\] is symmetric, idempotent, satisfies \(EP=0\), and fixes every vector in \(\ker E\); hence it is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker E\). For rank-deficient \(E\), the exact extension is \(P=I-E^\dagger E\). Projector products can be computed from a factorization without forming an explicit basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orthogonal null-space projector represents feasible directions implicitly and extends to rank-deficient constraints through the pseudoinverse.
assumptions_latex: The inverse formula assumes \(E\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^T=P,\quad P^2=P,\quad\operatorname{range}P=\ker E.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the constraint null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Null-Space Projector

children.title: Reduced-Hessian QP Solves
children.top_down_role: Lower-dimensional quadratic systems restricted to feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique KKT primal step is \(p=p_0+Zq\), where \((Z^THZ)q=-Z^T(Hp_0+g)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction of an equality-constrained convex quadratic subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Ep=r\), first compute any \(p_0\) satisfying \(Ep_0=r\), and represent every feasible step as \(p=p_0+Zq\), where \(EZ=0\). Minimize the quadratic over \(q\) by solving \[(Z^THZ)q=-Z^T(Hp_0+g).\] If \(Z^THZ\) is positive definite, this system has a unique solution. Output \(p=p_0+Zq\); an equality multiplier may subsequently be recovered from \(E^Ty=-(Hp+g)\). The reduced system has dimension \(n-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterize feasible steps with a particular solution plus null-space coordinates, solve the positive-definite reduced-Hessian system, and reconstruct the primal step.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian QP Solves

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: \(Ep_0=r\), \(EZ=0\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible \(p\) is stationary exactly when \(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hp+g)=0\); positive-semidefinite reduced curvature makes this sufficient for global optimality, and positive-definite reduced curvature also gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility and reduced-stationarity certificate for a reduced-Hessian QP solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reconstructed vector \(p=p_0+Zq\) is stationary on \(\{p:Ep=r\}\) if and only if \(Ep=r\) and \(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hp+g)=0\). If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\), these equalities certify global optimality on the affine feasible set; if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), they certify its unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality feasibility plus a zero reduced gradient is the exact stationarity test; semidefinite reduced curvature makes it sufficient for optimality, and positive-definite curvature also gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Optimality Certificate

assumptions_latex: The dense positive-definite reduced Hessian has already been assembled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dense Cholesky factorization uses \(O(k^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(k^2)\) storage, followed by \(O(k^2)\) arithmetic per right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage cost after dense reduced-Hessian assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense \(k\times k\) positive-definite reduced Hessian, a Cholesky factorization requires \(O(k^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(k^2)\) storage. Each subsequent solve with the stored factors requires \(O(k^2)\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense reduced Hessian costs cubic work to factor and quadratic work per subsequent right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Reduced-Solve Complexity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(R\succeq0\), a minimizer exists exactly when \(c\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), and it is unique exactly when \(R\succ0\); any negative-curvature direction makes the reduced quadratic unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature and compatibility classification of the reduced unconstrained quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Up to a constant, the reduced objective is \(\phi(q)=\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}Rq+c^{\mathsf T}q\). If \(R\succ0\), its unique minimizer solves \(Rq=-c\). If \(R\succeq0\) is singular, a minimizer exists if and only if \(c\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), and then all minimizers are \(q=-R^\dagger c+v\) with \(v\in\ker R\). If this range condition fails, a zero-curvature direction makes the objective unbounded below. If some \(d\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Rd<0\), the objective is unbounded below even when stationary points exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite reduced curvature gives one minimizer; singular semidefinite curvature requires a range condition and can give many; incompatible flat or negative-curvature directions cause unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Curvature Outcomes

children.title: Basis-Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes governing basis stability and reduced-system quality.

assumptions_latex: The columns of \(N\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker E\).
The restricted Hessian satisfies \(\alpha\|v\|^2\le v^THv\le\beta\|v\|^2\) on \(\ker E\), with \(0<\alpha\le\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(N^THN)\le(\beta/\alpha)\kappa_2(N)^2\), with no basis-conditioning factor when \(N\) is orthonormal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of reduced Hessians under orthonormal and general null-space coordinates.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(N\) spans \(\ker E\) and \(\alpha\|v\|^2\le v^THv\le\beta\|v\|^2\) for every \(v\in\ker E\). Then \[\alpha\,\sigma_{\min}(N)^2\le\lambda_{\min}(N^THN)\le\lambda_{\max}(N^THN)\le\beta\,\sigma_{\max}(N)^2,\] and consequently \[\kappa_2(N^THN)\le\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\kappa_2(N)^2.\] For an orthonormal basis \(Z\), this reduces to \(\kappa_2(Z^THZ)\le\beta/\alpha\). Thus a poorly conditioned nonorthogonal basis can square its coordinate-conditioning penalty in the reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal null-space basis preserves restricted Hessian conditioning, while a general basis can worsen the reduced condition number by the square of its own condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Conditioning Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant and coordinate-dependent reduced-Hessian features under a null-space basis change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(N_1\) and \(N_2\) are full-rank bases of the same null space, then \(N_2=N_1R\) for a nonsingular matrix \(R\), and \[N_2^THN_2=R^T(N_1^THN_1)R.\] Thus inertia, nonsingularity, and definiteness are basis-invariant. Eigenvalues and spectral conditioning are generally coordinate-dependent; if both bases are orthonormal, \(R\) is orthogonal and the reduced Hessians have identical eigenvalues and spectral condition numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced Hessians in different null-space coordinates are congruent: inertia and definiteness are invariant, while spectral conditioning is invariant between orthonormal bases only.
assumptions_latex: \(N_1,N_2\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) have full column rank and the same range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_2^THN_2=R^T(N_1^THN_1)R;\text{ inertia and definiteness are invariant.}

notation.meaning: Two bases of the same null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Change Invariants

children.title: Reduced-System Conjugate-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Conjugate-gradient families applied after constraint reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Conjugate-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned conjugate gradients on a finite-dimensional positive-definite null-space system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker E\), let \(p_0\) satisfy \(Ep_0=r\), and define \[R:=Z^THZ\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n-m},\qquad h:=-Z^T(Hp_0+g).\] Choose \(q_0\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and set \(r_0=h-Rq_0\). If \(r_0=0\), output \(p=p_0+Zq_0\). Otherwise set \(d_0=r_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{d_k^TRd_k},\qquad q_{k+1}=q_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kRd_k.\] If \(\|r_{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\), output \(p=p_0+Zq_{k+1}\). Otherwise compute \[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k,\] and continue. Every output is feasible, and with exact-arithmetic termination tolerance \(\varepsilon=0\), the method terminates in at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply conjugate gradients to the positive-definite reduced Hessian, checking convergence before any potentially zero denominator, and lift the reduced iterate to a feasible primal step. Exact arithmetic requires at most the reduced dimension in iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted output \(p=p_0+Zq\) satisfies \(Ep=r\); for \(\varepsilon=0\), exact-arithmetic CG terminates in at most \(n-m\) iterations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic spectral convergence of CG on the positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), let \(q_*\) solve \(Rq=h\), and set \(\kappa(R)=\lambda_{\max}(R)/\lambda_{\min}(R)\). Exact-arithmetic CG satisfies \[\|q_k-q_*\|_R\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa(R)}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa(R)}+1}\right)^k\|q_0-q_*\|_R,\] and terminates after at most \(\dim\ker E\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-system CG has the standard SPD condition-number rate and finite termination bound for the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|q_k-q_*\|_R\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa(R)}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa(R)}+1}\right)^k\|q_0-q_*\|_R.

notation.meaning: spectral condition number of the reduced Hessian

children.title: Projected Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Krylov families confined to feasible direction spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected conjugate gradients confined to the feasible-direction space of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be positive definite on \(\ker E\), and define the orthogonal projector \[P:=I-E^T(EE^T)^{-1}E.\] Given \(p_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ep_0=r\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), set \(\rho_0:=-P(Hp_0+g)\). If \(\rho_0=0\), output \(p_0\). Otherwise set \(d_0=\rho_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{\rho_k^T\rho_k}{d_k^THd_k},\qquad p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad \rho_{k+1}=\rho_k-\alpha_kPHd_k.\] If \(\|\rho_{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon\|\rho_0\|\), output \(p_{k+1}\). Otherwise compute \[\beta_k=\frac{\rho_{k+1}^T\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k^T\rho_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=\rho_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k,\] and continue. The corrections belong to \(\mathcal K_k(PHP,\rho_0)\subseteq\ker E\), so every iterate satisfies \(Ep_k=r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected conjugate gradients projects the stationarity residual and Hessian products into the constraint null space, updates only along feasible directions, and stops when the projected residual meets the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(H\in\mathbb S^n\) is positive definite on \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every projected-CG iterate satisfies \(Ep_k=r\), and its correction lies in a Krylov subspace of \(PHP\) contained in \(\ker E\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the constraint null space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic convergence on the feasible-direction subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(PHP)|_{\ker E}\) be positive definite with eigenvalues in \([\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\), and let \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}\). If \(p_*\) is the equality-constrained minimizer, exact-arithmetic projected CG satisfies \[\|p_k-p_*\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|p_0-p_*\|_H,\] where the norm is restricted to feasible displacements, and it terminates in at most \(\dim\ker E\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected CG has the standard condition-number rate for curvature restricted to feasible directions and terminates within the null-space dimension in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|p_k-p_*\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|p_0-p_*\|_H.

notation.meaning: projected Hessian restricted to the constraint null space
spectral condition number on feasible directions

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-CG Spectral Convergence Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of the positive-definite projected-operator regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonzero projected-CG direction \(d_k\in\ker E\), the step denominator is \(d_k^{\mathsf T}Hd_k\). If this quantity is nonpositive, the positive-definite CG recurrence and its minimization and convergence guarantees do not apply. A negative value certifies negative feasible curvature; a zero value gives a flat feasible direction and causes denominator breakdown unless convergence has already occurred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpositive projected-curvature denominator ends the SPD projected-CG regime and exposes negative or flat feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_k^{\mathsf T}Hd_k<0\text{ certifies negative feasible curvature, while }d_k^{\mathsf T}Hd_k=0\text{ is a flat-direction breakdown unless already converged}.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-CG Curvature Breakdown

children.title: Augmented-System Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Iterative solution of coupled saddle-point systems.

assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k=P^{-1/2}y_k\) is the first mapped MINRES iterate satisfying \(\lVert r-Kz_k\rVert_{P^{-1}}\leq\varepsilon\lVert r\rVert_{P^{-1}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned MINRES for a symmetric equality-constrained QP KKT system.

source_refs.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the symmetric system \(Kz=r\), where \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), choose a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(P\), an initial vector \(z_0\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Set \(y_0=P^{1/2}z_0\), \(\widetilde K=P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\), and \(\widetilde r=P^{-1/2}r\). Apply MINRES to \(\widetilde K y=\widetilde r\) from \(y_0\). For each MINRES iterate \(y_k\), define \(z_k=P^{-1/2}y_k\), and stop at the first \(k\) such that \(\lVert r-Kz_k\rVert_{P^{-1}}\leq\varepsilon\lVert r\rVert_{P^{-1}}\). Return \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply MINRES in symmetrically preconditioned coordinates, map each iterate back to the primal-dual variables, and stop when the preconditioned residual meets the relative tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Krylov Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional termination of augmented-system MINRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular symmetric \(N\)-by-\(N\) transformed system \(\widetilde K y=\widetilde r\), exact-arithmetic MINRES reaches the exact solution in at most the degree of the minimal polynomial of \(\widetilde K\) relative to the initial residual, and hence in at most \(N\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-arithmetic MINRES solves the nonsingular transformed KKT system in at most its dimension, often earlier when the relevant minimal polynomial has smaller degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_{\mathrm{term}}\le\deg\mu_{\widetilde K,\widetilde r_0}\le N.

notation.meaning: minimal polynomial of the operator relative to the initial residual

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Arithmetic MINRES Termination Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions required by the accepted augmented-system MINRES guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The MINRES construction relies on symmetry of \(\widetilde K=P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\). If \(P\) is not symmetric positive definite, or preconditioning makes the effective operator nonsymmetric, the symmetric Lanczos and MINRES residual-minimization guarantees no longer follow. If \(K\) is singular, compatibility and singular-system termination conditions are additionally required, so the accepted seed's nonsingularity-based conclusion does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES requires a symmetric effective operator and SPD symmetric preconditioning; nonsymmetric preconditioning or an untreated singular KKT system crosses the seed's guarantee boundary.
assumptions_latex: The method uses symmetric Lanczos recurrences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\text{ preserves the symmetric MINRES setting; loss of effective symmetry invalidates its stated guarantees}.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Preserving Preconditioning Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov characterization of symmetrically preconditioned augmented-system MINRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde K=P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\) be symmetric and \(\widetilde r_0=\widetilde r-\widetilde K y_0\). In exact arithmetic, \[y_k\in y_0+\mathcal K_k(\widetilde K,\widetilde r_0),\qquad \|\widetilde r-\widetilde K y_k\|_2=\min_{y\in y_0+\mathcal K_k(\widetilde K,\widetilde r_0)}\|\widetilde r-\widetilde K y\|_2.\] Equivalently, the mapped iterate minimizes the \(P^{-1}\)-norm KKT residual over the mapped affine Krylov space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each MINRES iterate minimizes the preconditioned KKT residual over its current augmented-system Krylov space.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact for the stated minimization identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_k\text{ minimizes }\|\widetilde r-\widetilde K y\|_2\text{ over }y_0+\mathcal K_k(\widetilde K,\widetilde r_0).

notation.meaning: Krylov subspace of the symmetrically preconditioned KKT operator

knowledge_statements.title: MINRES Residual-Minimization Property

children.title: Low-Rank Factorization Updates
children.top_down_role: Factorization changes induced by constraint exchanges or nearby systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and numerical breakdown of a one-constraint bordered KKT update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_+=\begin{bmatrix}K&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\) with nonsingular \(K\), exact breakdown occurs when \(\sigma=-a^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}a=0\). In floating-point arithmetic, if the computed \(\widehat\sigma=-a^{\mathsf T}\widehat w\) is not separated from a declared bound for the solve and inner-product errors, division by \(\widehat\sigma\) does not certify a stable update; the bordered system must be treated as rank-uncertain and sent to a pivoted or regularized refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero Schur complement makes the bordered matrix singular; a numerically unresolved complement makes the update uncertifiable.
assumptions_latex: The stored factors produce \(\widehat w\approx K^{-1}a\).
A numerical uncertainty bound for \(\widehat\sigma\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma=0\Rightarrow K_+\text{ is singular};\quad |\widehat\sigma|\text{ unresolved}\Rightarrow\text{the update must not be accepted}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered-Update Breakdown Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic update when one constraint and multiplier border a nonsingular KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb S^N\) be nonsingular and \(K_+=\begin{bmatrix}K&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\). Define \(w=K^{-1}a\) and \(\sigma=-a^{\mathsf T}w\). Then \(K_+\) is nonsingular if and only if \(\sigma\ne0\), and \[K_+^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}K^{-1}+\sigma^{-1}ww^{\mathsf T}&-\sigma^{-1}w\\-\sigma^{-1}w^{\mathsf T}&\sigma^{-1}\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus inverse actions for the bordered system use solves with the stored factors of \(K\) and one scalar Schur-complement solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-constraint KKT addition is a bordered update whose nonsingularity is decided by a scalar Schur complement; updated inverse actions use stored-system solves and a rank-one correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_+\text{ is nonsingular}\iff\sigma=-a^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}a\ne0, with the displayed inverse formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered KKT Update Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic bound for Woodbury inverse actions, not sparse factor modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(K\), nonsingular \(C\), and \(K_+=K+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), assume \(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\) is nonsingular and one stored-factor solve costs \(T_K\). Forming Woodbury data requires \(rT_K+O(Nr^2+r^3)\) work and \(O(Nr+r^2)\) storage. Each later inverse action requires one base solve and \(O(Nr+r^2)\) additional work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r inverse update uses r base solves and a small dense system; it provides no sparse-fill or pivoting bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{setup}}=rT_K+O(Nr^2+r^3),\quad M_{\mathrm{extra}}=O(Nr+r^2).

notation.meaning: Cost of one solve using stored factors of K.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Low-Rank Inverse-Action Work Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact removal of the last constraint from an inverse representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K_+^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}E&f\\f^{\mathsf T}&g\end{bmatrix}\) is the inverse of \(K_+=\begin{bmatrix}K&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(g\ne0\), then \[K^{-1}=E-ff^{\mathsf T}/g.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting the bordered constraint recovers the old inverse by a rank-one downdate when the trailing inverse scalar is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K^{-1}=E-ff^{\mathsf T}/g.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered KKT Downdate Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small-matrix inertia and nonsingularity test for a symmetric low-rank update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) and \(C\) be nonsingular symmetric matrices, \(K_+=K+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), and \(S=C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\). Then \[\operatorname{inertia}(K_+)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)+\operatorname{inertia}(S)-\operatorname{inertia}(C^{-1}).\] Moreover, \(K_+\) is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inertia and nonsingularity of a symmetric low-rank update are determined by the original matrix and a small Schur matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}(K_+)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)+\operatorname{inertia}(S)-\operatorname{inertia}(C^{-1})\).

notation.meaning: Small Schur matrix associated with the update.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Inertia Update Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise verification of factors produced after a low-rank symmetric modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_+=K+UCU^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\widehat K=P^{\mathsf T}\widehat L\widehat D\widehat L^{\mathsf T}P\). With \(E=\widehat K-K_+\), \[\eta_F=\frac{\lVert E\rVert_F}{\lVert K_+\rVert_F}\] is a factorization backward error: the computed factors exactly factor \(K_++E\). Thus \(\eta_F\le\tau\) certifies normwise backward accuracy, but not small forward error, acceptable element growth, or stable pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small factorization residual certifies normwise backward accuracy, but not forward stability or pivot quality.
assumptions_latex: The residual is evaluated with adequate accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_F\le\tau\Rightarrow\widehat K=K_++E\) with \(\lVert E\rVert_F\le\tau\lVert K_+\rVert_F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Modified-Factor Backward-Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure example for an unguarded low-rank modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=I_2\), \(U=e_1\), and \(C=[-1]\), \[K_+=K+UCU^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(0,1).\] Hence a rank-one modification of a well-conditioned matrix can produce a singular updated system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low algebraic rank does not make a factor update safe: a rank-one change can create singularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(K_+-K)=1\) while \(K_+\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Update Can Destroy Nonsingularity
Low-Rank Factorization Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updating a symmetric-indefinite KKT factorization after a small matrix modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=P^{\mathsf T}LDL^{\mathsf T}P\) be an existing symmetric-indefinite factorization, and suppose the next system has \(K_+=K+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{N\times r}\) and \(r\ll N\). Apply the \(r\) symmetric rank-one or rank-two modifications encoded by \(UCU^{\mathsf T}\) to \(L\) and \(D\), retaining \(P\) while acceptable pivots exist. Verify \(\lVert K_+-P^{\mathsf T}L_+D_+L_+^{\mathsf T}P\rVert\leq\tau\lVert K_+\rVert\); otherwise compute a new pivoted factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update an existing symmetric KKT factorization for a low-rank matrix change, but refactor when pivot stability or the factorization residual fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a verified factorization of \(K_+\) or a newly computed pivoted factorization.

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of sparsity orderings and elimination structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost separation for repeated factorizations sharing a validated symbolic envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\) matrices accepted by one symbolic analysis of cost \(S\), with numerical factorization costs \(F_1,\ldots,F_q\), reuse costs \[S+\sum_{j=1}^qF_j\] instead of \(qS+\sum_{j=1}^qF_j\). The saving is \((q-1)S\); numerical factorization, pivoting, and solves remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated symbolic reuse amortizes analysis but does not reuse changed numerical factors.
assumptions_latex: Every matrix is accepted by the same symbolic envelope and pivot-allocation policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{reuse}}=S+\sum_jF_j,\qquad T_{\mathrm{reanalyze}}-T_{\mathrm{reuse}}=(q-1)S.

notation.meaning: Numerical factorization cost for system j.

knowledge_statements.title: Amortized Symbolic-Analysis Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a fixed symbolic elimination structure under a pattern-only elimination rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be an analyzed symmetric sparsity envelope and let \(P\) and \(\mathcal L(\mathcal G,P)\) denote its fixed ordering and symbolic factor pattern. For every symmetric \(K_j\) with \(\operatorname{pat}(K_j)\subseteq\mathcal G\), a numerical factorization using the same pattern-only elimination rule and no pivot outside the declared envelope generates no structural factor entry outside \(\mathcal L(\mathcal G,P)\). Numerical values and factors must still be recomputed. A pivot interchange, pivot block, or generated entry outside the envelope invalidates reuse and requires enlargement or symbolic reanalysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symbolic analysis is reusable for matrices inside its pattern envelope only while the numerical factorization obeys the same declared ordering and pivot envelope.
assumptions_latex: The elimination and admissible-pivot rules encoded by the symbolic envelope are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted reuse avoids new global symbolic analysis but still requires numerical factorization of each changed matrix.

notation.meaning: Allocated symbolic factor pattern under ordering \(P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Envelope Symbolic Reuse Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Post-factorization verification that numerical factorization respected the allocated symbolic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) encode allocated factor entries, permitted permutations, and permitted \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. Reuse is accepted only if every realized structural entry of \(L\), pivot interchange, pivot block, and storage request is represented by \(\mathcal S\). Failure of containment or storage capacity invalidates the state and triggers enlargement or symbolic reanalysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic reuse is accepted only when the realized factors, pivots, and storage fit the allocated envelope.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) explicitly represents factor storage and admissible pivot metadata.
The realized numerical factor state is observable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{state}(L,D,P)\subseteq\mathcal S\) is necessary for accepting reuse of \(\mathcal S\).

notation.meaning: Allocated symbolic factor and pivot envelope.

knowledge_statements.title: Realized-Factor Envelope Acceptance Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identical Input Patterns Can Require Different Threshold Pivots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-dependent pivot boundary for pattern-only symbolic reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\alpha<1\) and a leading-pivot rule accepting \(a_{11}\) as a \(1\times1\) pivot only when \(|a_{11}|\ge\alpha\max_{j>1}|a_{j1}|\). The matrices \[K_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}\varepsilon&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_M=\begin{bmatrix}M&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}\] have identical structural patterns. If \(0<\varepsilon<\alpha\) and \(M\ge\alpha\), the first rejects the leading scalar pivot while the second accepts it. Thus input pattern alone does not determine an indefinite numerical pivot structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Same-pattern symmetric-indefinite matrices can cause a threshold rule to choose different pivot structures.
assumptions_latex: The stated leading-pivot threshold rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{pat}(K_\varepsilon)=\operatorname{pat}(K_M)\), but their leading pivot decisions differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Identical Input Patterns Can Require Different Threshold Pivots
Symbolic Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusing ordering and elimination metadata across KKT matrices with unchanged sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric matrices \(K_j\) satisfying \(\operatorname{pat}(K_j)=\operatorname{pat}(K_0)\), compute once a fill-reducing permutation and symbolic elimination structure for \(PK_0P^{\mathsf T}\). For each \(j\), reuse this symbolic structure and recompute only the numerical factors, allowing numerical pivoting within preallocated admissible pivot regions. If a required pivot or nonzero lies outside that structure, discard the symbolic state and repeat symbolic analysis for \(K_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse ordering and elimination metadata while the structural sparsity pattern remains valid; redo symbolic analysis when new nonzeros or pivots violate it.
assumptions_latex: The declared structural pattern includes all potentially nonzero entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted reuse performs numerical factorization without repeating global symbolic analysis.

notation.meaning: structural nonzero pattern of a matrix

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Accuracy recovery for computed QP linear-system solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement for a computed QP linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular system \(Kz=r\), an initial computed solution \(z_0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), repeat: form the residual \(s_k=r-Kz_k\) in higher precision, approximately solve \(K d_k=s_k\) using the stored factors, and set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+d_k\). Stop when \(\lVert s_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon(\lVert K\rVert\lVert z_k\rVert+\lVert r\rVert)\), or declare stagnation if the residual no longer decreases. Return the last accepted iterate and its computed residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute residuals accurately, solve correction equations with stored factors, and update until backward error is small or refinement stagnates.
assumptions_latex: Residual evaluation is more accurate than the correction solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output has normwise backward error at most \(\varepsilon\).

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

assumptions_latex: A factorization of \(K\) is already stored.
One refinement step evaluates a residual and applies the stored factors once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each refinement step needs one residual multiplication and one factor solve, without refactorization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental dense cost of refinement relative to an existing direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With stored factors of an \(N\times N\) matrix \(K\), one refinement step evaluates \(r-Kz_k\) and solves one correction equation with the factors. In the dense case this is \(O(N^2)\) arithmetic per step with \(O(N^2)\) factor storage, compared with \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic for a new factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement reuses the factorization, so each dense correction costs quadratic rather than cubic work.
knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Reuse Cost

assumptions_latex: The computed correction is modeled by \(d_k=B(r-Kz_k)\).
Residual-evaluation error remains below the requested terminal accuracy during the contracting phase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error contracts at least linearly by \(\theta\) until the residual-error floor, requiring \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/|\log\theta|)\) corrections for reduction by a factor \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence condition for classical or mixed-precision iterative refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_*\) solve \(Kz=r\), and let \(d_k=B(r-Kz_k)\). In exact residual arithmetic, \(\theta:=\|I-BK\|<1\) implies \(\|z_*-z_{k+1}\|\leq\theta\|z_*-z_k\|\). With finite-precision residuals, contraction persists until residual-evaluation errors dominate. A reduction by a factor \(\varepsilon\) therefore requires \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/|\log\theta|)\) correction solves. If \(\theta\geq1\), or residuals are not sufficiently accurate, monotone improvement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement converges linearly while the reused correction solve is a contracting approximate inverse and residual errors remain small; otherwise it may stagnate or diverge.
knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Contraction Regime

children.title: KKT Regularization
children.top_down_role: Primal, dual, and block perturbation regimes for difficult KKT systems.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(\sigma>0\), and a right-hand side \(b\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized KKT matrix is nonsingular with inertia \((n,m,0)\), so its primal-dual solution is uniquely defined even when \(A\) is row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric quasi-definite primal-dual diagonal regularization and solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\delta\) so that \(B=H+\delta I\succ0\), choose \(\sigma>0\), form \(K_{\delta,\sigma}=\begin{bmatrix}B&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\), and solve \(K_{\delta,\sigma}z=b\) by a symmetric factorization. The multiplier-block Schur complement is \(-\sigma I-AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\prec0\); hence \(K_{\delta,\sigma}\) is symmetric quasi-definite, nonsingular, and has inertia \((n,m,0)\), without requiring full row rank of \(A\). Acceptance for the original KKT equations additionally requires testing their unregularized residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Make the primal block positive definite and the multiplier block strictly negative, solve the resulting quasi-definite system, and separately test the original KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Definite Regularized Solve

assumptions_latex: \((K+D)\widehat z=b\) is solved exactly for a block-diagonal regularization \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original residual is \(b-K\widehat z=D\widehat z\), so regularized-system accuracy alone does not certify accuracy for the original equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact a posteriori measurement of regularization bias for the original KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((K+D)\widehat z=b\), then \(b-K\widehat z=D\widehat z\). For \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\delta I,-\sigma I)\) and \(\widehat z=(\widehat p,\widehat y)\), the residual left in the original equations is \((\delta\widehat p,-\sigma\widehat y)\). Thus a small residual for the shifted system can coexist with a large regularization bias, and acceptance for the unregularized system requires testing \(b-K\widehat z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The shift times the computed solution is exactly the residual left in the original KKT equations, so that residual must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-System Bias Certificate
KKT Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual diagonal regularization of an equality-constrained QP KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), choose initial \(\delta>0\) and \(\sigma\geq0\), and factor \(K_{\delta,\sigma}=\begin{bmatrix}H+\delta I&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\). Increase \(\delta\) or \(\sigma\) geometrically until the factorization is numerically stable and has the prescribed inertia. Solve the regularized system, evaluate the residual for the original KKT equations, and reduce the regularization or apply refinement until the original residual tolerance is met; otherwise report regularization failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add controlled primal and dual diagonal shifts until factorization is stable, then reduce their bias until the original KKT residual is acceptable.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
A target inertia and original-system residual tolerance are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an accepted primal-dual vector or reports that the regularization target was unattainable.

children.title: Inertia Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Factorization signatures used to assess curvature and system suitability.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), and the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\) if and only if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\).

notation.meaning: triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts
block-diagonal factor in a symmetric-indefinite factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic inertia certificate for positive curvature on the constraint null space.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), and define \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\). Then \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(R)+(m,m,0)\). Consequently, if a symmetric pivoted factorization \(PKP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) is computed, summing the inertias of the \(1\)-by-\(1\) and \(2\)-by-\(2\) diagonal blocks of \(D\) yields \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)\). The value \((n,m,0)\) certifies \(R\succ0\); an excess negative count or a nonzero zero count certifies negative or degenerate feasible curvature, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT inertia equals the reduced-Hessian inertia plus one positive and one negative eigenvalue per independent constraint; it can be extracted from the diagonal pivot blocks of a symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Monitoring

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

assumptions_latex: The computed symmetric factorization is exact for \(K+\Delta K\), with \(\|\Delta K\|_2\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every eigenvalue of \(K+\Delta K\) has magnitude greater than \(\eta\), its inertia equals that of \(K\); otherwise the computed signs need not certify the exact inertia.

notation.meaning: Backward perturbation represented by the factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision reliability boundary for inertia inferred from a backward-stable symmetric factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a computed symmetric factorization is exact for \(K+\Delta K\), where \(\|\Delta K\|_2\leq\eta\). If \(\min_i|\lambda_i(K+\Delta K)|>\eta\), then \(K+\Delta K\) and \(K\) have the same inertia. If an eigenvalue or factor pivot block lies within the perturbation threshold of zero, its sign is numerically uncertain and the computed inertia must not be treated as an exact curvature certificate for \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed inertia certifies the original matrix only when the represented matrix's spectrum is separated from zero by more than the backward-error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Perturbation Margin

children.title: Regularization-Curvature Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where stabilization obscures or conflicts with the intended curvature regime.

assumptions_latex: The primal block is shifted from \(H\) to \(H+\delta I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness of the shifted reduced Hessian does not certify positive definiteness of the original reduced Hessian when the shift can mask a nonpositive eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between numerical stabilization and faithful diagnosis of original feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\), the shifted reduced Hessian is \(R_\delta=Z^{\mathsf T}(H+\delta I)Z=R+\delta I\), so \(\lambda_i(R_\delta)=\lambda_i(R)+\delta\). Therefore \(R_\delta\succ0\) does not imply \(R\succ0\): if \(\lambda_{\min}(R)\leq0\) and \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(R)\), the shifted model is positive definite while the original has flat or negative feasible curvature. Inertia of the shifted KKT matrix consequently certifies only the shifted model unless the shift is accounted for in the spectral interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large primal shift can make a singular or indefinite reduced Hessian appear positive definite, so shifted inertia alone cannot certify original curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Masking Boundary

assumptions_latex: Only the multiplier block is shifted in \(K_\sigma=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced primal curvature remains \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) for every \(\sigma\); a dual shift neither repairs nor masks its eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a pure dual-block KKT shift on feasible primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every equality-feasible direction \(d=Zq\), the primal quadratic curvature under \(K_\sigma=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\) is \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=q^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}HZq\), independently of \(\sigma\). Hence a pure dual shift may regularize multiplier coupling or rank deficiency but cannot turn zero or negative feasible primal curvature into positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-block shift changes multiplier coupling but leaves the reduced Hessian, and therefore feasible primal curvature, unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Shifts Preserve Reduced Curvature
Regularization-Curvature Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring a primal KKT shift preserves positive feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\), and regularize the primal Hessian by \(H_\delta=H+\delta I\). The regularization is curvature-compatible with a positive-definite reduced model precisely when \(Z^{\mathsf T}H_\delta Z=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ+\delta I\succ0\), equivalently \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\). If nonnegative regularization is required, any \(\delta>\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\}\) satisfies the strict condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal diagonal shift is compatible when it moves every reduced-Hessian eigenvalue strictly above zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) and \(A\) has a well-defined null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compatible shifts are exactly those satisfying \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is standard and the selected content kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no citation. An authoritative locator is required, preferably also addressing the nontrivial-null-space case in which the smallest reduced eigenvalue is defined.

children.title: Shared Linear-Algebra Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Rank, curvature, and conditioning regimes that affect both algorithmic paradigms.

children.title: Dependent Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Rank-deficient equality and working-constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity caused by linearly dependent equality or working-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), then there exists \(0\neq y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Hence \(K\begin{bmatrix}0\\y\end{bmatrix}=0\), so \(K\) is singular independently of the Hessian \(H\). Primal solutions may remain identifiable, but multipliers are nonunique: whenever \((x,\lambda)\) solves the KKT equations, so does \((x,\lambda+y)\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraint rows make the KKT matrix singular and render multipliers nonunique, even when the primal solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is singular and every existing multiplier is nonunique modulo \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: nonzero dependence vector among constraint rows

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility test separating redundant consistent rows from inconsistent row dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(Ax=b\) is feasible if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently \(y^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Thus any \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\) with \(y^{\mathsf T}b\ne0\) certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent rows are consistent only when their right-hand sides satisfy the same dependencies; a violated dependency certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is feasible exactly when \(b\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Certificate for Dependent Equalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature condition under which dependent equality rows do not destroy primal uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b\}\), where \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\) and the feasible set is nonempty. If \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A\), then the problem has a unique primal minimizer. Row dependence affects multiplier uniqueness but not the feasible-direction curvature criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equalities do not prevent a unique primal minimizer when the Hessian is positive definite on every feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-constrained quadratic program has exactly one primal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Uniqueness Despite Constraint Dependence

children.title: Singular Reduced Models
children.top_down_role: Flat feasible directions and nonunique equality-constrained solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudoinverse Representation of Singular Reduced Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete solution set and value for the bounded singular positive-semidefinite reduced model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(u)=\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}Ru+g_r^{\mathsf T}u+c\), where \(R\succeq0\) is singular and \(g_r\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}q=-R^{\dagger}g_r+\ker R,\qquad \min q=c-\tfrac12g_r^{\mathsf T}R^{\dagger}g_r.\] The minimum-norm minimizer is \(-R^{\dagger}g_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a singular reduced model is bounded, its minimizers are a pseudoinverse solution plus all null-curvature directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}q=-R^{\dagger}g_r+\ker R\) and \(\min q=c-\tfrac12g_r^{\mathsf T}R^{\dagger}g_r\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the reduced Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudoinverse Representation of Singular Reduced Minimizers
Singular Reduced Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy and nonuniqueness from a singular positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasible parametrization \(x=x_p+Zu\), where \(AZ=0\), and the reduced quadratic \(q(u)=\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}Ru+g_r^{\mathsf T}u+c\) with \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\). If \(R\) is singular and \(g_r\perp\ker R\), every reduced minimizer is nonunique along \(\ker R\). If instead some \(v\in\ker R\) satisfies \(g_r^{\mathsf T}v\neq0\), then \(q\) is unbounded below in one of the directions \(v\) or \(-v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian yields either flat families of minimizers or unbounded descent, depending on the reduced linear term.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and spans \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orthogonality of \(g_r\) to \(\ker R\) separates nonunique minimizers from unboundedness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional positive-semidefinite reduced-quadratic dichotomy is mathematically coherent and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but no evidence source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Loss of numerical reliability in coupled or eliminated systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw KKT Conditioning Is Scaling Dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an unscaled KKT condition number to be coordinate invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(D_t=\operatorname{diag}(t,1)\) for \(t\ge1\). The congruent system with \(K_t=D_tKD_t=\begin{bmatrix}t^2&t\\t&0\end{bmatrix}\) is equivalent under the corresponding nonsingular variable and equation scaling, but \(\kappa_2(K_t)\to\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent diagonal scaling can make a nonsingular KKT system arbitrarily ill conditioned in raw coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Variables and right-hand sides are transformed consistently with the congruence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(D_tKD_t)\to\infty\) although the scaled systems are algebraically equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Raw KKT Conditioning Is Scaling Dependent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning degradation caused by a normal-equation elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every full-column-rank matrix \(B\), \(\kappa_2(B^{\mathsf T}B)=\kappa_2(B)^2\), where the condition number of \(B\) is the ratio of its extreme singular values. Thus a normal-equation reduction can square the spectral conditioning of the underlying KKT-related operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal equations square the spectral condition number and can amplify numerical unreliability.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(B^{\mathsf T}B)=\kappa_2(B)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Condition Squaring in Normal Equations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct finite-perturbation bound for a nonsingular coupled KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=r\), with \(K\) nonsingular and \(r\ne0\), and suppose \((K+\Delta K)(z+\Delta z)=r+\Delta r\). For a consistent subordinate norm, set \(\varepsilon_K=\lVert\Delta K\rVert/\lVert K\rVert\) and \(\varepsilon_r=\lVert\Delta r\rVert/\lVert r\rVert\). If \(\kappa(K)\varepsilon_K<1\), then \[\frac{\lVert\Delta z\rVert}{\lVert z\rVert}\le \frac{\kappa(K)}{1-\kappa(K)\varepsilon_K}(\varepsilon_K+\varepsilon_r).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative primal-dual error is amplified by the KKT condition number, with a finite-perturbation denominator that deteriorates near singularity.
assumptions_latex: A consistent subordinate norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\Delta z\rVert/\lVert z\rVert\le\kappa(K)(\varepsilon_K+\varepsilon_r)/(1-\kappa(K)\varepsilon_K)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Normwise Perturbation Bound
Ill-Conditioned KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error amplification near singularity of a coupled KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=r\) be nonsingular and let computed data satisfy \((K+\Delta K)(z+\Delta z)=r+\Delta r\). For a consistent subordinate norm, if \(\kappa(K)\lVert\Delta K\rVert/\lVert K\rVert<1\), then \(\lVert\Delta z\rVert/\lVert z\rVert\) is bounded to first order by \(\kappa(K)\bigl(\lVert\Delta K\rVert/\lVert K\rVert+\lVert\Delta r\rVert/\lVert r\rVert\bigr)\). Thus large \(\kappa(K)\) permits small factorization or data errors to produce large primal-dual errors despite a small residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-singular KKT matrices amplify small data and factorization errors, so a small residual alone may not imply an accurate primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relative solution sensitivity scales with \(\kappa(K)\), marking numerical unreliability when it is large.
