children.title: Unexpected Curvature Signatures
children.top_down_role: Observed curvature behavior inconsistent with the expected convex-QP structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient Hessian Inertia Does Not Determine Feasible Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to diagnosing equality-constrained curvature from the ambient Hessian alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)\) and \(A=[1\ 0]\). Although \(H\) has one negative eigenvalue, \(\ker A=\operatorname{span}\{(0,1)\}\) and the reduced Hessian is \([1]\). The KKT matrix has inertia \((2,1,0)\), the expected signature for \(n=2\), \(m=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ambient negative eigenvalue can lie normal to the feasible subspace and need not signal feasible negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\min}(H)<0\not\Rightarrow\exists d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}:d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient Hessian Inertia Does Not Determine Feasible Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Boundary for the Expected KKT Signature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the full-row-rank signature interpretation with redundant equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), any nonzero \(v\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\) gives \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0\\v\end{bmatrix}=0.\] Thus redundant equality rows create at least \(m-\operatorname{rank}(A)\) zero KKT eigenvalues independently of reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equality rows create multiplier null vectors and zero KKT eigenvalues unrelated to flat feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{nullity}(K)\ge m-\operatorname{rank}(A).
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Boundary for the Expected KKT Signature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature-signature classification for a full-row-rank equality-constrained KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), and let \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\). If \(\operatorname{inertia}(R)=(p,q,s)\), then for \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] one has \[\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(p+m,q+m,s).\] Hence excess negative KKT eigenvalues beyond the mandatory \(m\) correspond to feasible negative curvature, while zero KKT eigenvalues correspond to flat feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent equalities, KKT inertia equals reduced-Hessian inertia plus one positive and one negative eigenvalue per equality.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(p+m,q+m,s)\).

notation.meaning: Positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts of the reduced Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT–Reduced-Hessian Inertia Identity
Unexpected Curvature Signatures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT inertia signatures induced by negative or zero reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), and put \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\). If \(R\) has inertia \((p,q,s)\), then the equality-constrained KKT matrix \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) has inertia \((p+m,q+m,s)\). Therefore \(q>0\) exposes negative curvature along feasible directions, while \(s>0\) exposes flat feasible directions and singularity; either signature contradicts the strictly convex reduced regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extra negative or zero KKT eigenvalues correspond exactly to negative or flat curvature in feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected strictly convex signature \((n,m,0)\) fails exactly when \(q+s>0\).

notation.meaning: positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts of the reduced Hessian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inertia formula and its curvature interpretation are mathematically consistent and the failure-boundary content kind is appropriate, but the record contains no source for the exact KKT-reduced-Hessian inertia identity.

children.title: Inertia-Mismatch Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Factorization signatures indicating incompatible or unstable KKT structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia-Mismatch Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparing factorization inertia with the signature required by reduced convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-row-rank constraint matrix \(A\), compute a symmetric pivoted factorization \(PKP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\). Count positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of the \(1\)-by-\(1\) and \(2\)-by-\(2\) diagonal blocks of \(D\), obtaining \(\widehat{\mathcal I}(K)\). In exact arithmetic, \(\widehat{\mathcal I}(K)\neq(n,m,0)\) certifies that the reduced Hessian is not positive definite. In floating-point arithmetic, blocks whose eigenvalues lie below a declared threshold must instead be reported as numerically indeterminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract inertia from the pivot blocks and compare it with the signature required for positive feasible curvature, flagging threshold-level pivots as uncertain.
assumptions_latex: \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) is the KKT matrix for \(n\) primal variables and \(m\) independent constraints.
The factorization uses symmetric permutations and inertia-preserving pivots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reliable signature different from \((n,m,0)\) certifies an inertia-curvature mismatch.

notation.meaning: target KKT signature for positive reduced curvature

assumptions_latex: The quadratic program is \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q=Q^T\).
For a candidate working set \(W\), the rows of \(K_W=[A^T\;G_W^T]^T\) are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A convex-QP working-face step is justified only when \(Z_W^TQZ_W\succeq0\), where the columns of \(Z_W\) span \(\ker K_W\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_W\) have full column rank and satisfy \(K_WZ_W=0\). The objective restricted to the affine working face has Hessian \(Z_W^TQZ_W\). If \(Z_W^TQZ_W\succeq0\), the restricted model is convex; if \(Z_W^TQZ_W\succ0\), its stationary point is the unique minimizer on that face. If \(Z_W^TQZ_W\) has a negative eigenvalue, a stationary KKT solve is not a convex-face minimization certificate: some tangent direction \(d=Z_Wp\) satisfies \(d^TQd<0\). Thus algorithms relying on convexity, descent from the face minimizer, or convex KKT inertia cross their validity boundary at the first negative reduced-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-face QP is convex exactly when its reduced Hessian is positive semidefinite; negative reduced curvature invalidates convex minimization and associated KKT-inertia interpretations.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity-Regime Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness for the equality-defined affine working subproblem when reduced curvature is positive semidefinite but singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the objective on the equality-defined affine working manifold as \(\phi(p)=\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Rp+g_R^{\mathsf T}p+\gamma\), where \(p\in\mathbb R^q\) is unrestricted and \(R=Z_W^{\mathsf T}QZ_W\succeq0\). If \(g_R\notin\operatorname{range}(R)\), then \(\phi\) is unbounded below along a direction in \(\ker R\). If \(g_R\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), minimizers exist and form \(p_*+\ker R\); they are nonunique whenever \(\ker R\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a singular positive-semidefinite affine working subproblem, a reduced-gradient range condition separates unboundedness from an affine family of minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The working subproblem uses unrestricted null-space coordinates; inactive inequalities are not imposed in this classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}\phi\ne\varnothing\iff g_R\in\operatorname{range}(R);\quad\text{uniqueness additionally requires }R\succ0.

notation.meaning: reduced Hessian on the equality-defined working manifold

assumptions_latex: The feasible polyhedron is \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active constraints determine the minimal face of \(P\) containing \(x\) through their equality hyperplanes.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in P\), define the active index set by \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:(Gx)_i=h_i\}\). The face exposed by these tight inequalities is \(F(x)=\{y\in P:G_i y=h_i\ \text{for every }i\in\mathcal A(x)\}\). Its tangent space is \(T_{F(x)}=\{d:Ad=0,\ G_i d=0\ \text{for every }i\in\mathcal A(x)\}\), while feasible first-order directions additionally satisfy \(G_i d\le0\) for active inequalities that are not imposed as equalities by a chosen working face. Redundant active rows may describe the same face and need not be linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, tight inequalities define its active set, exposed face, tangent space, and cone of locally feasible directions.

children.title: Working Constraint Estimates
children.top_down_role: Algorithmic constraint subsets used to represent a candidate face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling Dependence of Absolute Slack Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of a working-set estimate formed from unnormalized absolute slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(G_ix\le h_i\), replace its representation by \(\rho_iG_ix\le\rho_ih_i\), where \(\rho_i>0\). The feasible set and exact activity are unchanged, but the slack becomes \(\rho_i s_i(x)\). Hence membership in \(W_\tau(x)=\{i:s_i(x)\le\tau\}\) can change when \(\tau>0\). Invariance requires prescribed row normalization or row-specific thresholds transformed as \(\tau_i\mapsto\rho_i\tau_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive threshold applied to raw slacks depends on constraint scaling; normalization or correspondingly scaled thresholds are required for invariance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_\tau(x)\ \text{need not be invariant under }(G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\rho_iG_i,\rho_ih_i).

notation.meaning: positive scaling of inequality row i

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Dependence of Absolute Slack Estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing removal of dependent estimated rows after consistency has been verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(C_Wy=d_W\) is consistent. Select indices \(J\) whose rows form a basis for the row space of \([C_W\ d_W]\). Then \[\{y:C_Wy=d_W\}=\{y:(C_W)_Jy=(d_W)_J\},\] and \((C_W)_J\) has full row rank. Thus a rank-revealing factorization of the augmented system may discard nonbasis rows without changing the estimated affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent estimate, retaining an augmented-row basis removes dependence without changing the represented affine set.
assumptions_latex: J\text{ indexes a row basis of }[C_W\ d_W]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sol}(C_W,d_W)=\operatorname{sol}((C_W)_J,(d_W)_J).

notation.meaning: indices of retained independent augmented rows

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Set-Preserving Rank Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for imposing estimated constraints as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_Wy=d_W\) stack the original equalities and estimated working inequalities. Its affine solution set is nonempty exactly when \[d_W\in\operatorname{range}(C_W),\] equivalently \(u^Td_W=0\) for every \(u\in\ker(C_W^T)\), or \(C_WC_W^\dagger d_W=d_W\). Row dependence is harmless when these compatibility conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimated working equalities are consistent exactly when their right-hand sides satisfy every dependence among their normals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:C_Wy=d_W\}\ne\varnothing\iff d_W\in\operatorname{range}(C_W).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the working-row matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Estimated-Face Consistency Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested, scale-invariant near-activity estimate for nonzero inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible \(x\) and rows \(G_i\ne0\), define \(\widehat s_i(x)=(h_i-G_ix)/\|G_i\|_2\) and \(\widehat W_\tau(x)=\{i:0\le\widehat s_i(x)\le\tau\}\). Then \(\widehat W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x)\), and \(\widehat W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq\widehat W_{\tau_2}(x)\) for \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\). Positive row rescaling \((G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\rho_iG_i,\rho_ih_i)\) leaves both \(\widehat s_i\) and the estimate unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized slacks give nested working-constraint estimates that equal exact activity at zero tolerance and are invariant under positive row scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x),\quad \tau_1\le\tau_2\Rightarrow\widehat W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq\widehat W_{\tau_2}(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Slack-Threshold Estimate

assumptions_latex: The current iterate satisfies \(x\in P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimate \(W_\tau(x)\) contains constraints whose current slack is at most \(\tau\), and equals the active set when \(\tau=0\).

notation.meaning: Slack vector for the inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A canonical slack-threshold estimate, not a claim that every implementation uses this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the slack vector \(s(x)=h-Gx\ge0\). A canonical geometric estimate of the constraints defining the current or nearby face is \(W_\tau(x)=\{i:0\le s_i(x)\le\tau\}\). Hence \(W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x)\), and \(W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq W_{\tau_2}(x)\) whenever \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\). The estimated working face is \(F_{W_\tau}(x)=\{y:Ay=b,\ G_i y=h_i\ \text{for every }i\in W_\tau(x)\}\). The estimate is admissible for an equality-constrained face solve only if this affine set is consistent; rank-revealing selection may remove dependent estimated rows without changing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraints with slack below a chosen tolerance form a nested estimate of the nearby active face; consistency and row dependence must be checked before a face solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Working Constraint Estimates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack-threshold construction is plausible and clearly labeled canonical, but working-set estimation and dependent-row handling require an inspectable active-set source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and Descent after Releasing a Negative-Multiplier Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-QP working-set release result; strict feasibility and descent require the stated second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\succeq0. Suppose G\hat x+c=\sum_{i\in\hat{\mathcal W}}a_i\hat\lambda_i and a_i^T\hat x=b_i for all i\in\hat{\mathcal W}, where \{a_i:i\in\hat{\mathcal W}\} is linearly independent. Let j\in\hat{\mathcal W} correspond to an inequality a_j^Tx\ge b_j and satisfy \hat\lambda_j<0. If p solves \min_p\{\tfrac12p^TGp+(G\hat x+c)^Tp:a_i^Tp=0\ \forall i\in\hat{\mathcal W}\setminus\{j\}\}, then a_j^Tp\ge0. If the second-order sufficient conditions hold for this reduced subproblem at p, then a_j^Tp>0 and (G\hat x+c)^Tp<0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a stationary point of the equality-constrained working-set problem, release a working inequality whose multiplier is negative and solve the reduced equality-constrained quadratic subproblem. The resulting step is feasible for the released inequality. Under the reduced subproblem's second-order sufficient conditions, it is strictly feasible for that inequality and is a descent direction for the original quadratic objective.
assumptions_latex: j\in\hat{\mathcal W}\text{ indexes an inequality }a_j^Tx\ge b_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_j^Tp\ge0;\qquad \operatorname{SOSC}_{16.43}(p)\Longrightarrow\left(a_j^Tp>0\ \land\ (G\hat x+c)^Tp<0\right).

children.title: Activity-Estimate Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Regimes where geometric activity differs from the maintained working-set estimate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that an underestimated working face can admit an infeasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1\ge0\}\), \(x=(0,0)\), and \(W=\varnothing\). The inequality is active but omitted. For \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1\), the working-face descent direction \(d=(-1,0)\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x)^Td=-1<0\), yet \(x+\alpha d\notin P\) for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting an active inequality can make the working-face model propose an immediately infeasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla f(x)^Td<0\quad\text{but}\quad x+\alpha d\notin P\ \text{for every }\alpha>0.

notation.meaning: descent direction admitted by the underestimated working face

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Active-Constraint Feasibility Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic certificate for equality of a working estimate and the pointwise active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E^+(W,x)=W\setminus\mathcal A(x)\), \(E^-(W,x)=\mathcal A(x)\setminus W\), and \(m(W,x)=|W\triangle\mathcal A(x)|\). Then \[W=\mathcal A(x)\iff E^+(W,x)=E^-(W,x)=\varnothing\iff m(W,x)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working estimate identifies the active set exactly if and only if both directed mismatches, equivalently their symmetric difference, vanish.
assumptions_latex: W\text{ and }\mathcal A(x)\text{ are finite index sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |W\triangle\mathcal A(x)|=0\iff W=\mathcal A(x).

notation.meaning: working indices that are inactive at x
active indices omitted from the working estimate

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Activity-Identification Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that an overestimated working set need not contain the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge0\}\), take \(x=1\), and let \(W\) contain the sole inequality although it is inactive at \(x\). Imposing it as \(x=0\) gives the estimated face \(F_W=\{0\}\), so \(x\notin F_W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an inactive constraint as an equality can produce a working-face estimate that excludes the current feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\notin F_W.

notation.meaning: affine set obtained by imposing working inequalities as equalities

knowledge_statements.title: Extra-Inactive-Constraint Face-Containment Failure

assumptions_latex: The true active set is \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:(Gx)_i=h_i\}\), and \(W\) is a proposed working set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetric difference \(W\triangle\mathcal A(x)\) separates falsely retained constraints from omitted active constraints.

notation.meaning: Working constraints that are not active.
Active constraints omitted from the working set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic boundary between exact face identification and an erroneous working-set estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E^+(W,x)=W\setminus\mathcal A(x)\) and \(E^-(W,x)=\mathcal A(x)\setminus W\). Exact activity identification holds precisely when \(E^+(W,x)=E^-(W,x)=\varnothing\), equivalently \(W\triangle\mathcal A(x)=\varnothing\). An index in \(E^+(W,x)\) imposes an equality not satisfied by \(x\), so the purported working face need not contain the iterate. An index in \(E^-(W,x)\) removes a tight boundary equation from the face model, so a computed direction can point outside the feasible tangent cone. Therefore either nonempty mismatch set invalidates identification of the equality-constrained model with the actual active face, although a subsequent ratio test or constraint exchange may repair the estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working set is exact only when it has neither inactive extra constraints nor omitted active constraints; either mismatch invalidates its identification with the current face.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Estimate Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-theoretic mismatch definitions are coherent and the failure_boundary kind fits, but the algorithmic consequences of extra and omitted indices lack cited support.

children.top_down_role: Quadratic models restricted to the current estimated face.

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q=Q^T\).
The working set \(W\) is treated as equality constraints and \(K_W=[A^T\;G_W^T]^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The working-face model is an equality-constrained QP whose stationary points satisfy the displayed saddle-point system.

notation.meaning: Combined matrix of permanent and working equalities.
Multipliers for permanent and working equalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_W=[b^T\;h_W^T]^T\). Restricting the QP to the working face gives \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(K_Wx=r_W\). At a feasible face point \(x_k\), its step form is \(\min_p \tfrac12p^TQp+(Qx_k+c)^Tp\) subject to \(K_Wp=0\). A stationary pair \((p,y_W)\) satisfies \(\begin{bmatrix}Q&K_W^T\\K_W&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\y_W\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}Qx_k+c\\0\end{bmatrix}\). If \(K_W\) has full row rank and \(Q\) is positive definite on \(\ker K_W\), this system has a unique solution and the step is the unique face minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating working inequalities as equalities yields an equality-constrained QP, represented by its face-tangent step problem and saddle-point KKT system.

children.title: Multiplier-Based Face Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual evidence used to retain or reject the current face.

assumptions_latex: A feasible point \(x\) satisfies the working-face equalities \(Ax=b\) and \(G_Wx=h_W\).
The inequality convention is \(Gx\le h\), and stationarity is \(Qx+c+A^T\nu+G^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonnegative working multipliers together with primal feasibility and stationarity certify global optimality for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT sign certificate for retaining or rejecting inequalities on a convex-QP working face.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extend the face multipliers by \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i
otin W\). If \(Q\succeq0\), \(x\) is primal feasible, \(Qx+c+A^T
u+G_W^T\lambda_W=0\), and \(\lambda_W\ge0\), then \((x,
u,\lambda)\) satisfies stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity; it is therefore a verifiable global-optimality certificate. If a face-stationary point has some \(\lambda_i<0\) for \(i\in W\), that multiplier fails the dual sign condition. The current face cannot be certified by these multipliers, and a primal-feasible active-set method may select such an index for deletion, commonly choosing a most-negative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex QP, feasible face stationarity and nonnegative active multipliers certify optimality; a negative working multiplier rejects the current face certificate.

children.title: Primal-Feasible Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initialization regimes that begin from a feasible primal face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible feasible point and canonical initial working-set choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) and \(I(x_0)=\{i:G_ix_0=h_i\}\). A primal-feasible active-set initialization is a pair \((x_0,W_0)\) satisfying \(x_0\in P\) and \(W_0\subseteq I(x_0)\). The maximal choice is \(W_0=I(x_0)\). If the working-face solver requires independent equations, dependent equality rows are first removed and \(W_0\) may be chosen so that \([A^T\ G_{W_0}^T]^T\) has full row rank. A basis choice that also spans the row space of \([A^T\ G_{I(x_0)}^T]^T\) has the same tangent null space as the maximal choice. Neither stationarity nor multiplier-sign feasibility is part of primal-feasible initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a feasible point and select only tight inequalities. One may use all tight constraints or an independent basis when the face solver requires it.
assumptions_latex: \text{Any rank requirement is imposed by the selected working-face solver.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0\in P,\quad W_0\subseteq I(x_0);\qquad \operatorname{row}(A,G_{W_0})=\operatorname{row}(A,G_{I(x_0)})\Rightarrow\ker(A,G_{W_0})=\ker(A,G_{I(x_0)}).

notation.meaning: Tight inequality indices at the initial point.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Initialization

assumptions_latex: The constraint set is \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid primal-feasible initialization is a pair \((x_0,W_0)\) with \(x_0\in P\) and \(W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization condition for active-set iterations that must preserve primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-feasible initialization consists of \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a working set \(W_0\) satisfying \(Ax_0=b\), \(Gx_0\le h\), and \(W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0)=\{i:G_ix_0=h_i\}\). If the initial face model requires independent normals, the rows of \([A^T\;G_{W_0}^T]^T\) must additionally have full row rank after redundant rows are removed. This condition supplies a feasible initial face for methods whose line search truncates steps at newly encountered constraints. It does not impose stationarity or dual feasibility; those are established through face minimization and working-set exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-feasible initialization requires a feasible point and a working set drawn from its tight constraints, with dependent rows removed when the face solver requires full rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initialization condition is standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports the active-set-specific rank and initialization requirements.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible starting triple \((x_0,\nu_0,\lambda_0)\) satisfies \(Qx_0+c+A^T\nu_0+G^T\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_0\ge0\). Equality feasibility \(Ax_0=b\), inequality feasibility \(Gx_0\le h\), and complementarity \(\lambda_{0i}(G_ix_0-h_i)=0\) are not required by dual feasibility alone. A compatible initial working estimate may be defined by \(W_0=\{i:\lambda_{0i}>0\}\), optionally augmented by zero-multiplier indices. Dual active-set iterations then preserve the multiplier sign condition while exchanging constraints to reduce primal infeasibility and ultimately seek the remaining KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible start satisfies stationarity with nonnegative inequality multipliers, while primal feasibility and complementarity may initially fail and are repaired by constraint exchanges.

children.title: Active-Set Phase-I Methods
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary face-navigation families for finding primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Always-feasible auxiliary LP for mixed equality and inequality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), solve \[\Phi^*=\min_{x,p,n,v}\ \mathbf1^T(p+n)+\mathbf1^Tv\] subject to \[Ax-b=p-n,\qquad Gx-h\le v,\qquad p,n,v\ge0.\] The auxiliary LP is feasible for all finite data and has an attained finite optimum. Moreover, \(\Phi^*=0\) if and only if \(P\ne\varnothing\). A zero optimum returns a feasible \(x^*\); a positive optimum, together with an optimal auxiliary dual solution, provides a checkable infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize total equality artificials and inequality violations. The optimum is zero exactly when the original constraints are feasible.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is unrestricted, and }p,n,v\text{ are componentwise nonnegative.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi^*=0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Fully Elastic Linear Phase I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination and worst-case boundary for simplex-style active-set solution of the auxiliary LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplex-style Phase-I implementation using an anti-cycling pivot rule terminates after finitely many bases and returns the auxiliary optimum or its dual certificate. Without an anti-cycling rule, degeneracy can cause repeated bases; finite termination does not imply a polynomial pivot bound, since exponentially long pivot paths are possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anti-cycling gives finite Phase-I pivot termination, but degeneracy can otherwise cycle and finite termination is not a polynomial-time guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary LP is solved by exact simplex-style basis pivots.
A finite anti-cycling rule is used for the finite-termination conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{anti-cycling}\Rightarrow\text{finite basis termination},\qquad \text{finite termination}\not\Rightarrow\text{polynomial pivot complexity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Pivot Termination Boundary

assumptions_latex: The linear constraint system is \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
The auxiliary problem is solved to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Phase-I optimum \(t^*=0\) yields a feasible point for the original constraints; \(t^*>0\) certifies infeasibility of this system.
review_flags: specific authoritative active-set Phase-I locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-slack linear Phase-I construction for finding feasibility before QP optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((A,b,G,h)\). Initialize any \(x^{(0)}\) satisfying \(Ax^{(0)}=b\), when the equalities are consistent, and set \(t^{(0)}=\max\{0,\max_i(G_ix^{(0)}-h_i)\}\). Solve the auxiliary linear program \(\min_{x,t}t\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx-h\le t\mathbf1\), and \(t\ge0\), using working-face steps and ratio tests. Stop at a global minimizer \((x^*,t^*)\). If \(t^*=0\), output \(x^*\), which is feasible for the original constraints, together with its tight-constraint working set. If \(t^*>0\), report that the original linear constraint system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a common nonnegative constraint-violation variable by active-set steps; zero optimum provides a feasible start, while a positive global optimum proves the constraints infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Phase-I Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Phase-I conclusion is valid only when the equality system is consistent and the auxiliary LP has an optimum. As written, the algorithm does not handle inconsistent equalities despite claiming to diagnose the full constraint system, and it has no source.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x_0,W_0)\) with \(x_0\) feasible and \(W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the equality-constrained working-face QP for \(p_k\). If \(p_k\ne0\), choose \(\alpha_k=\min\{1,\min_{i\notin W_k,\ G_ip_k>0}(h_i-G_ix_k)/(G_ip_k)\}\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and add a blocking index when \(\alpha_k<1\). If \(p_k=0\), compute working multipliers; stop when they are nonnegative, otherwise delete an index with negative multiplier. Output the terminal primal-dual pair. The ratio rule preserves \(Ax_k=b\) and \(Gx_k\le h\) at every accepted iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal multiplier step preserving nonnegativity during a dual active-set exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \lambda\ge0 and let p be a multiplier direction. The maximal forward step preserving dual feasibility is \alpha_{\max}=\min_{i:p_i<0}(-\lambda_i/p_i), with \alpha_{\max}=+\infty if p_i\ge0 for every i. Every 0\le\alpha\le\alpha_{\max} satisfies \lambda+\alpha p\ge0; at a finite maximal step, at least one blocking multiplier becomes zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum multiplier ratio is the longest forward step preserving dual feasibility and identifies leaving candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\alpha\le\alpha_{\max}\Rightarrow\lambda+\alpha p\ge0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite primal regime in which dual-feasible exchanges operate on a bound-constrained quadratic dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n, the primal QP \min_x\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx subject to Ax\ge b has dual \max_{\lambda\ge0}d(\lambda), where d(\lambda)=-\tfrac12(A^T\lambda-c)^TH^{-1}(A^T\lambda-c)+b^T\lambda. Every \lambda\ge0 is dual feasible, and x(\lambda)=H^{-1}(A^T\lambda-c) satisfies stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite curvature, the dual is a concave quadratic over nonnegative multipliers, each inducing a stationary primal estimate.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is Ax\ge b with \lambda\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\ge0\Rightarrow Hx(\lambda)+c-A^T\lambda=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every restricted-dual solve is unique, every nonterminal pivot strictly increases d, and an anti-cycling rule prevents revisiting a working set, then the dual-feasible active-set algorithm terminates after finitely many working-set changes at a dual KKT point. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_x\tfrac12x^2 subject to two duplicate constraints x\ge1. Its dual is \max_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0}-\tfrac12(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)^2+\lambda_1+\lambda_2, and its optimal set is \{\lambda\ge0:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\}. An unrestricted exchange policy may alternate between (1,0) and (0,1). Both points are dual feasible and optimal, so the objective supplies no strict progress although the primal estimate remains x=1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated active constraints allow zero-progress exchanges between distinct optimal multiplier supports.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Constraint Zero-Progress Exchanges

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For H\succeq0, the Lagrangian infimum of \min_x\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx subject to Ax\ge b is finite at \lambda\ge0 exactly when A^T\lambda-c\in\operatorname{range}(H). On that domain, d(\lambda)=b^T\lambda-\tfrac12(A^T\lambda-c)^TH^\dagger(A^T\lambda-c). Thus dual feasibility requires both nonnegativity and the range constraint; when H\succ0 the range constraint is automatic and H^\dagger=H^{-1}.

otin W_0\). While primal feasibility or complementarity fails, select a violated or incompatible constraint and solve the associated equality-constrained primal-dual correction system. Move along that correction only until either the selected primal residual is removed or some positive working multiplier reaches zero; in the latter case delete its index and continue. Maintain stationarity, nonnegative multipliers, and zero multipliers outside \(W_k\). Stop and output the iterate when primal feasibility and complementarity also hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain stationarity and nonnegative multipliers while pivoting constraints to repair primal infeasibility; stop when primal feasibility and complementarity complete the convex-QP KKT system.

children.title: Complementarity-Based Primal-Dual Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Families that update primal and dual activity through complementarity partitions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of unrestricted primal-dual partition updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without suitable nondegeneracy, reduced-system solvability, and an anti-cycling or globalization rule, complementarity-partition iterations can revisit partitions, alternate among weakly active constraints, or encounter singular reduced KKT systems. Finiteness of the set of partitions alone therefore does not imply finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy and unrestricted partition exchanges can cause cycling or singular reduced systems.
assumptions_latex: No anti-cycling or nondegeneracy hypothesis is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\{\text{partitions}\}<\infty\not\Rightarrow\text{finite termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cycling and Singular-Partition Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth equation underlying complementarity-partition active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \min_x\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx subject to r=Ax-b\ge0, the KKT conditions are equivalent to Hx+c-A^T\lambda=0 and \Phi(r,\lambda)=0, where \Phi_i(r,\lambda)=\min\{r_i,\lambda_i\}. For any \gamma>0, selecting the branch by \lambda_i-\gamma r_i>0 versus \lambda_i-\gamma r_i\le0 defines an active/inactive partition; fixing that partition reduces the equations to a linear KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The QP KKT system is stationarity plus a componentwise complementarity equation whose branch choices define an active partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{r_i,\lambda_i\}=0\ \forall i\iff r\ge0,\ \lambda\ge0,\ r_i\lambda_i=0\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity-Function QP System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness of a complementarity-based primal-dual partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (x^*,\lambda^*) be a KKT point satisfying strict complementarity, and suppose its active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular. For every fixed \gamma>0, the signs of \lambda_i-\gamma r_i agree with the optimal partition throughout some neighborhood of (x^*,\lambda^*). Once a pair in that neighborhood is classified and the resulting reduced KKT system is solved exactly, the solve returns (x^*,\lambda^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity and KKT nonsingularity make the correct partition locally stable, after which one exact reduced solve returns the solution.
assumptions_latex: The optimal active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular.
The reduced linear system is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U:\ (x,\lambda)\in U\Rightarrow\mathcal A_\gamma(x,\lambda)=\mathcal A^*.

notation.meaning: Partition selected by the complementarity test.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Active-Partition Identification

assumptions_latex: Fallback partition-feasibility systems are decided exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns a KKT pair whenever one exists and otherwise exhausts at most }2^m\text{ fallback partitions}.

notation.meaning: Fixed maximum number of residual-decreasing trial steps before fallback.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic complementarity-partition iteration with a finite exhaustive safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For F(x,\lambda)=(Hx+c-A^T\lambda,\min\{Ax-b,\lambda\}), classify index i as active when \lambda_i-\gamma(Ax-b)_i>0 and inactive otherwise, resolving equality by a fixed index rule. Solve the corresponding linear branch equations for \widehat z. If the branch system has a unique solution, test z+2^{-j}(\widehat z-z) for j=0,\ldots,J and accept the first trial that strictly decreases \|F\|_2. If the branch system is singular, no tested trial decreases the residual, or a partition repeats, enumerate all subsets \mathcal A lexicographically and decide Hx+c-A_{\mathcal A}^T\lambda_{\mathcal A}=0, A_{\mathcal A}x=b_{\mathcal A}, \lambda_{\mathcal A}\ge0, A_{\mathcal I}x-b_{\mathcal I}\ge0, and \lambda_{\mathcal I}=0. Return the first feasible partition system, or report absence of a KKT pair after exhausting all subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use complementarity branches and finitely many residual-decreasing trials, then fall back deterministically to exhaustive KKT partition testing when a branch is singular, unproductive, or repeated.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Complementarity-Partition Method

assumptions_latex: Each partition-feasibility problem is decided exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{tests}}\le2^m.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness and combinatorial cost of exhaustive complementarity-partition resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are 2^m complementarity partitions. Every KKT pair satisfies the feasibility system of at least one partition, and every feasible partition system is a KKT certificate. Therefore exhaustive deterministic partition testing terminates after at most 2^m tests and returns a KKT pair exactly when one exists. The bound is exponential and supplies no polynomial guarantee for ordinary primal-dual active-set iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive partition safeguarding is finitely correct but may require exponentially many tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Partition Safeguard Correctness
Complementarity-Based Primal-Dual Active-Set Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual working-set iteration for a convex inequality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\). Initialize \((x^0,\lambda^0)\) and partition indices into \(\mathcal A^k\) and \(\mathcal I^k\). Solve the reduced primal-dual equations \(Hx^{k+1}+c-A_{\mathcal A^k}^T\lambda_{\mathcal A^k}^{k+1}=0\), \(A_{\mathcal A^k}x^{k+1}=b_{\mathcal A^k}\), and \(\lambda_{\mathcal I^k}^{k+1}=0\). Move to \(\mathcal A^{k+1}\) every violated inactive constraint and to \(\mathcal I^{k+1}\) every active index with negative multiplier, using a deterministic tie rule. Stop when primal feasibility and \(\lambda^{k+1}\ge0\) hold; then output \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve equality-constrained primal-dual systems, activating violated inequalities and releasing active inequalities with invalid multipliers, until all KKT complementarity conditions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and the feasible polyhedron is nonempty.
Each reduced KKT system is solvable.
The inequality convention is \(Ax\ge b\) with \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(Hx+c-A^T\lambda=0\), \(Ax-b\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda_i(Ax-b)_i=0\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-projection variant for differently scaled box coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D\succ0 be diagonal and y=P_\Omega^D(x-\alpha D^{-1}\nabla q(x)), where P_\Omega^D minimizes \tfrac12\|z-v\|_D^2 over z\in\Omega. With d=y-x, \nabla q(x)^Td\le-\|d\|_D^2/\alpha. Because D is diagonal and \Omega is a box, y is obtained by coordinatewise clipping of the scaled trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal metric gives a scaled feasible descent displacement while preserving coordinatewise box clipping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\ne0\Rightarrow\nabla q(x)^Td<0.

notation.meaning: Projection in the D-weighted Euclidean norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Scaled Projected Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate descent geometry and optimality test for a Euclidean projected direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For d=P_\Omega(x-\alpha
abla q(x))-x with \alpha>0, the projection variational inequality gives 
abla q(x)^Td\le-\|d\|^2/\alpha. Hence d is a feasible strict-descent displacement when d
e0. Moreover, d=0 if and only if 0\in
abla q(x)+N_\Omega(x); for a convex quadratic this is equivalent to global optimality over \Omega.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected displacement is feasible and descending unless zero, and zero displacement exactly characterizes a convex box-QP solution.
assumptions_latex: q is convex for the global-optimality equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla q(x)^Td\le-\|d\|^2/\alpha,\qquad d=0\iff0\in\nabla q(x)+N_\Omega(x).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone of the box at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Step Descent and Fixed-Point Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Decrease of a Projected QP Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective decrease obtained from projection and quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H\succeq0, L=\lambda_{\max}(H), and d=P_\Omega(x-\alpha\nabla q(x))-x. If L>0 and 0<\alpha<2/L, then q(x+d)-q(x)\le-(1/\alpha-L/2)\|d\|^2. If L=0, the same inequality with L=0 holds for every \alpha>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-gradient step below the two-over-curvature threshold gives quantified objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\ne0\Rightarrow q(x+d)<q(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Decrease of a Projected QP Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate formula and breakpoint behavior for projection onto a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \Omega=[\ell,u], g=\nabla q(x), and \alpha\ge0, d(\alpha)=P_\Omega(x-\alpha g)-x has components d_i(\alpha)=\min\{u_i-x_i,\max\{\ell_i-x_i,-\alpha g_i\}\}. Thus d(\alpha) is continuous and piecewise affine in \alpha, and a coordinate changes slope only when the unprojected ray reaches a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box-projected gradient displacement is coordinatewise clipping and is piecewise affine in the step length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_i(\alpha)=\operatorname{clip}(-\alpha g_i,\ell_i-x_i,u_i-x_i).

notation.meaning: Projected-gradient displacement at step length alpha.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Projected-Gradient Displacement
Projected Search Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection displacement for bound-constrained convex quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(q(x)=	frac12x^THx+c^Tx\), and choose \(\alpha>0\). Define \(d_\alpha(x)=P_\Omega(x-\alpha
abla q(x))-x\). Then \(x+d_\alpha(x)\in\Omega\), and the projection variational inequality gives \(
abla q(x)^Td_\alpha(x)\le-\|d_\alpha(x)\|^2/\alpha\). Consequently, \(d_\alpha(x)\) is a feasible descent displacement whenever it is nonzero. Moreover, \(d_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in
abla q(x)+N_\Omega(x)\), which is the first-order optimality condition for minimizing the convex quadratic over \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected-gradient displacement remains feasible, is a descent direction unless zero, and vanishes exactly at a first-order solution of the bound-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla q(x)^Td_\alpha(x)\le-\|d_\alpha(x)\|^2/\alpha\), and \(d_\alpha(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla q(x)+N_\Omega(x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone to the box at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the projected-direction leaf, and the projection inequality, feasibility, descent conclusion, and normal-cone fixed-point characterization are mathematically consistent for Euclidean projection onto the box. No source is supplied, so the nontrivial projection and optimality claims require an authoritative projected-gradient or convex-analysis citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Candidate-Face Discovery
children.top_down_role: Geometric information through which projected searches reveal likely active faces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact acceptance test for a proposed box face after restricted minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a candidate box face have lower-active indices \mathcal A_\ell, upper-active indices \mathcal A_u, and free indices \mathcal F. If x minimizes the convex quadratic over that face, then x is globally optimal over [\ell,u] exactly when 
abla_{\mathcal F}q(x)=0, 
abla_iq(x)\ge0 for i\in\mathcal A_\ell, and 
abla_iq(x)\le0 for i\in\mathcal A_u. A failed bound-sign test identifies a fixed bound that cannot be retained in a globally optimal face containing x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face minimizer is globally optimal exactly when its free gradient vanishes and every fixed-bound gradient has the correct sign.
assumptions_latex: x minimizes q over the proposed face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{[\ell,u]}q\iff\text{the free-gradient and bound-sign conditions hold}.

notation.meaning: Lower-active, upper-active, and free coordinate sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Face KKT Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual correctness of projected-trial face information for a box QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^* solve a convex box-constrained QP and satisfy strict complementarity at each active bound. If x_k\to x^*, \alpha_k\in[\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha] with 0<\underline\alpha\le\overline\alpha<\infty, and y_k=P_{[\ell,u]}(x_k-\alpha_k\nabla q(x_k)), then for all sufficiently large k every bound active at x^* is active at y_k, while every coordinate strictly interior at x^* remains interior at y_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent projected trials eventually identify strictly complementary active bounds and preserve truly interior coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Step lengths are bounded above and away from zero.
Strict complementarity holds at every active bound of x^*.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K:\ k\ge K\Rightarrow\mathcal A(y_k)=\mathcal A(x^*).

notation.meaning: Projected trial point used for face discovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Identification under Strict Complementarity

assumptions_latex: x\in[\ell,u], all bounds are finite, and \alpha>0.
All absolute and relative tolerances are nonnegative.
Endpoint priority and tie rules are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A_\ell,\mathcal A_u,\mathcal F\ \text{form a disjoint partition and define a box face}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint scale-aware lower, upper, free, and narrow-interval classification for a finite box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For x\in[\ell,u], choose \alpha>0 and set y=P_{[\ell,u]}(x-\alpha
abla q(x)). Let \delta_i^x=	au_x^{m abs}+	au_x^{m rel}\max\{1,|\ell_i|,|u_i|,|x_i|\} and \delta_i^g=	au_g^{m abs}+	au_g^{m rel}\max\{1,|
abla_iq(x)|\}. First classify every i with u_i-\ell_i\le2\delta_i^x as narrow and assign it to the nearer endpoint using a fixed tie rule. For each remaining coordinate, classify it lower-active if y_i-\ell_i\le\delta_i^x and 
abla_iq(x)\ge-\delta_i^g; otherwise classify it upper-active if u_i-y_i\le\delta_i^x and 
abla_iq(x)\le\delta_i^g; otherwise classify it free. The ordered tests make the classes disjoint. Fix classified coordinates at their assigned endpoints and leave free coordinates within their bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a gradient trial and apply scaled position and gradient tests, with deterministic treatment of narrow intervals and overlaps, to form a disjoint candidate face.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled-Tolerance Projected Face Estimator
Candidate-Face Discovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A projected-gradient rule for proposing the active face of a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(x)=	frac12x^THx+c^Tx\) on \(\Omega=[\ell,u]\), choose \(\alpha>0\), compute \(y=P_\Omega(x-\alpha
abla q(x))\), and select a tolerance \(	au\ge0\). Define \(\mathcal A_\ell=\{i:y_i=\ell_i,\ 
abla_iq(x)\ge-	au\}\), \(\mathcal A_u=\{i:y_i=u_i,\ 
abla_iq(x)\le	au\}\), and \(\mathcal F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(\mathcal A_\ell\cup\mathcal A_u)\). The candidate face fixes \(z_i=\ell_i\) on \(\mathcal A_\ell\), fixes \(z_i=u_i\) on \(\mathcal A_u\), and leaves coordinates in \(\mathcal F\) free within their bounds. Output this face for subsequent restricted minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a gradient trial point, classify bounds whose gradient signs support activity, and use the resulting fixed coordinates as a candidate face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the box face \(F=\{z\in\Omega:z_{\mathcal A_\ell}=\ell_{\mathcal A_\ell},\ z_{\mathcal A_u}=u_{\mathcal A_u}\}\).

notation.meaning: Proposed lower- and upper-active coordinate sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Bound Identification under Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-identification result for convergent projected-gradient iterates on a box; strict complementarity is not asserted to be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{k+1}=P_{[\ell,u]}(x_k-\alpha_k
abla q(x_k))\), where \(q\in C^1\), \(x_k	o x^*\), and \(0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha<\infty\). Suppose that, for every \(i\) with \(\ell_i<u_i\), \(
abla_iq(x^*)>0\) when \(x_i^*=\ell_i\) and \(
abla_iq(x^*)<0\) when \(x_i^*=u_i\). Then there is \(K\) such that, for every \(k\ge K\), each active coordinate of \(x^*\) is fixed at its corresponding bound, each coordinate interior at \(x^*\) remains interior, and every fixed coordinate \(\ell_i=u_i\) remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent box-projected gradient iterates finitely identify every strictly complementary active bound; coordinates interior at the limit are eventually interior.
assumptions_latex: Every nonfixed active bound at \(x^*\) has the stated strict gradient sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K\), the lower-bound, upper-bound, interior, and fixed-coordinate classifications of \(x_k\) agree with those of \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the bound box.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Bound Identification under Strict Complementarity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\alpha<1\Rightarrow x_k>0\ \forall k\text{ and }x_k\to0;\qquad \alpha=1\Rightarrow x_1=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-rule dependence of finite identification at a zero-multiplier active bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize q(x)=\tfrac12x^2 over [0,\infty). The unique solution x^*=0 has zero bound multiplier. From x_0>0, projected gradient with constant 0<\alpha<1 gives x_{k+1}=P_{[0,\infty)}((1-\alpha)x_k)=(1-\alpha)x_k>0 for every finite k, although x_k\to0. With \alpha=1, the same problem reaches x^*=0 in one step. Thus absence of strict complementarity removes a general finite-identification guarantee but does not make finite identification impossible for every step rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-multiplier solution, one valid projected-gradient step rule approaches the active bound forever while another identifies it immediately.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Multiplier Identification Depends on the Step Rule
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Multiplier Identification Depends on the Step Rule
Projection-Induced Identification Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stable active-face identification without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(q_\varepsilon(x)=\tfrac12x^2-\varepsilon x\) on \(\Omega=[0,\infty)\). Its unique solution is \(x_\varepsilon^*=\max\{\varepsilon,0\}\). For \(\varepsilon<0\), the lower bound is active with multiplier \(-\varepsilon>0\); for \(\varepsilon>0\), the solution is interior; and at \(\varepsilon=0\), the solution lies on the bound with zero multiplier. Thus arbitrarily small perturbations of the gradient change the correct active face at the degenerate instance. Projection alone cannot provide locally stable finite identification there; strict complementarity or an equivalent separation condition is needed for robust face identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-multiplier active bound, arbitrarily small objective perturbations switch the solution between boundary and interior, so projection cannot stably identify the face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), active-face identification is not locally invariant under perturbations of \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the scalar example correctly demonstrates that the optimal active face is not locally invariant with respect to the parameter at the zero-multiplier instance. The stronger assertion that projection alone cannot provide locally stable finite identification, and that strict complementarity or an equivalent condition is necessary, is not established by the example alone and has no citation. A finite-identification or active-manifold identification source is required, and the final claim must be calibrated to the exact hypotheses of that source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-CG Complexity on a Fixed Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner solution complexity for a positive-definite reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If R=Z^THZ\succ0, conjugate gradients applied to Rp=-g reaches the exact reduced minimizer in at most \dim\ker B iterations in exact arithmetic. If the eigenvalues of R lie in [m,L], then \|p_k-p^*\|_R\le2((\sqrt{L/m}-1)/(\sqrt{L/m}+1))^k\|p_0-p^*\|_R.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed face with positive-definite reduced curvature, reduced CG terminates in the subspace dimension and has the standard condition-number rate.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact for the finite-termination assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k\le\dim\ker B:\ p_k=p^*.

notation.meaning: Energy norm induced by the reduced Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-CG Complexity on a Fixed Face

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-Hull Solvability of the Reduced Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness for the unrestricted reduced subspace problem, before face-bound truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=Z^THZ and g=Z^T(Hx_F+c). If R\succ0, the affine-hull restriction has the unique minimizer p^*=-R^{-1}g. If R\succeq0, it has a minimizer exactly when g\in\operatorname{range}(R), in which case the minimizers solve Rp=-g. If g\notin\operatorname{range}(R), the affine-hull quadratic is unbounded below along a null direction. These statements do not by themselves assert feasibility with respect to additional inequalities bounding the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite reduced curvature gives a unique subspace minimizer; semidefinite curvature requires reduced-gradient compatibility.
assumptions_latex: Optimization is over the entire affine hull represented by Z.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathbb R^{\dim\ker B}}\widehat q(p)\ne\varnothing\iff g\in\operatorname{range}(R).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Hull Solvability of the Reduced Quadratic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Coordinates on a Working Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space representation of the quadratic on the affine hull of a selected face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the affine hull of a nonempty face be \{x:Bx=d\}, choose x_F in that affine hull, and let the columns of Z form a basis of \ker B. Then x=x_F+Zp and q(x)=\tfrac12p^T(Z^THZ)p+[Z^T(Hx_F+c)]^Tp+q(x_F). The reduced stationarity equation is (Z^THZ)p=-Z^T(Hx_F+c).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space coordinates turn affine-hull minimization on a selected face into a reduced unconstrained quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The face affine hull is nonempty.
Z has full column rank and BZ=0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla\widehat q(p)=Z^T(H(x_F+Zp)+c).

notation.meaning: Basis of directions parallel to the face.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Coordinates on a Working Face

assumptions_latex: The current point satisfies all free-coordinate bounds.
Every fixed coordinate already equals the bound defining the current face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^+\in[\ell,u],\quad \beta_*=1\Rightarrow\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x^+)=0,\quad \beta_*<1\Rightarrow\text{at least one formerly free bound is reached}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact free-coordinate Newton step with first-bound refinement on a box face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x lie on a box face with fixed coordinates \mathcal A and free coordinates \mathcal F. Solve H_{\mathcal F\mathcal F}p_{\mathcal F}=-\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x) and set p_{\mathcal A}=0. Define \beta_*=\min\left\{1,\min_{i\in\mathcal F:p_i<0}(x_i-\ell_i)/(-p_i),\min_{i\in\mathcal F:p_i>0}(u_i-x_i)/p_i\right\}, with an empty inner minimum equal to +\infty, and set x^+=x+\beta_*p. If \beta_*=1, x^+ is the affine-hull minimizer and has zero free gradient. If \beta_*<1, every index attaining the minimum reaches a bound and is fixed there in the refined face; all simultaneous hitters are added together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the exact free Newton direction, truncate it at the first bound, and either finish the affine-hull minimization or refine the face with every hitting coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Box-Face Reduced Newton Step and Boundary Truncation
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Face Reduced Newton Step and Boundary Truncation
Face-Restricted Subspace Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or truncated quadratic minimization over a discovered box face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a box face with active coordinates \(\mathcal A\) fixed at \(\bar x_{\mathcal A}\) and free coordinates \(\mathcal F\). For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\), solve \(H_{\mathcal F\mathcal F}p_{\mathcal F}=-\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x)\) and set \(p_{\mathcal A}=0\). Choose the largest \(\beta\in[0,1]\) for which \(x+\beta p\) remains in the face bounds, and update \(x^+=x+\beta p\). If \(\beta=1\), the free-gradient vanishes at \(x^+\); otherwise, at least one free coordinate reaches a boundary and the candidate face is refined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the Newton equations on free coordinates, truncate at the first face boundary, and either minimize over the face or discover another active bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x^+)=0\), or the step reaches a previously free bound while remaining feasible on \(F\).
