children.title: Strictly Convex Finite-Termination Theory
children.top_down_role: Finite face-transition theory in the nonsingular convex regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Convex Finite-Termination Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination for an exact feasible active-set method with deterministic anti-cycling transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible active-set method for \(\min_x \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), where \(H\succ0\). At each iteration it exactly solves the equality-constrained QP for the current working set, takes the maximal feasible step, and changes the working set whenever the KKT sign test fails. Assume every degenerate tie is resolved by a rule that prevents revisiting a previously encountered zero-progress working-set state. Then the method performs finitely many working-set transitions and terminates at the unique minimizer \(x^*\). The conclusion follows at the algorithmic level only with the stated anti-cycling condition; strict convexity alone does not exclude repeated degenerate working sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact feasible active-set method for a strictly convex QP terminates finitely when its tie rule forbids repeated zero-progress working-set states.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) and the feasible set is nonempty.
Equality-constrained subproblems and blocking steps are computed exactly.
The transition rule prevents repeated zero-progress working-set states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty:\ x_K=x^*\) and the KKT conditions hold at \(x_K\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits, but the described method is not sufficiently fixed to derive finite termination. A source must connect exact subproblem solves, transition rules, and the stated nonrevisitation safeguard to termination.

children.title: Semidefinite Active-Set Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior with flat directions and nonunique minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Active-Set Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence for convex QPs with flat directions and possibly nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succeq0\), let the polyhedral feasible set be nonempty, and suppose the QP has a minimizer. Consider a feasible active-set method that produces nonincreasing objective values, solves each working-face subproblem globally, detects feasible recession directions of zero or negative curvature, and uses an anti-cycling rule for zero-progress transitions. If no unboundedness certificate is returned, every accumulation point satisfies the QP KKT conditions and is therefore globally optimal. When the optimal set is non-singleton, the assumptions do not imply convergence to a unique minimizer or stabilization of a unique working set; those conclusions require an additional selection or regularization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a semidefinite convex QP, safeguarded face minimization yields optimal accumulation points, but flat directions can prevent unique point or working-set convergence.
assumptions_latex: Every working-face subproblem is solved globally with recession detection.
Zero-progress transitions obey an anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{acc}(x_k)\Rightarrow \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax\ge b}f(x)\), without necessarily \(x_k\to\bar x\).

notation.meaning: set of accumulation points of the iterates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semidefinite setting and qualified conclusion fit the leaf, but monotonicity, global face solves, recession detection, and anti-cycling do not define a standard method sufficiently precisely to establish that every accumulation point is KKT.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{acc}(x_k)=\{0,1\}\subset X^*,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}x_k\ \text{does not exist}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic sequence-level observation on a flat optimal set; deferred because it is not tied to an active-set QP algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{0\le x\le1}0\), a convex QP with \(H=0\) and optimal set \(X^*=[0,1]\). The feasible sequence \(x_{2k}=0\), \(x_{2k+1}=1\) has constant objective value, every accumulation point is globally optimal, and yet \(\{x_k\}\) does not converge. Therefore, in the semidefinite regime, monotonic objective values and optimality of every accumulation point do not imply convergence to one minimizer without an additional selection, regularization, or asymptotic-regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a flat optimal face, an arbitrary feasible sequence can alternate between optimal points; this does not by itself describe an active-set method.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Accumulation Does Not Imply Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Accumulation Does Not Imply Iterate Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own convergence behavior of a specified active-set QP method when curvature is only semidefinite, including the distinction between optimal accumulation points, full-sequence convergence, and working-set stabilization. The positive theorem remains algorithmically ambiguous, and the Builder's arbitrary alternating optimal sequence is not an active-set counterexample, so it is deferred. PSD model definitions, reduced-Hessian geometry, inexact face solves, positive-definite termination, anti-cycling, and complexity bounds were excluded as prerequisite or sibling scopes.

children.title: Lexicographic Anti-Cycling Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Safeguard families for repeated or zero-length face transitions.

children.title: Anti-Cycling Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms preventing repeated working-face patterns or nonproductive transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Anti-Cycling Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A state-ordering requirement that prevents repeated degenerate active-set transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an active-set state be the pair \((x_k,W_k)\). An anti-cycling safeguard assigns every admissible zero-progress transition a value in a well-founded strict order and accepts such a transition only when that value decreases; equivalently, it may use a lexicographic perturbation whose induced pivot sequence is strictly ordered. Positive-step transitions retain the usual feasibility and objective tests. Because no infinite strictly descending sequence or repeated ordered state is possible, only finitely many consecutive zero-progress transitions can occur. This safeguard excludes cycling among working sets representing the same primal point, but finite termination of the complete method additionally requires well-posed subproblems and progress away from degenerate states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order zero-progress states lexicographically or by another well-founded ranking; strict descent prevents cycling, while full termination still needs ordinary progress conditions.
assumptions_latex: Every zero-progress working-set transition receives a deterministic rank.
The rank belongs to a well-founded strict order.
Only rank-decreasing zero-progress transitions are accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\,k,r>0:\ (x_{k+r},W_{k+r})=(x_k,W_k)\) within an accepted zero-progress transition chain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits. Strict descent in a well-founded order excludes an infinite zero-progress chain, but the asserted equivalence with lexicographic perturbation and its integration into active-set transitions require an algorithm-specific source.

children.title: Lexicographic Pivot Selection
children.top_down_role: Ordered selection regimes for resolving ambiguous admissions or releases.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic program is handled by a deterministic primal or dual active-set method in exact arithmetic.
At an iteration, the admissible pivot set \(E\) is finite, and every \(e\in E\) has a finite comparison vector \(v_e\in\mathbb{R}^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pivot is unique whenever the comparison vectors are distinct under lexicographic order.

notation.meaning: finite set of admissible entering or leaving pivots
comparison vector associated with pivot e

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: lexicographic comparison is the standard deterministic perturbation surrogate for resolving active-set pivot ties
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic lexicographic rule for choosing one admissible active-set pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vectors \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^q\), write \(u<_{\mathrm{lex}}v\) when, at the first index \(j\) satisfying \(u_j\ne v_j\), one has \(u_j<v_j\). Assign every admissible pivot \(e\in E\) a comparison vector \(v_e=(\rho_e,\delta_{e,1},\ldots,\delta_{e,q-1})\), whose first component is the ordinary blocking ratio or multiplier test and whose remaining components encode a fixed symbolic perturbation. Select \[e_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{e\in E}^{\mathrm{lex}}v_e.\] If residual equality remains, append the fixed constraint index to \(v_e\). Execute \(e_*\), update the working set, and stop only when the active-set optimality test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare eligible pivots by ratio, then symbolic perturbation components, and finally fixed index. The lexicographically smallest pivot gives a deterministic tie-breaking update.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Pivot Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and terminal placement fit, and the lexicographic rule is mathematically coherent. A dedicated active-set QP source is required for the perturbation key, pivot semantics, and claimed anti-cycling role.

children.title: Degeneracy-Tie Resolution
children.top_down_role: Tie-handling regimes for coincident blockers, multipliers, or zero-length moves.

assumptions_latex: The admissible pivot set \(E_k\) at iteration \(k\) is finite.
Each candidate has a primary test value \(\rho_e\), perturbation signature \(s_e\), and fixed index \(i_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonempty tied candidate set yields exactly one selected pivot, including when the primary step length is zero.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: total lexicographic ordering with a fixed final index uniquely resolves finite degeneracy ties
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic resolution of simultaneous blockers and zero-length degenerate pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(e\in E_k\), form the ordered key \(\kappa_e=(\rho_e,s_e,i_e)\), where \(\rho_e\) is the primary ratio or multiplier value, \(s_e\) is the finite symbolic-perturbation signature, and \(i_e\) is a distinct fixed index. Order keys lexicographically and choose \[e_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{e\in E_k}^{\mathrm{lex}}\kappa_e.\] Thus simultaneous blocking constraints, tied multiplier violations, and candidates with \(\rho_e=0\) are resolved without an arbitrary choice. The index is consulted only when all preceding components agree, so it does not alter any strict primary comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve every ratio or multiplier tie by a fixed lexicographic perturbation signature, using the constraint index only as the final deterministic discriminator.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Tie Resolution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits deterministic degeneracy-tie resolution, but no source supports applying this key uniformly to blocking, multiplier, and zero-length pivots.

children.title: Inexact Working-Face Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families allowing approximate equality-constrained solves.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\ \forall k,\qquad x_k\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\ge0}f.

notation.meaning: basis for the tangent space of the working face

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global KKT convergence when an accurately solved but incorrect working face is never released.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12(x-1)^2\). Start at \(x_0=0\), retain the bound as an equality forever, and set \(x_k=0\) for every \(k\). The working face is the singleton \(\{0\}\), so its tangent space is \(\{0\}\) and every reduced-gradient residual is exactly zero. Nevertheless \(x=0\) is not optimal and its active multiplier under \(\nabla f(x)-\lambda=0\) equals \(\lambda=-1<0\). Hence vanishing working-face residuals alone do not imply a KKT accumulation point; an incorrect active constraint must eventually be released.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact stationarity on the wrong face can hold forever at a nonoptimal point unless violated multiplier tests force constraint release.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Face Residual Without Fair Constraint Release
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Face Residual Without Fair Constraint Release

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_*\ \text{satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and belongs to }\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x).

notation.meaning: approximate multipliers on the stabilized working face

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit certificate for inexact solves after the working face has stabilized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx:x\in P\}\), where \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\) and \(Q\succeq0\). Let feasible iterates satisfy \(x_k\to x_*\), and suppose that for all sufficiently large \(k\), \(W_k=W\subseteq\mathcal A(x_*)\). If multipliers \(\lambda_{k,W}\) satisfy \[\|\nabla f(x_k)-A_W^T\lambda_{k,W}\|\to0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\lambda_{k,W},\mathbb R_+^{|W|})\to0,\] and possess a convergent subsequence, then \(x_*\) satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After the working face stabilizes, vanishing stationarity error and asymptotic multiplier nonnegativity make the iterate limit KKT and globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Convergence After Working-Face Stabilization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Accumulation under Varying Working Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit-certificate theorem allowing infinitely many working-face changes; it is not an algorithm-specific convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx:x\in P\}\), where \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\), \(Q\succeq0\), and \(x_k\in P\) is bounded. Let \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\), and extend each working multiplier \(\lambda_k\) by zero outside \(W_k\). If \[\|\nabla f(x_k)-A^T\lambda_k\|\to0,\qquad \|[\lambda_k]_-\|\to0,\qquad \sup_k\|\lambda_k\|<\infty,\] then every accumulation point of \(\{x_k\}\) satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions. If the minimizer is unique, the bounded sequence converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded approximate multipliers with vanishing stationarity and sign residuals yield KKT accumulation points even if working faces change infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{acc}(x_k)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x);\qquad |\operatorname*{argmin}_{P}f|=1\Longrightarrow x_k\to x_* .

notation.meaning: Componentwise negative part of a multiplier vector.
Set of accumulation points of the iterate sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Accumulation under Varying Working Faces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-free limit certificate for varying working faces in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(Q\succeq0\). Suppose \(x_k\in P\) is bounded, \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\), and \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\nabla f(x_k),\operatorname{cone}\{A_i^{\mathsf T}:i\in W_k\}\right)\to0.\] Then every accumulation point of \(x_k\) satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal. If the minimizer is unique, then \(x_k\) converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing distance from the gradient to the selected active-normal cone yields optimal accumulation points without requiring a bounded chosen multiplier sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{acc}(x_k)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x);\quad |\operatorname*{argmin}_{P}f|=1\Longrightarrow x_k\to x_*

notation.meaning: Set of inequalities active at x.
Conic hull of the selected active normals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Face-Solve Error Can Produce a Non-KKT Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of driving working-face stationarity errors to zero, even without face changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the unconstrained convex QP \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\tfrac12x^2\). For any fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the constant sequence \(x_k=\varepsilon\) is bounded and has zero step lengths and constant objective values, but its stationarity residual is \(|\nabla f(x_k)|=\varepsilon\). Its unique accumulation point \(\varepsilon\) is not optimal. Thus boundedness and nonincrease alone do not yield KKT accumulation when the face-solve error is bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded nonincreasing sequence may remain at a nonstationary point if the working-face solve tolerance does not vanish.

|

otin\operatorname*{argmin}f.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Face-Solve Error Can Produce a Non-KKT Limit

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full KKT Residual on an Inexact Working Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stopping certificate distinguishing working-face stationarity from global convex-QP stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\), let \(x\in P\), \(W\subseteq\mathcal A(x)\), and extend \(\lambda_W\) by zero outside \(W\). Define \[r_{\mathrm{stat}}=\|\nabla f(x)-A_W^{\mathsf T}\lambda_W\|,\qquad r_{\mathrm{sign}}=\|[\lambda_W]_-\|.\] Then \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}=r_{\mathrm{sign}}=0\) if and only if \(x\) and the extended multiplier satisfy the KKT conditions. Thus vanishing reduced-gradient error alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point on a selected working face is globally KKT exactly when full stationarity and multiplier-sign residuals both vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\mathrm{stat}}=r_{\mathrm{sign}}=0\iff x\text{ and the extended multiplier satisfy the convex-QP KKT conditions}.

notation.meaning: Set of inequalities active at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Full KKT Residual on an Inexact Working Face

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\ge b\}\) is nonempty, and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) has \(Q\succeq0\).
Accepted feasible iterates satisfy \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\sigma\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) for some \(\sigma>0\).
Face-solve errors satisfy \(\|Z_k^T\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|\le\eta_k\), with \(\eta_k\to0\), and persistently violated multiplier tests are eventually acted upon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \(x_*\) satisfies the KKT conditions for the convex quadratic program; if \(Q\succ0\), the entire bounded sequence converges to its unique minimizer.

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns span the null space of the current working-face matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-QP convergence under vanishing face-solve errors and fair working-set updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{x_k\}\subset P\) be bounded. Suppose each accepted working-face step has sufficient decrease, its reduced-gradient residual obeys \(\|Z_k^T\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|\le\eta_k\) with \(\eta_k\to0\), and the update rule eventually removes any active constraint whose estimated KKT multiplier remains below a fixed negative threshold. Then every accumulation point \(x_*\) admits \(\lambda_*\ge0\) such that \[Qx_*+c-A^T\lambda_*=0,\qquad Ax_*-b\ge0,\qquad \lambda_*^T(Ax_*-b)=0.\] Hence every accumulation point is globally optimal. When \(Q\succ0\), the optimizer is unique, so boundedness implies \(x_k\to x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing reduced-gradient errors, sufficient decrease, and fair release of persistently wrong active constraints make every accumulation point KKT; strict convexity gives full-sequence convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Working-Face Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits, but sufficient decrease, vanishing face residuals, and release only below a fixed negative threshold do not plainly ensure KKT accumulation points when faces change. An algorithm-specific convergence theorem and its full hypotheses are required.

children.title: Active-Set Worst-Case Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial face counts and the limits of interpreting finite termination as a polynomial guarantee.

assumptions_latex: A quadratic program in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is described by \(m\) inequalities.
An active-set method changes subsets of constraints and does not revisit a working set under its finite-termination assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination based only on nonrepetition permits up to \(\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{m,n\}}\binom{m}{j}\) working sets, which is not a polynomial iteration bound in the joint input dimensions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial limitation of deriving complexity solely from finite face enumeration.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linearly independent working set contains at most \(n\) of the \(m\) inequalities. Consequently the number of combinatorially possible working sets is bounded by \[N(m,n)=\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{m,n\}}\binom{m}{j}.\] An argument proving that every iteration visits a new working set therefore yields at best \(N(m,n)\) iterations. For \(m=2n\), the term \(\binom{2n}{n}\) already grows exponentially in \(n\). Thus noncycling and finite termination do not, without an additional progress or structural argument, establish a polynomial worst-case bound in \(m+n\) or in the encoded input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrevisiting active-set method may still examine exponentially many constraint subsets, so finite termination alone is not a polynomial-time guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Worst-Case Complexity Boundary

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

children.title: Sparse Reduced-Gradient Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Sparse working-face families based on reduced-gradient organization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-form equivalence between a vanishing reduced gradient and stationarity on the current working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_W=[B\ N]\), with \(B\) nonsingular, let \(g=(g_B,g_N)\), and define \(Z=\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\I\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(A_WZ=0\) and \[Z^Tg=g_N-N^TB^{-T}g_B=r.\] Since the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A_W\), \(r=0\) if and only if \(g^Td=0\) for every \(d\in\ker A_W\), equivalently \(g\in\operatorname{range}(A_W^T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basis-form reduced gradient vanishes exactly when the objective is stationary along every direction tangent to the working face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r=0\iff g\perp\ker A_W\iff g\in\operatorname{range}(A_W^T).

notation.meaning: fundamental null-space basis induced by B

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Gradient Face-Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and numerical conditions for the basis-form reduced-gradient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formulas \(d_B=-B^{-1}Nd_N\) and \(r=g_N-N^TB^{-T}g_B\) require a nonsingular basis block \(B\). If \(B\) is singular, they do not define a fundamental null-space basis. If \(B\) is nonsingular but ill-conditioned, sparse triangular-solve errors can be strongly amplified, motivating rank-revealing basis exchange or an orthogonal null-space representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular basis block invalidates the fundamental reduced-gradient formulas, while an ill-conditioned block makes them numerically unreliable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \det B=0\Longrightarrow\text{the fundamental-basis formulas are undefined}.

notation.meaning: condition number of the selected basis block

knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental-Basis Validity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic update of the fundamental null-space representation after an admissible variable-basis exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_W=[B\ N]\) with \(B\) nonsingular. After exchanging dependent and independent columns, write the permuted partition as \(A_W=[B^+\ N^+]\). The exchange is admissible exactly when \(B^+\) is nonsingular. In the corresponding coordinate ordering, \(Z^+=\begin{bmatrix}-(B^+)^{-1}N^+\\I\end{bmatrix}\) spans \(\ker A_W\), and \(r^+=g_{N^+}-(N^+)^T(B^+)^{-T}g_{B^+}\). A sparse implementation must reject or refactor an exchange that fails its rank or stability test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After an admissible dependent-independent variable exchange, recompute the fundamental null-space basis and reduced gradient in the new coordinate partition.
assumptions_latex: A_W=[B^+\ N^+]\text{ is the partition after a column exchange}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}(Z^+)=\ker A_W,\qquad r^+=g_{N^+}-(N^+)^T(B^+)^{-T}g_{B^+}.

notation.meaning: Fundamental null-space basis in the new coordinate ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental-Basis Exchange Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental-basis active-set iteration with blocker admission, multiplier release, and refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At feasible \(x_k\), choose a rank-revealing column permutation of the independent working-row matrix \(A_{W_k}\), obtaining \([B_k\ N_k]\) with nonsingular \(B_k\). With \(g_k=Qx_k+c\), form \(r_k=g_{N_k}-N_k^TB_k^{-T}g_{B_k}\), choose \(d_{N_k}=-D_kr_k\) with \(D_k\succ0\), and recover \(d_{B_k}=-B_k^{-1}N_kd_{N_k}\). If \(r_k\ne0\), take the smaller of a prescribed descent trial step and the first inactive blocking ratio; select tied admissible blockers by increasing index, then refactor and retest rank. If \(r_k=0\), determine whether any working multiplier vector is nonnegative. Terminate if one exists; otherwise use a specified multiplier solution, delete its smallest-index negative component, and refactor. Reject a proposed basis exchange that fails the stated rank or stability test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a rank-revealing sparse basis for reduced-gradient steps, deterministic blocker admission and multiplier release, and refactor after every structural change.
assumptions_latex: A_{W_k}\text{ is maintained as an independent working-row representation}
B_k\text{ passes the prescribed rank and stability test}
\text{the mathematical sparse solves and blocking ratios are exact}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_{W_k}d_k=0,\qquad g_k^Td_k=-r_k^TD_kr_k<0\ \text{when }r_k\ne0;\qquad \text{accepted iterates remain feasible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Sparse Reduced-Gradient Outer Iteration

assumptions_latex: The current face is \(A_Wx=b_W\), and a full-row-rank basis partition satisfies \(A_W=[B\ N]\) with nonsingular \(B\).
The quadratic objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\), and the current iterate is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed direction is tangent to the working face, since \(A_Wd=0\), and its directional derivative is \(\nabla f(x)^Td=r^Td_N\).

notation.meaning: reduced gradient in the independent variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-form reduced-gradient iteration for a sparse equality working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(g=Qx+c\) and compute the reduced gradient \(r=g_N-N^TB^{-T}g_B\) using sparse triangular solves. Choose an independent-variable direction \(d_N\) with \(r^Td_N<0\), for example \(d_N=-D r\) with \(D\succ0\), and recover \(d_B=-B^{-1}Nd_N\). Let \(\alpha\) be the largest nonnegative step not exceeding a chosen trial step and preserving every inactive inequality. Update \(x\leftarrow x+\alpha d\); if an inactive constraint blocks the step, add one blocker to \(W\). When \(r=0\), test active multipliers, remove a violating constraint if one exists, and otherwise return \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use sparse basis solves to form a reduced gradient, move tangentially in independent variables, add blockers, and release active constraints with invalid multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Reduced-Gradient Active-Set Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and the reduced-gradient identity is standard, but the coordinate partitions defining g_B, g_N, d_B, and d_N are not introduced explicitly. A sparse active-set or reduced-gradient source is also required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-sign completion of face stationarity for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\ge h\), with \(Q\succeq0\). Let \(x\) be feasible, let \(W\) contain only inequalities tight at \(x\), and suppose the reduced gradient on \(\ker[A;G_W]\) vanishes. Then multipliers \((\lambda,\mu_W)\) exist with \(\nabla f(x)-A^T\lambda-G_W^T\mu_W=0\). If one such multiplier satisfies \(\mu_W\ge0\), extending it by zeros outside \(W\) gives a global KKT certificate. A negative component in a computed working multiplier rejects that particular certificate but, when multipliers are nonunique, does not by itself prove that no nonnegative certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Face stationarity plus a nonnegative working multiplier certifies global optimality; a negative computed multiplier rejects only that multiplier certificate when multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(\lambda,\mu_W\ge0)\text{ satisfying stationarity}\Longrightarrow x\text{ is globally optimal}.

notation.meaning: multipliers of the working inequalities under the stated sign convention

children.title: Projected Iterative Subproblem Solves
children.top_down_role: Large-scale working-face solution through projected iterative methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov Restart after a Working-Face Change
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for projected Krylov recurrences after adding or deleting a working constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_W=\ker A_W\). If the working set changes to \(W^+\) with \(T_{W^+}\ne T_W\), directions generated in \(T_W\) need not lie in \(T_{W^+}\), and their conjugacy relations need not hold for the new projected operator. Continuation therefore requires recomputing the projector and residual and restarting, or rebuilding a reprojected and reorthogonalized basis in \(T_{W^+}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the working face changes the projected operator, so projected CG must restart or rebuild a feasible conjugate basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The old projected-CG recurrence is not generally valid on }T_{W^+}.

notation.meaning: tangent null space for working set W
working set after a constraint exchange

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Restart after a Working-Face Change

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate convergence on a fixed face with positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\ker A_W\) have dimension \(r\), and suppose \(m\|v\|^2\le v^TQv\le L\|v\|^2\) for all \(v\in T\), where \(0<m\le L\). If the working face remains fixed and no inactive constraint truncates an iteration, exact-arithmetic projected CG reaches the unique face minimizer in at most \(r\) iterations. With \(\kappa=L/m\), \[\|e_k\|_Q\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_Q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed unblocked face with positive-definite reduced curvature, projected CG has the standard finite-termination and condition-number bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact termination occurs in at most }r\text{ iterations, with the stated energy-norm bound.}

notation.meaning: dimension of the working-face tangent space
spectral condition number of the reduced Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Blocker-Free Projected-CG Termination and Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-curvature handling for a projected CG direction on a convex working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\ker A_W\), let \(P_T\) be its orthogonal projector, and suppose \(Q|_T\succeq0\). If \(0\ne p\in T\) and \(p^TQp=0\), then \(P_TQp=0\). If additionally \(g^Tp<0\), the face objective decreases linearly along \(p\); the ordinary CG quotient \(-g^Tp/(p^TQp)\) is undefined, so a finite blocking step must be taken or an unbounded feasible face ray reported. If \(g^Tp=0\), the direction gives no decrease and singular-system handling is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero reduced curvature invalidates the ordinary CG quotient and requires boundary, unbounded-ray, or singular-system handling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_TQp=0\quad\text{and the positive-definite CG recurrence is not applicable.}

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the tangent space

review_flags: corrected_builder_claim: Qp=0 was too strong; only the tangent projection P_TQp is forced to vanish
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Projected-CG Breakdown Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected CG on a working face with blocker, residual, restart, and zero-curvature exits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\ker A_W\) and let \(P_T\) be its orthogonal projector. From feasible \(z_0\), set \(r_0=P_T(Qz_0+c)\); return \(\mathrm{RESIDUAL}\) if \(\|r_0\|\le\eta\), otherwise set \(p_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(j\), compute \(\delta_j=p_j^TQp_j\). If \(\delta_j>0\), set \(\alpha_j^{\rm cg}=r_j^Tr_j/\delta_j\), compute the first inactive blocker \(\alpha_j^{\rm blk}\), and update by the smaller step. Return \(\mathrm{BLOCKER}\) when the blocker is attained; otherwise form \(r_{j+1}=P_T(Qz_{j+1}+c)\), test its norm before any further division, and set \(p_{j+1}=-r_{j+1}+(r_{j+1}^Tr_{j+1}/r_j^Tr_j)p_j\). If \(\delta_j=0\), take a finite blocking step and return \(\mathrm{BLOCKER\_ZERO\_CURVATURE}\), or return \(\mathrm{UNBOUNDED\_RAY}\) when the descent ray is unblocked. A zero-curvature direction with zero slope returns \(\mathrm{SINGULAR\_NO\_DECREASE}\). After any working-set change, recompute the projector, residual, and initial direction and restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected CG stays on the face, truncates at blockers, tests convergence before divisions, handles zero curvature explicitly, and restarts after a face change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every point-valued return is feasible and carries a residual, blocker, or singular flag; an unblocked zero-curvature descent ray is reported as unbounded}.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite-Safe Blocker-Aware Projected CG

assumptions_latex: The current feasible iterate satisfies \(A_Wx=b_W\), where \(A_W\) has full row rank.
The face-restricted quadratic is convex, and matrix-vector products with \(Q\), \(A_W\), and \(A_W^T\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated search direction lies in \(\ker A_W\); the returned point is feasible after truncation at the first inactive blocking constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z_0=x\), \(r_0=P_W(Qz_0+c)\), and \(p_0=-r_0\). Apply conjugate-gradient recurrences to the projected system on \(\ker A_W\), projecting residuals when necessary. At each inner iteration, compute the unconstrained CG step \(\alpha_j\) and the first inactive-constraint blocking step \(\alpha_j^{\mathrm{blk}}\). Set \(z_{j+1}=z_j+\min\{\alpha_j,\alpha_j^{\mathrm{blk}}\}p_j\). Return immediately at a blocker; otherwise stop when \(\|P_W(Qz_{j+1}+c)\|\le\eta\), and return \(z_{j+1}\) with the blocker or residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run projected conjugate gradients in the face tangent space, truncating at an inactive blocker or stopping when the projected-gradient residual meets tolerance.

children.title: Partial Face Minimization
children.top_down_role: Face-restricted progress obtained without fully minimizing the local quadratic model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Face Minimizer as an Energy Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of partial minimization for a strictly convex quadratic on a fixed face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(d)=q(0)+g^Td+\tfrac12d^THd\) on a tangent space \(T\), with \(H\) positive definite on \(T\), and let \(S\subseteq T\) be a linear subspace. If \(d_T\) and \(d_S\) minimize \(q\) over \(T\) and \(S\), respectively, then \[d_S=\Pi_S^Hd_T,\qquad q(d_S)-q(d_T)=\tfrac12\|d_S-d_T\|_H^2.\] Thus partial and full face minimization agree exactly when \(d_T\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partial minimizer is the Hessian-orthogonal projection of the full face step, and the missed decrease is its squared energy distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_S=\Pi_S^Hd_T\quad\text{and}\quad q(d_S)-q(d_T)=\tfrac12\|d_S-d_T\|_H^2.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto S in the H inner product

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Face Minimizer as an Energy Projection

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}\phi\ne\varnothing\iff g_S\in\operatorname{range}(H_S),\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}\phi=-H_S^\dagger g_S+\ker H_S.

notation.meaning: basis of the selected tangent subspace
Hessian restricted to the selected subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite solvability boundary for the unconstrained quadratic model on a selected working-face tangent subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) span the selected subspace and write \(\phi(z)=\phi(0)+g_S^Tz+\tfrac12z^TH_Sz\), where \(H_S=U^THU\succeq0\) and \(g_S=U^T\nabla f(x)\). A finite minimizer exists exactly when \(g_S\in\operatorname{range}(H_S)\). In that case every minimizer has the form \[z_*=-H_S^\dagger g_S+v,\qquad v\in\ker H_S,\] and all minimizers have the same objective value. If \(g_S\notin\operatorname{range}(H_S)\), then the unconstrained selected-subspace model is unbounded below along a vector in \(\ker H_S\); inactive inequalities may instead block and truncate that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semidefinite selected-subspace model is solvable exactly when its linear term lies in the reduced-Hessian range; otherwise a null direction is unbounded unless an inactive inequality blocks it.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Partial-Minimization Solvability and Nonuniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization over a selected proper subspace of the current working-face tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At feasible \(x\) with working equalities \(A_Wx=b_W\), select a nonzero block basis \(U\) with \(A_WU=0\) and \(\operatorname{range}(U)\subsetneq\ker A_W\). Compute \[z_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x+Uz):G_i(x+Uz)\le h_i\ \forall i\notin W\},\qquad x^+=x+Uz_* .\] Return as blockers the inactive rows having positive slack at \(x\) and zero slack at \(x^+\). Outer termination uses the full working-face stationarity and multiplier tests, not stationarity only in \(\operatorname{range}(U)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize over a selected proper tangent subspace subject to all inactive inequalities, return newly encountered blockers, and retain an external full-face termination test.
assumptions_latex: \text{the restricted problem has a finite attained minimum}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_Wx^+=b_W,\qquad Gx^+\le h,\qquad f(x^+)\le f(x).

notation.meaning: Basis for the selected proper tangent subspace.

assumptions_latex: The current point \(x\) lies on the working face \(F_W=\{y:Ay\ge b,\ A_Wy=b_W\}\).
A nonzero subspace \(S\subseteq\ker A_W\) is selected, and the quadratic is bounded below on \((x+S)\cap F_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output remains in \(F_W\) and has objective value no larger than \(f(x)\); equality holds only when the chosen subspace offers no improving feasible displacement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization over only a selected subspace of the current face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a basis \(U\) for \(S\) and solve the lower-dimensional problem \[z_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z:\,x+Uz\in F_W} f(x+Uz).\] Set \(x^+=x+Uz_*\). If the solution reaches a previously inactive inequality, return that constraint as a blocker; otherwise retain \(W\). This is partial rather than full face minimization because \(S\) may be a proper subspace of \(\ker A_W\). The step is accepted only when \(f(x^+)\le f(x)\), and termination of the outer active-set method still uses the full projected-gradient and multiplier tests, not stationarity restricted to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize exactly over a chosen tangent subspace, preserve feasibility, report any blocker, and retain full-face stationarity tests for outer termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Face Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits partial face minimization, and the subspace problem preserves the face. A source is required for its role within an inexact active-set method and the associated blocker and termination rules.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Face Stationarity Test After a Partial Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed generic face-stationarity test after selected-subspace minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a partial solve returns \(x^+\in F_W\), compute the residual on the entire working-face tangent space \(T_W\), not only on the selected subspace \(S\). The equality \(P_{T_W}\nabla f(x^+)=0\) is equivalent to \(\nabla f(x^+)^Td=0\) for every \(d\in T_W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-face stationarity requires the gradient to vanish on the entire face tangent space, not merely on the selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{T_W}\nabla f(x^+)=0\iff \nabla f(x^+)^Td=0\ \forall d\in T_W.

children.title: Truncated Face Minimization
children.top_down_role: Face solves terminated by resource, curvature, or progress criteria.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective behavior when a positive-curvature face step is shortened at a blocking constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(\alpha)=f(z+\alpha p)\), suppose \(g^Tp<0\) and \(p^TQp>0\), where \(g=\nabla f(z)\). Let \(\alpha_*=-g^Tp/(p^TQp)\). Every \(0<\alpha\le\alpha_*\) satisfies \[f(z+\alpha p)-f(z)=\alpha g^Tp+\tfrac12\alpha^2p^TQp<0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortening a positive-curvature descent step to a positive length no greater than its line minimizer preserves strict decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(z+\alpha p)<f(z).
knowledge_statements.title: Descent Preservation under Step Truncation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical strength of residual, blocker, curvature, and resource-limit return flags.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible working-face iterate \(z\), a residual flag satisfying \(\|P_W\nabla f(z)\|\le\eta\) certifies only \(\eta\)-stationarity on the current face. A blocker flag certifies feasibility of the returned truncated step and tightness of at least one newly encountered inequality. A curvature flag certifies a face-tangent direction \(p\) satisfying the algorithm's stated curvature test. A work-limit flag alone certifies none of these assertions and does not imply QP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation flags have distinct, limited meanings; exhausting the work budget is not a stationarity or optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: z\text{ is feasible on the working face}
P_W\text{ is the orthogonal projector onto }\ker A_W
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A work-limit flag alone implies neither face stationarity nor QP optimality.}

notation.meaning: projector onto the working-face tangent space

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation-Flag Certification Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of interpreting an arbitrary inner-iteration cutoff as an accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(t)=\tfrac12t^2\) on the unconstrained face \(\mathbb R\), start at \(t_0=1\), and terminate before an inner update because the work limit is zero. The returned point is feasible but \(\nabla f(t_0)=1\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource cutoff can return a feasible point with a nonzero face gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla f(t_0)\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limit Nonstationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary or unbounded-ray handling when the face line model lacks a finite minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(\alpha)=f(z+\alpha p)\), suppose \(g^Tp<0\) and \(p^TQp\le0\). If \(p^TQp=0\), \(\phi\) decreases linearly for \(\alpha>0\); if \(p^TQp<0\), it decreases strictly and concavely. No positive finite unconstrained line minimizer exists. A finite blocking inequality determines a boundary step; if the entire ray remains feasible, the face problem is unbounded below along that ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a descent slope and nonpositive curvature, the step must reach a boundary or certify an unbounded feasible ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{There is no positive finite unconstrained line minimizer along }p.

notation.meaning: gradient at the current face iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpositive-Curvature Truncation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-complete first-event driver for iterative minimization on a fixed working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from feasible \(z_0\), generate \(p_j\in\ker A_W\) with \(\sigma_j=\nabla f(z_j)^Tp_j\le0\). First return \((z_j,\mathrm{RESIDUAL})\) if \(\|P_W\nabla f(z_j)\|\le\eta\). Otherwise set \(\delta_j=p_j^TQp_j\) and compute the maximal inactive-feasible step \(\alpha_j^{\rm blk}\). If \(\delta_j>0\) and \(\sigma_j<0\), let \(\alpha_j^*=-\sigma_j/\delta_j\), take \(\min\{\alpha_j^*,\alpha_j^{\rm blk}\}\), and return \(\mathrm{BLOCKER\_POSITIVE\_CURVATURE}\) when the blocker is attained. If \(\delta_j=0\) and \(\sigma_j<0\), or if \(\delta_j<0\) and \(\sigma_j\le0\), take a finite blocking step with the corresponding zero- or negative-curvature blocker flag; if no blocker exists, return the corresponding unbounded-ray flag. If \(\sigma_j=0\) and \(\delta_j\ge0\), return \(\mathrm{NO\_DECREASE}\). After a nonblocking positive-curvature update, return \(\mathrm{WORK\_LIMIT}\) only when the prescribed budget is exhausted; otherwise continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver tests residuals first and gives distinct feasible-return or unbounded-ray flags for every slope, curvature, blocker, and work-limit branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every point-valued return is feasible, and each exit has one branch-specific flag}.

children.title: Early-Exit Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Outer-solver consequences of limited accuracy in face-restricted subproblems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Face Residual Accuracy Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based accuracy for a strongly convex quadratic restricted to a fixed working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(z)=\tfrac12z^TH_Fz+b^Tz+\gamma\), where \(H_F\succeq\mu I\) and \(\mu>0\), and let \(z_*\) minimize \(q\). If \(\|\nabla q(z)\|\le\eta\), then \[\|z-z_*\|\le\frac{\eta}{\mu},\qquad 0\le q(z)-q(z_*)\le\frac{\eta^2}{2\mu}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a strongly convex working face, a reduced-gradient tolerance bounds distance to the face minimizer and face-objective error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z-z_*\|\le\eta/\mu\quad\text{and}\quad q(z)-q(z_*)\le\eta^2/(2\mu).
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Face Residual Accuracy Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner face-solve stopping regimes without an algorithm-independent outer convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_{k+1}=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_{k+1})\) and require \(\|r_{k+1}\|\le\eta_k\). The standard forcing regimes are \[(A)\ \eta_k\to0;\qquad (S)\ \eta_k\ge0,\ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty;\qquad (R)\ 0\le\eta_k\le\theta_kR_k,\ 0\le\theta_k\le\bar\theta<1,\ R_k\to0.\] Each regime implies \(\|r_{k+1}\|\to0\). None alone certifies feasibility, descent, correct working-set status, or outer convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing, summable, and relative tolerances force the face residual to zero when the relative regime explicitly assumes that its outer residual vanishes.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(q_\varepsilon(z)=\tfrac12\varepsilon z^2\), whose minimizer is \(z_*=0\). At \(z=1\), \[\|\nabla q_\varepsilon(1)\|=\varepsilon\to0,\qquad |1-z_*|=1.\] Thus a small absolute reduced residual gives no uniform distance-to-minimizer bound over faces whose smallest positive reduced eigenvalue can approach zero.

children.title: Working-Set Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated sequences of working faces without durable algorithmic progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A degenerate cycle of a deterministic primal-simplex active-set rule, viewed as a convex QP with zero Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP (linear program) \[\max\ 10x_1-57x_2-9x_3-24x_4\] subject to \[\tfrac12x_1-\tfrac{11}{2}x_2-\tfrac52x_3+9x_4\le0,\quad \tfrac12x_1-\tfrac32x_2-\tfrac12x_3+x_4\le0,\quad x_1\le1,\quad x\ge0.\] Introduce slacks \(x_5,x_6,x_7\), start with \(B_0=(x_5,x_6,x_7)\), choose an entering variable by Dantzig's largest-positive-reduced-cost rule, and break minimum-ratio ties by choosing the eligible basic variable with smallest index. Apply the ordinary reduced-cost stopping test after every pivot. In exact arithmetic the degenerate pivots give \[(x_5,x_6,x_7)\to(x_1,x_6,x_7)\to(x_1,x_2,x_7)\to(x_2,x_3,x_7)\to(x_3,x_4,x_7)\to(x_4,x_5,x_7)\to(x_5,x_6,x_7).\] Each displayed basis is nonterminal, while the basic feasible point and objective remain unchanged, so the deterministic six-basis orbit repeats.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Beale's degenerate linear program, a zero-Hessian convex QP, cycles through six nonterminal simplex bases under Dantzig entering and smallest-index minimum-ratio tie breaking.
assumptions_latex: \text{Dantzig entering and smallest-index minimum-ratio tie breaking are used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_6=B_0\quad\text{and the nonterminal six-pivot orbit repeats in exact arithmetic}.

notation.meaning: Slack variables for the three displayed inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact definition of cycling for a deterministic active-set algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic active-set method exhibits working-set cycling when its complete successor-determining states satisfy \(s_{k+1}=T(s_k)\) and there exist \(k\ge0\) and \(p\ge1\) such that \(s_{k+p}=s_k\), while none of \(s_k,\ldots,s_{k+p-1}\) satisfies the stopping test. Determinism makes the subsequent orbit periodic, so finite termination fails. Repetition of a working set alone is not cycling when another successor-determining component differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Working-set cycling is positive-period repetition of a complete deterministic nonterminal state, not merely reuse of the same constraint set.
assumptions_latex: s_k\text{ is a complete successor-determining state}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k\ge0,\ p\ge1:\ s_{k+p}=s_k\text{ with a nonterminal period}\Longrightarrow\text{finite termination fails}.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-State Definition of Working-Set Cycling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-state cycling caused by degenerate working-set transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Working-set cycling occurs when there exist integers \(k\ge0\) and \(p\ge1\) such that \[s_{k+p}=s_k,\qquad s_{k+j+1}=T(s_{k+j})\quad(0\le j<p),\] while no state in the period satisfies the termination test. Determinism then gives \(s_{k+ell p}=s_k\) for every integer \(\ell\ge1\). A typical mechanism is degeneracy: several constraints are simultaneously active, each pivot has zero primal step or zero dual change, and inconsistent tie choices successively add and remove constraints without changing the iterate or objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling is periodic repetition of a nonterminal iterate and working set; degeneracy can drive zero-progress additions and removals around such a cycle.

children.title: Transition Stalling
children.top_down_role: Ineffective or negligible working-set transitions near difficult faces.

assumptions_latex: The active-set method generates feasible iterates \(x_k\), working sets \(W_k\), steps \(d_k\), and feasible step lengths \(\alpha_k\).
A working-set transition is executed whenever the current optimality test fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An infinite subsequence with vanishing steps and nonvanishing stationarity measure is a progress failure, even if the working sets do not form an exact cycle.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstationary working-set changes whose accepted movement and objective progress vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transition stalling is present if some infinite index set \(K\) and constant \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \[\alpha_k\|d_k\|\to0,\qquad |f(x_{k+1})-f(x_k)|\to0,\qquad R(x_k,W_k)\ge\varepsilon\quad(k\in K).\] The working sets may continue changing, so exact periodicity is not required. Zero-length degenerate pivots are the sharp case \(\alpha_k=0\). Because the KKT residual stays bounded away from zero, neither small steps nor a nearly constant objective justify termination; the method requires a tie-breaking, constraint-release, regularization, or accuracy safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stalling means working-set transitions continue while steps and objective changes vanish but a KKT residual remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition Stalling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but R(x,W) is not formally defined as a nonnegative scalar residual, and the proposed subsequence criterion is algorithm-specific and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Repeated-Face Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable patterns used to distinguish cycling from slow legitimate progress.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{warning}_{j,k}=1\ \text{does not by itself imply a mathematical cycle}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point repeated-face warning that does not claim a mathematical cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_f\ge0\). For \(j<k\), raise a repeated-face warning when \[W_j=W_k,\qquad \|x_j-x_k\|\le\varepsilon_x,\qquad |f(x_j)-f(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_f.\] The warning may trigger state logging or an anti-cycling safeguard, but it is not a cycle certificate unless the compared data form an exactly equal complete deterministic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near repetition of a face, iterate, and objective is a floating-point warning, not a proof of cycling.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Level Repeated-Face Warning

assumptions_latex: T\text{ is deterministic on the complete state}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma(s_0)=\sigma(s_1)\ \not\Rightarrow\ \sigma(T(s_0))=\sigma(T(s_1)).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of cycle certification when hidden deterministic state is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the complete state be \(s=(x,W,h)\), where \(h\in\{0,1\}\), and define the deterministic transition \[T(0,\varnothing,0)=(0,\varnothing,1),\qquad T(0,\varnothing,1)=(1,\varnothing,1).\] The visible signature \(\sigma(s)=(x,W)\) repeats at the first transition, yet the next visible states differ. Thus equality of \((x,W)\) does not certify a cycle when omitted state affects the transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same iterate and working set can occur with different hidden state and different successors, so an incomplete repeated signature is only a warning.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Signatures Can Falsely Indicate Cycling
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Signatures Can Falsely Indicate Cycling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cycle certificate from repetition of a complete deterministic nonterminal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_{k+1}=T(s_k)\), where \(s_k\) contains every variable, tie-breaking datum, and solver state determining the next update and \(T\) is deterministic. If \(s_j=s_k\) for \(0\le j<k\) and none of \(s_j,\ldots,s_{k-1}\) is terminal, then \(s_{j+\ell+(k-j)}=s_{j+\ell}\) for every \(\ell\ge0\). Thus the match certifies a nonterminal periodic orbit. Equality of an incomplete or tolerance-level signature does not provide this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact repetition of a complete nonterminal state under a deterministic update certifies a periodic orbit; incomplete or approximate repetition does not.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is deterministic on the complete successor-determining state space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_{j+\ell+(k-j)}=s_{j+\ell}\quad\forall\ell\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Complete-State Repetition Certificate

assumptions_latex: The implementation records deterministic state signatures \(\Sigma_k=(W_k,x_k,f(x_k),\tau_k)\), including all data that influence the next update.
Exact equality is used in exact arithmetic; numerical comparisons use declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exactly repeated complete signature certifies cycling for a deterministic update rule; a tolerance-level repetition is only a diagnostic trigger.

notation.meaning: all tie-breaking and solver state affecting the next transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-signature test distinguishing certified cycles from numerical repeated-face warnings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store \(\Sigma_k=(W_k,x_k,f(x_k),\tau_k)\) in a visited-state table. If \(\Sigma_j=\Sigma_k\) for some \(j<k\) and the update is deterministic, then the transitions from \(j\) and \(k\) coincide; if neither state is terminal, \(k-j\) is a certified cycle period. In floating-point arithmetic, flag a repeated-face warning when \[W_j=W_k,\qquad \|x_j-x_k\|\le\varepsilon_x,\qquad |f(x_j)-f(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_f.\] Because omitted solver state or tolerance-level equality can change the next transition, this warning triggers logging or an anti-cycling safeguard but does not by itself certify a mathematical cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hash complete states to certify exact deterministic cycles; use tolerant repeats of working set, iterate, and objective only as numerical warnings.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Face Diagnostics

children.title: Numerical Face Misclassification
children.top_down_role: Incorrect activity decisions near tolerances or under poor scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual activity indicators invariant under positive rescaling of a nonzero inequality row; the normalization does not eliminate general roundoff or conditioning errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero inequality row \(G_i x\le h_i\), let \(s_i=h_i-G_ix\), \(\rho_i=s_i/\|G_i\|_2\), and, when \(\lambda_i\ge0\) is available, \(\eta_i=\lambda_i\|G_i\|_2\). Under \((G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\alpha G_i,\alpha h_i)\) with \(\alpha>0\), the compatible multiplier is \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\), so \(\widetilde\rho_i=\rho_i\) and \(\widetilde\eta_i=\eta_i\). In contrast, the raw quantities become \(\widetilde s_i=\alpha s_i\) and \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\); consequently any fixed positive raw-slack or raw-multiplier threshold can change its classification under an equivalent row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row-normalized slack and multiplier indicators are invariant under positive constraint scaling, whereas fixed thresholds on raw slacks or multipliers can classify an equivalent row differently.
assumptions_latex: The rescaled multiplier is transformed compatibly as \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde\rho_i=\rho_i\), \(\widetilde\eta_i=\eta_i\), while raw-threshold classifications need not be invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Scaling-Invariant Activity Indicators
Numerical Face Misclassification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of absolute activity tolerances under equivalent constraint rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the inequality representation \(g_i(x)=G_i x-h_i\le 0\), with slack \(s_i(x)=-g_i(x)\). An absolute rule declares constraint \(i\) active when \(s_i(x)\le\tau\), where \(\tau>0\). Replacing the inequality by the equivalent constraint \(\alpha g_i(x)\le0\), with \(\alpha>0\), changes its computed slack to \(\widetilde s_i(x)=\alpha s_i(x)\). For every point satisfying \(0<s_i(x)<\infty\), choosing \(\alpha\le\tau/s_i(x)\) makes the rule declare the constraint active, whereas choosing \(\alpha>\tau/s_i(x)\) makes it inactive. Thus absolute slack tests do not define a representation-invariant numerical face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute slack tolerance can classify the same geometric constraint as active or inactive after harmless positive rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau>0\) is an absolute, unscaled activity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i(x)\le\tau\) is not invariant under the equivalent replacement \(g_i\mapsto\alpha g_i\).

notation.meaning: slack of inequality i at x

Poor Initial-Face Prediction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange lower bound for single-index working-set updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_0\) be the initially predicted working set and \(W_*\) the working set that an active-set QP method must attain before termination. Suppose each iteration adds or removes at most one constraint. With \(d=|W_0\triangle W_*|\), every sequence \(W_0,W_1,\ldots,W_k=W_*\) satisfying \(|W_{j+1}\triangle W_j|\le1\) has \(k\ge d\). Consequently, even when every exchange is correct and no constraint is revisited, an initial-face error of symmetric-difference size \(d\) requires at least \(d\) working-set changes; cycling or mistaken exchanges can only increase this count.

children.title: Indefinite-QP Active-Set Boundary
children.top_down_role: The boundary between convex-QP guarantees and local methods requiring explicit curvature control.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Inertia-Controlling Methods for General Quadratic Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order boundary for local optimality of a stationary linearly constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point of a QP with affine constraints and symmetric Hessian \(Q\), and define its critical cone by \(C(x^*)=\{d\in T_\Omega(x^*):\nabla q(x^*)^{\mathsf T}d=0\}\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer, then \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd\ge0\) for every \(d\in C(x^*)\). If some \(d\in C(x^*)\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd<0\), then \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer. Conversely, if \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*)\), then \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer with local quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT is insufficient for an indefinite QP: curvature must be nonnegative on the critical cone, while strict positivity there certifies a strict local minimum.
assumptions_latex: The constraints are affine and \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\).
\(T_\Omega(x^*)\) is the tangent cone of the polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimum}\Rightarrow Q\succeq0\text{ on }C(x^*);\quad Q\succ0\text{ on }C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\Rightarrow x^*\text{ strict local minimum}.

notation.meaning: Critical cone of first-order-neutral feasible directions.
Tangent cone to the feasible polyhedron at x*.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Curvature Boundary
Indefinite-QP Active-Set Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convex-QP guarantees when reduced curvature is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), let \(W\) be a working set and \(Z\) span the null space of the corresponding active-constraint matrix. Convex active-set optimality guarantees require \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\succeq0\). If some feasible tangent direction \(p=Zd\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}QZd<0\), a stationary KKT point on that face need not be a local minimizer. For example, minimizing \(-x^2/2\) over \([-1,1]\) has the interior KKT point \(x=0\), which is a strict local maximum. Curvature detection or negative-curvature steps are therefore necessary beyond this boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative reduced curvature invalidates convex active-set guarantees: a KKT point may be a maximum rather than a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The active constraints define feasible tangent directions \(p\) through their null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\not\succeq0\) permits KKT points that are not local minima.

children.title: Logarithmic-Barrier QP Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Feasibility Does Not Ensure Barrier Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict feasibility alone does not guarantee existence of logarithmic-barrier minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{-x:x\ge0\}\), the strict domain is \(D=(0,\infty)\) and \(\phi_\mu(x)=-x-\mu\log x\). For every \(\mu>0\), \(\phi_\mu(x)\to-\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\), so the barrier minimizer set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible unbounded improving direction can make every barrier subproblem unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is \(x\ge0\), with strict domain \(D=(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x>0}\phi_\mu(x)=-\infty\quad\text{and}\quad X(\mu)=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Feasibility Does Not Ensure Barrier Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier Hessian and Sharp Strict-Convexity Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-space curvature criterion for the logarithmic-barrier QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in D\), let \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(h-Gx)\). Then \(\nabla^2\phi_\mu(x)=Q+\mu G^{\mathsf T}S^{-2}G\), and for \(d\in\ker A\), \[d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\phi_\mu(x)d=d^{\mathsf T}Qd+\mu\|S^{-1}Gd\|_2^2.\] Hence the Hessian is positive definite on \(\ker A\), and the barrier objective is strictly convex on the equality-feasible affine space, exactly when \(\ker A\cap\ker Q\cap\ker G=\{0\}\). Under this condition any existing minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic curvature and constraint-normal curvature combine to give a sharp nullspace test for strict convexity and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2\phi_\mu(x)\succ0\text{ on }\ker A\iff\ker A\cap\ker Q\cap\ker G=\{0\}.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrix of positive inequality slacks

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Hessian and Sharp Strict-Convexity Test
Logarithmic-Barrier QP Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained logarithmic barriers for strictly feasible QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) and the strict domain \(D=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h\}\). For every \(\mu>0\), the logarithmic-barrier QP is
\[\min_{x\in D}\ \phi_\mu(x):=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^{m}\log\bigl(h_i-G_i x\bigr).\]
The collection \(\{\phi_\mu:\mu>0\}\), together with its minimizer sets \(X(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}\phi_\mu(x)\), is the logarithmic-barrier QP family. If \(Q\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), every nonempty \(X(\mu)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family adds a weighted negative-log penalty for every positive inequality slack while retaining equality constraints exactly.
assumptions_latex: Each row \(G_i\) corresponds to one inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}\left[f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log(h_i-G_i x)\right]\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly covers logarithmic-barrier QPs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The barrier family is coherently defined, the strict domain and parameter are explicit, and the conditional uniqueness statement follows the appropriate equality-feasible curvature condition. The definition has no supporting source reference or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and Derivative of the Primal Central Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smoothness and sensitivity equation for a regular primal central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(\mu)=h-Gx(\mu)>0\), \(S(\mu)=\operatorname{Diag}(s(\mu))\), and \(H_\mu=Q+\mu G^{\mathsf T}S(\mu)^{-2}G\). If \[K_\mu=\begin{bmatrix}H_\mu&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular, then \((x(\mu),y(\mu))\) is locally differentiable and \[K_\mu\begin{bmatrix}x'(\mu)\\y'(\mu)\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}G^{\mathsf T}s(\mu)^{-1}\\0\end{bmatrix}.\] If the bordered matrix is singular, this stationarity system alone does not guarantee such a regular local parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular path point, the primal path is differentiable and its parameter derivative is obtained from one bordered-Hessian solve.
assumptions_latex: Each barrier problem on an open parameter interval has a path point x(\mu) and equality multiplier y(\mu).
The displayed bordered matrix is nonsingular at the parameter considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_\mu\begin{bmatrix}x'(\mu)\\y'(\mu)\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}G^{\mathsf T}s(\mu)^{-1}\\0\end{bmatrix}.

notation.meaning: barrier Hessian at the path point

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity and Derivative of the Primal Central Path
Primal Central Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal trajectory of unique logarithmic-barrier minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the logarithmic-barrier QP family, assume that for every \(\mu>0\) the barrier objective has a unique minimizer. The primal central path is the mapping \(x:(0,\infty)\to D\) defined by
\[x(\mu)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}\left\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_{i=1}^{m}\log(h_i-G_i x)\right\}.\]
Equivalently, \(x(\mu)\) is accompanied by an equality multiplier \(y(\mu)\) and satisfies \(Ax(\mu)=b\) and
\[Qx(\mu)+c+A^{\mathsf T}y(\mu)+\mu G^{\mathsf T}(h-Gx(\mu))^{-1}=0,\]
where the inverse is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal central path traces the unique minimizers of the logarithmic-barrier QPs as the barrier parameter varies.
assumptions_latex: The strict feasible domain is nonempty.
Each barrier subproblem has a unique minimizer.
The equality constraints admit Lagrange multipliers at those minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu\mapsto x(\mu)\) is the primal central path.

notation.meaning: equality multiplier at the path point

children.title: Primal-Dual Central Path
children.top_down_role: Coupled interior trajectories in primal-dual space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for a Unique Primal-Dual Central Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness at each positive barrier parameter under strict convexity, equality independence, and strict primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q\succ0\), \(A\) has full row rank, and \(\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h\}\neq\varnothing\). For every \(\mu>0\), the logarithmic-barrier QP has a unique minimizer \(x(\mu)\). With \(s=h-Gx(\mu)\) and \(z_i=\mu/s_i\), there is a unique \(y(\mu)\) such that \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu),z(\mu))\) satisfies the primal-dual central-path equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict convexity, independent equality constraints, and strict primal feasibility ensure a unique primal-dual central point for every positive barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,(x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu),z(\mu))\text{ satisfying the central-path equations}.
review_flags: These are sufficient, not necessary, conditions for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Conditions for a Unique Primal-Dual Central Point
Primal-Dual Central Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed KKT trajectory for a convex inequality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(\mu>0\), a primal-dual central-path point is a quadruple \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu),z(\mu))\) satisfying
\[Ax=b,\qquad Gx+s=h,\qquad Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\]
\[s>0,\qquad z>0,\qquad S z=\mu\mathbf 1,\]
where \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). The primal-dual central path is the set, or the parameterized trajectory when the solution is unique, of all such quadruples as \(\mu\) ranges over \((0,\infty)\). Its duality gap is \(s^{\mathsf T}z=m\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual central path consists of feasible positive primal-dual points satisfying complementarity products equal to the barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: Strictly feasible primal and dual points exist.
The displayed perturbed KKT system has a solution for each considered \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S z=\mu\mathbf1\) and \(s^{\mathsf T}z=m\mu\) along the primal-dual central path.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the perturbed-KKT definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbed KKT system, positivity conditions, and duality-gap identity consistently define the primal-dual central path. The selected definition kind fits the leaf, but the record contains no authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual central path for a linearly constrained convex quadratic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-QP specialization of the perturbed slack-form KKT system; the internally inconsistent displayed Newton equation is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \frac12x^TGx+g^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\ge b,\qquad G=G^T\succeq0,\] and introduce \(y=Ax-b\). With \(Y=\operatorname{diag}(y)\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)\), and \[F(x,y,\lambda)=\begin{bmatrix}Gx-A^T\lambda+g\\Ax-y-b\\Y\Lambda e\end{bmatrix},\] the primal-dual central path is \[\mathcal C=\left\{(x_\tau,y_\tau,\lambda_\tau):F(x_\tau,y_\tau,\lambda_\tau)=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\\tau e\end{bmatrix},\ (y_\tau,\lambda_\tau)>0,\ \tau>0\right\}.\] Thus the path retains stationarity and slack feasibility while replacing complementarity \(Y\Lambda e=0\) by the positive perturbation \(Y\Lambda e=\tau e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic program with linear inequalities, introduce nonnegative slacks. The primal-dual central path consists of strictly positive slack-multiplier triples satisfying stationarity and slack feasibility, with every complementary product equal to the same positive parameter.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad g\in\mathbb R^n,\quad b\in\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C=\left\{(x_\tau,y_\tau,\lambda_\tau):Gx_\tau-A^T\lambda_\tau+g=0,\ Ax_\tau-y_\tau-b=0,\ Y_\tau\Lambda_\tau e=\tau e,\ (y_\tau,\lambda_\tau)>0\right\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of a bounded primal central path to a unique QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a convex QP with a nonempty strict feasible domain and a finite attained optimum. For every \(\mu>0\), let \(x(\mu)\) be a primal logarithmic-barrier minimizer. Assume that \(\{x(\mu):0<\mu\le\bar\mu\}\) is bounded for some \(\bar\mu>0\). If the original QP has the unique primal optimal solution \(x_*\), then
\[\lim_{\mu\downarrow0}x(\mu)=x_*.\]
This conclusion concerns only the primal path and does not assert uniqueness of limiting multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the small-parameter logarithmic-barrier path is bounded and the convex QP has a unique primal optimizer, the path converges to that optimizer as the barrier parameter tends to zero.
