children.title: Potential-Reduction Complexity Family
children.top_down_role: Polynomial guarantees organized around potential reduction rather than path neighborhoods.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: A Class of Potential Reduction Algorithms and Proofs of Convergence Theorems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positivity Gives No Global Potential Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling boundary for the logarithmic primal-dual potential with parameter \(\rho>m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi_\rho(s,z)=\rho\log(s^{\mathsf T}z)-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(s_i z_i)\) and any \(\tau>0\), \[\Phi_\rho(\tau s,z)=\Phi_\rho(s,z)+(\rho-m)\log\tau.\] Thus, when \(\rho>m\), letting \(\tau\downarrow0\) makes \(\Phi_\rho(\tau s,z)\to-\infty\) despite \(\tau s,z>0\). Positivity alone therefore cannot supply the finite nonterminal lower bound needed to telescope a uniform potential decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithmic potential is unbounded below over the positive orthant, so a complexity proof needs a termination-dependent or invariant-set lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{s,z>0}\Phi_\rho(s,z)=-\infty.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling of one complementarity vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Gives No Global Potential Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite lower bound before a complementarity target is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>m\), \(s,z>0\), and \(\mu=(s^{\mathsf T}z)/m>\varepsilon>0\), \[\Phi_\rho(s,z)\ge(\rho-m)\log(m\varepsilon)+m\log m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive complementarity stopping threshold supplies a finite nonterminal lower bound, although positivity alone does not.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi_\rho(s,z)\ge L_\varepsilon:=(\rho-m)\log(m\varepsilon)+m\log m.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Nonterminal Potential Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential Imbalance Controls the Smallest Complementarity Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centrality consequence of bounding the shape component of the potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i=s_i z_i>0\), \(q_i=mp_i/\sum_jp_j\), and \(D=-\sum_i\log q_i\). Since \(q_i\le m\), \[D\le B\Rightarrow s_i z_i\ge e^{-B}m^{-(m-1)}\mu\quad\text{for every }i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded imbalance term prevents any complementarity product from vanishing relative to the mean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_i(s_i z_i/\mu)\ge e^{-B}m^{-(m-1)}.
knowledge_statements.title: Potential Imbalance Controls the Smallest Complementarity Product

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale-Imbalance Decomposition of the Logarithmic Potential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition separating complementarity scale from imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i=s_i z_i>0\), \(t=\sum_i p_i=m\mu\), and \(q_i=mp_i/t\). Then \[\Phi_\rho(s,z)=(\rho-m)\log t+m\log m-\sum_{i=1}^m\log q_i.\] The last term is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when every \(p_i=\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The potential separates into a complementarity-scale term and a nonnegative imbalance term vanishing on the central path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi_\rho\ge(\rho-m)\log(m\mu)+m\log m.

notation.meaning: Complementarity product normalized to mean one.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Imbalance Decomposition of the Logarithmic Potential

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a logarithmic-potential bound into an average-complementarity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>m\), \(s,z\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), and \(\mu=s^{\mathsf T}z/m\), \[\Phi_\rho(s,z)\le B\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mu\le \frac1m\exp\!\left(\frac{B-m\log m}{\rho-m}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper bound on the logarithmic potential supplies an explicit upper bound on average complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu\le m^{-1}\exp((B-m\log m)/(\rho-m))\).

notation.meaning: Certified upper bound on the potential.

knowledge_statements.title: Potential Upper Bound Certifies Complementarity
Potential-Reduction Complexity Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional feasible-start potential-reduction iteration bound for a convex QP with inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For complementarity pairs \(s^k,z^k\in\mathbb R_{++}^{m}\), let \(\mu_k=(s^k)^{\mathsf T}z^k/m\) and \[\Phi_\rho(s,z)=\rho\log(s^{\mathsf T}z)-\sum_{i=1}^{m}\log(s_i z_i),\qquad \rho>m.\] Suppose each nonterminal iteration satisfies \(\Phi_\rho(s^{k+1},z^{k+1})\le \Phi_\rho(s^k,z^k)-\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), and suppose a finite constant \(L_\varepsilon\) satisfies \(\Phi_\rho(s^k,z^k)\ge L_\varepsilon\) whenever \(\mu_k>\varepsilon\). Then the first index \(N\) for which \(\mu_N\le\varepsilon\) satisfies \[N\le \left\lceil\frac{\Phi_\rho(s^0,z^0)-L_\varepsilon}{\delta}\right\rceil.\] In particular, if \(\Phi_\rho(s^0,z^0)-L_\varepsilon=O\!\left(\delta\sqrt m\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right)\), then \(N=O\!\left(\sqrt m\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform potential decrease gives an iteration bound only when the potential has a finite lower bound along all nonterminal iterates. A square-root logarithmic rate additionally requires the corresponding bound on the initial potential gap.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and a strictly feasible primal-dual starting point exists.
The potential decreases by at least \(\delta>0\), and \(L_\varepsilon\) is a finite lower bound on the nonterminal potentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\le\left\lceil(\Phi_\rho(s^0,z^0)-L_\varepsilon)/\delta\right\rceil\), with the stated conditional polynomial specialization.

notation.meaning: Finite lower bound for the potential over nonterminal iterates.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: telescoping a uniform potential decrease against a finite lower bound

children.title: QP Status-Certificate Complexity
children.top_down_role: Iteration analysis tied to approximate optimality and status certification.

children.title: Optimality-Certificate Complexity
children.top_down_role: Iteration regimes for obtaining approximate primal-dual optimality evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Certificate Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration and sparse-arithmetic verification costs for an approximate KKT certificate of a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx+s=h,\quad s\ge0.\] An absolute \(\varepsilon\)-KKT certificate is a tuple \((x,y,s,z)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\) with \(s,z\ge0\) satisfying \[\max\!\left\{\|Ax-b\|,\|Gx+s-h\|,\|Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\|,s^{\mathsf T}z\right\}\le\varepsilon.\] A short-step primal-dual path-following method initialized in its prescribed neighborhood and having the standard contraction bound produces such a certificate after \[O\!\left(\sqrt m\log\frac{m\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\] iterations, because the gap condition requires average complementarity at most \(\varepsilon/m\). Given the tuple, verification costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+n+p+m)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step method reaches an absolute KKT-gap tolerance after a square-root logarithmic number of iterations, with the logarithm adjusted because the total gap equals m times average complementarity. The supplied certificate is checked using sparse matrix-vector products and vector operations.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible primal-dual point in the short-step neighborhood is available.
The method satisfies its stated short-step complementarity contraction, and the residual norm is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=O\!\left(\sqrt m\log(m\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right)\), and certificate verification is linear in the stored matrix nonzeros up to vector operations.

notation.meaning: Primal variables, equality multipliers, slacks, and inequality multipliers.
Absolute residual and total complementarity tolerance.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: total complementarity equals m times average complementarity

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Complexity
children.top_down_role: Iteration regimes for producing approximate evidence of primal or dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a validated infeasibility certificate from a merely small numerical Farkas residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), vectors \((y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\), \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\) certify infeasibility. If only \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\|\le\varepsilon\) is known, the uncancelled term \(x^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z)\) need not be controlled when no bound on a putative feasible \(x\) is available. Thus a small cancellation residual alone is not an exact infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized multiplier with a small but nonzero cancellation residual is not automatically an exact infeasibility certificate; rigorous validation or an applicable error bound is required.
assumptions_latex: No a priori bound controls the residual inner product with a putative feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\|\le\varepsilon\ \text{alone does not certify exact infeasibility.}
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Farkas Residual Boundary
Infeasibility-Certificate Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation and direct verification boundary for a Farkas certificate of primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint system \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), an exact primal-infeasibility certificate is a pair \((y,z)\) satisfying \[A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0.\] After normalization \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\), verification costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+m+n)\) arithmetic operations. If an embedding-based interior-point method has iteration bound \(T(\varepsilon)\) for reaching a normalized certificate residual at most \(\varepsilon\), certificate generation requires at most \(T(\varepsilon)\) iterations; this complexity is not implied by an optimality-only path-following bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized Farkas vector is cheaply verifiable, but polynomial-time generation requires an infeasibility-aware embedding or phase method rather than an optimality-only path follower.
assumptions_latex: The constraint data are finite-dimensional and explicitly represented.
The exact certificate is normalized by \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{verify}}=O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+m+n)\), while generation complexity equals the bound established for the chosen status-detecting method.

notation.meaning: Iteration bound of the selected embedding or phase method.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional Farkas certificates have direct sparse verification costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized Farkas conditions and sparse verification estimate are standard, but no inspectable citation supports them or a status-generation bound. The claim that generation requires specifically an embedding or phase method is also broader than justified; other status-detecting algorithms are possible.

children.title: Unboundedness-Status Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity considerations for distinguishing unbounded behavior from numerical failure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates verification of a supplied recession ray from algorithmic generation of an unboundedness status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP over a nonempty polyhedron, feasible iterates with decreasing objective values, large norms, or failed KKT residuals do not by themselves certify \(\inf f=-\infty\). A rigorous status requires validated recession evidence, such as a feasible base point \(x_0\) and direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Therefore an iteration bound proved only for convergence to an optimal primal-dual point gives no unboundedness-detection bound unless the method is separately proved to generate such evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diverging iterates or decreasing objective values are not unboundedness certificates. An optimality-only iteration theorem does not bound production of a validated recession ray.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is a nonempty polyhedron.
No separate status-detection theorem is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Optimality-only iteration complexity}\not\Rightarrow\text{unboundedness-detection complexity}.

notation.meaning: Feasible base point for the recession ray.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Detection Boundary
Unboundedness-Status Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse-arithmetic verification complexity for an exact recession certificate of convex-QP unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). For the objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a supplied pair \((x_0,d)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) is an exact sufficient certificate of unboundedness below if \[Ax_0=b,\qquad Gx_0\le h,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad Gd\le0,\qquad Qd=0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] These conditions can be checked in \[O\!\left(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+n+p+m\right)\] arithmetic operations, excluding input reading conventions already represented by the nonzero counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible base point together with a feasible recession direction having zero quadratic curvature and negative linear cost is a sufficient exact certificate of unboundedness. Verification uses sparse matrix-vector products and vector comparisons.
assumptions_latex: The base point \(x_0\) and direction \(d\) are supplied explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditions certify \(\inf f=-\infty\) and have verification cost linear in the stored matrix nonzeros up to vector operations.

notation.meaning: Number of stored nonzero entries of a matrix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sufficient recession-ray certificate for a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective

children.title: Iteration-Arithmetic Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinction between polynomial iteration counts and the cost or conditioning of each Newton solve.

children.title: Polynomial Iteration Bounds
children.top_down_role: Iteration-count guarantees expressed independently of detailed linear-algebra costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Iteration Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step path-following iteration count, distinct from the arithmetic cost of solving Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP with \(m\) complementarity pairs, suppose a short-step primal-dual method keeps every iterate in a fixed central-path neighborhood and chooses steps satisfying \[\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt m}\right)\mu_k\] for a constant \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) independent of the data and \(k\). Then an iterate with \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) is obtained after at most \[\left\lceil\frac{\sqrt m}{\gamma}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil+1\] iterations. This is an iteration bound only; it does not bound factorization cost, finite-precision bit complexity, or conditioning-dependent work inside an iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform square-root-scaled complementarity contraction yields a logarithmic-accuracy polynomial iteration count but says nothing by itself about linear-system cost.
assumptions_latex: Every iterate remains in the neighborhood for which the contraction estimate holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=O(\!\sqrt m\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\!)\) outer iterations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: geometric complementarity contraction gives the displayed iteration estimate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed iteration count follows correctly from the assumed contraction and appropriately excludes arithmetic and bit complexity. No citation or inspectable locator establishes that contraction for a specified convex-QP short-step method.

children.title: Per-Iteration Arithmetic Cost
children.top_down_role: Factorization, matrix-operation, and structured-solve costs within each interior iteration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-independent dense cost once a Newton system of fixed order has been assembled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Once a dense symmetric Newton system of order \(r\) has been assembled, a standard dense direct factorization costs \(O(r^3)\) arithmetic operations and each triangular solution costs \(O(r^2)\). The assembly cost is formulation-dependent and must be accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense Newton factorization is cubic in the system order, while triangular solves are quadratic; assembly depends on the chosen elimination.
assumptions_latex: A dense unit-cost arithmetic model is used.
A standard dense direct factorization is applicable to the assembled system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{factor}}=O(r^3)\) and \(C_{\mathrm{solve}}=O(r^2)\).

notation.meaning: Order of the assembled Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Dense Direct-Solve Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on sparsity-only operation counts for Newton factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sparse symmetric Newton matrix, an elimination ordering generally creates fill. Triangular solution work is proportional to the number of stored factor entries, while factorization work and storage depend on elimination fronts, ordering, and the sparsity graph. Without structural restrictions, the filled factor can be dense, so an order-\(r\) sparse input can still require \(O(r^3)\) factorization work and \(O(r^2)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse input alone does not determine direct-solve cost; fill and ordering control the work, whose worst case remains dense.
assumptions_latex: A direct symmetric factorization is used.
No graph class or fill guarantee is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{factor}}=O(r^3)\) and storage \(O(r^2)\) remain possible in the worst case.

notation.meaning: Order of the sparse Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Fill Determines Direct-Solve Cost
Per-Iteration Arithmetic Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense direct-solve cost for one primal-dual Newton iteration after standard block elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal-dual QP iteration whose block eliminations produce a dense symmetric Newton system of order \(r=n+p\), where \(n\) is the primal dimension and \(p\) is the number of equality constraints. Forming its coefficient matrix costs at most \(O(n^2m+n m^2)\) arithmetic operations under naive dense multiplication, while a dense symmetric-indefinite factorization and triangular solves cost \(O(r^3)\) and \(O(r^2)\), respectively. Consequently, one iteration has polynomial dense arithmetic cost \[O(n^2m+n m^2+(n+p)^3).\] For sparse implementations, this expression is only an upper bound because actual work depends on ordering and factor fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After eliminating complementarity blocks, a dense Newton step costs cubic work in the reduced system size plus the work required to assemble that system.
assumptions_latex: All matrices are treated as dense and arithmetic operations have unit cost.
The diagonal complementarity blocks are nonsingular because \(s>0\) and \(z>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{iter}}=O(n^2m+n m^2+(n+p)^3)\) in the stated dense arithmetic model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dense assembly and factorization admit polynomial arithmetic bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cubic dense factorization estimate is standard, but the assembly expression depends on the precise eliminated Newton system and is not derivable from the unspecified block elimination. An authoritative formulation and operation count are required.

children.title: Conditioning-Driven Solve Complexity
children.top_down_role: Arithmetic and precision costs arising from difficult Newton-system conditioning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-accuracy limitation for an inexact Newton-system solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be nonsingular, \(Hd=r\), and \((H+E)\widehat d=r\), with \(\|E\|\le\delta\|H\|\) in a subordinate norm. If \(\kappa(H)\delta<1\), then \(\|\widehat d-d\|/\|d\|\le\kappa(H)\delta/(1-\kappa(H)\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning amplifies backward error, so a stable solve need not give a uniformly accurate Newton direction when the condition number is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat d-d\|/\|d\|\le\kappa(H)\delta/(1-\kappa(H)\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Number Amplification of Backward Error
Conditioning-Driven Solve Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative solution cost for a symmetric positive-definite reduced Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the reduced Newton equation be \(H_k d=r_k\), where \(H_k\) is symmetric positive definite, and let \(P_k\) be a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner. Preconditioned conjugate gradients returns \(d_j\) satisfying \[\|d_j-d_*\|_{H_k}\le\eta\|d_0-d_*\|_{H_k}\] after \[j=O\!\left(\sqrt{\kappa(P_k^{-1/2}H_kP_k^{-1/2})}\log(1/\eta)\right)\] preconditioned matrix-vector iterations. Thus polynomial outer iteration complexity does not alone imply a uniform arithmetic bound: the inner work also depends on spectral conditioning, preconditioner application cost, and the accuracy \(\eta\) required to preserve the outer neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterative Newton solve scales with the square root of the preconditioned condition number and logarithmically with the requested relative accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The stopping criterion is relative error in the \(H_k\)-energy norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j=O(\sqrt{\kappa_k}\log(1/\eta))\), where \(\kappa_k=\kappa(P_k^{-1/2}H_kP_k^{-1/2})\).

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the preconditioned system.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical preconditioned conjugate-gradient convergence estimate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated energy-norm PCG rate is standard for SPD matrices and the content kind fits the leaf. A specific source is still required, particularly for the claim connecting inner accuracy and preservation of an outer QP path neighborhood.

children.title: Practical Predictor-Corrector Theory Boundary
children.top_down_role: Separation between polynomially analyzed path-following families and widely used heuristic centering variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Practical Predictor-Corrector Theory Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between safeguarded polynomial path following and unsafeguarded practical predictor-corrector choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A predictor-corrector QP method inherits a polynomial path-following bound only if its accepted step preserves the neighborhood, positivity, and complementarity-decrease conditions used by that bound. A practical rule that chooses the centering parameter from an affine-scaling prediction and then accepts a fraction-to-boundary step does not, by that rule alone, imply \[\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt m}\right)\mu_k\] or invariance of any prescribed central-path neighborhood. Therefore the standard polynomial iteration theorem cannot be asserted for the unsafeguarded heuristic. It becomes applicable only after adding safeguards and proving the required invariants for the resulting algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Practical affine predictor and adaptive-centering rules are not automatically covered by polynomial path-following theory unless explicit safeguards preserve its neighborhood and decrease invariants.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial theorem being invoked requires positivity, neighborhood invariance, and a uniform complementarity contraction.
The practical rule has no additional acceptance test establishing those properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No polynomial iteration bound follows solely from the unsafeguarded predictor-corrector prescription.

notation.meaning: Uniform contraction constant required by the analyzed method.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: theorem hypotheses cannot be transferred to a heuristic lacking their invariants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical warning is appropriately classified as a failure boundary: a heuristic does not inherit a theorem whose invariants have not been established. No predictor-corrector source or locator supports the algorithm-specific characterization and boundary.

children.title: Strictly Feasible-Start Methods
children.top_down_role: Interior methods initialized within the primal-dual feasible region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary initialization regime for a strictly primal-dual feasible-start method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method whose invariant requires exact primal feasibility, exact stationarity, and strictly positive complementary variables cannot be invoked directly from a tuple violating any required equality or sign condition. Such a tuple must first be repaired by Phase I, replaced by an infeasible-start method, or mapped into an embedding; positivity of slacks alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without the complete strictly primal-dual feasible tuple required by the invariant, this method class cannot start directly.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm requires its initial iterate to satisfy its stated feasible central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^0\notin\mathcal F_{++}^{pd}\Rightarrow\text{the feasible-start invariant is unavailable at iteration }0.

notation.meaning: The algorithm's strictly primal-dual feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Invocation Feasibility Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Feasibility Invariance of Feasible-Start Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preservation of the affine primal-dual equations by homogeneous Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((x,y,s,z)\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(Gx+s=h\), and \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\). If a direction satisfies \[A\Delta x=0,\qquad G\Delta x+\Delta s=0,\qquad Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=0,\] then every common-step update preserves all three affine equations exactly. If additionally \(s+\alpha\Delta s>0\) and \(z+\alpha\Delta z>0\), the updated tuple remains strictly primal-dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogeneous feasible-start directions preserve the affine primal-dual equations; positivity and the chosen neighborhood remain to be safeguarded.
assumptions_latex: The initial affine primal-dual equations hold exactly.
The same scalar step is applied to all direction blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w\in\mathcal F_{++}^{pd},\ \Delta w\in T_{\mathrm{aff}}\mathcal F^{pd},\ s^+,z^+>0\Rightarrow w^+\in\mathcal F_{++}^{pd}.

notation.meaning: Direction space of the affine primal-dual feasibility equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Feasibility Invariance of Feasible-Start Directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of the Strict Feasible-Start Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of tuples satisfying the affine feasible-start invariant and strict sign conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(Ax=b\), \(Gx+s=h\), and \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\). If two tuples \(w^1=(x^1,y^1,s^1,z^1)\) and \(w^2=(x^2,y^2,s^2,z^2)\) satisfy these equations with \(s^j,z^j>0\), then for every \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), \(w^\lambda=\lambda w^1+(1-\lambda)w^2\) satisfies the same equations and has \(s^\lambda,z^\lambda>0\). Thus the strictly primal-dual feasible-start domain is convex. This does not assert convexity of every method-specific central neighborhood contained in it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex combinations of strictly primal-dual feasible tuples remain strictly primal-dual feasible.
assumptions_latex: Both endpoint tuples satisfy the same fixed QP affine equations.
Both endpoint slack and multiplier vectors are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^1,w^2\in\mathcal F_{++}^{pd},\ 0<\lambda<1\Rightarrow\lambda w^1+(1-\lambda)w^2\in\mathcal F_{++}^{pd}.

notation.meaning: Strictly primal-dual feasible-start domain for the fixed QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity of the Strict Feasible-Start Domain
Strictly Feasible-Start Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual feasible-start interior iteration for a convex QP with equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Q\succeq0\) and an initial tuple \((x^0,y^0,s^0,z^0)\) satisfying \[Ax^0=b,\quad Gx^0+s^0=h,\quad Qx^0+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^0+G^{\mathsf T}z^0=0,\quad s^0,z^0>0,\] repeat: choose a centering target \(\sigma_k\mu_k\), solve the primal-dual Newton equations for \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s,\Delta z)\), and select \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) so that \(s^{k+1},z^{k+1}>0\) and the prescribed path neighborhood is retained. Stop when \(s^{k\mathsf T}z^k\le\varepsilon\), and output the current primal-dual tuple as an approximate optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from an exactly feasible positive primal-dual point, take safeguarded centered Newton steps, and stop when complementarity reaches the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A strictly primal-dual feasible initial tuple is available.
The Newton system and neighborhood acceptance test are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output remains primal-dual feasible and positive, with \(s^{\mathsf T}z\le\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical feasible-start primal-dual interior-point iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the feasible-start container, but the Newton equations and accepted neighborhood are not defined precisely enough to substantiate feasibility preservation or convergence. A specific feasible-start QP algorithm and locator are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal leaves the neighborhood, parameter rule, and step rule unspecified and substantially regenerates the deferred seed.
assumptions_latex: A method-specific neighborhood and acceptance rule would be required.

children.top_down_role: Initialization allowing primal or dual residuals before path tracking.

assumptions_latex: Step length is chosen solely to preserve strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^{k+1},z^{k+1}>0\ \not\Rightarrow\ r_p^k\to0,\ r_d^k\to0,\ \mu_k\to0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of fraction-to-boundary safeguarding in an infeasible-start method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fraction-to-boundary step guarantees only \(s^{k+1}>0\) and \(z^{k+1}>0\). Without a merit, filter, central-neighborhood, or other globalization rule and suitable regularity, it does not imply decrease of the primal residual, dual residual, or complementarity and supplies neither convergence nor an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping slacks and multipliers positive does not by itself reduce residuals, prove convergence, or certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Is Not Globalization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^0,y^0,s^0,z^0)\text{ lies in the complementarity interior although }r_p^0\text{ and }r_d^0\text{ may be nonzero}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an algebraic infeasible start with positive complementarity variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary finite \(x^0,y^0\), any \(s^0>0\) and \(z^0>0\) define a complementarity-interior algebraic iterate when the mismatches are retained as residuals \(r_p^0=(Ax^0-b,\,Gx^0+s^0-h)\) and \(r_d^0=Qx^0+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^0+G^{\mathsf T}z^0\). Thus an infeasible start requires positivity of complementarity variables, not satisfaction of the original affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite primal and equality-dual guesses can be paired with positive slacks and multipliers while violations are carried explicitly as residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Absorbing Positive Initialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra-type direction variant from a positive residual-infeasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \((x,y,s,z)\) with \(s,z>0\), first solve the primal-dual Newton equations with complementarity right-hand side \(-Sz\) to obtain an affine direction. Compute maximal positivity-preserving affine steps and predicted complementarity \(\mu_a\), and choose a declared \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), commonly \(\sigma=(\mu_a/\mu)^3\). Resolve the same Newton matrix with complementarity right-hand side \(-Sz+\sigma\mu\mathbf1-\Delta S^a\Delta z^a\), retaining the primal and dual residual right-hand sides. Take declared fraction-to-boundary primal and dual steps. A separate acceptance or neighborhood rule is required for convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine predictor estimates complementarity reduction, and a second solve adds centering and the second-order complementarity correction.
assumptions_latex: Both Newton systems are solved to their prescribed tolerances.
A separate globalization or neighborhood policy governs acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^+>0,\ z^+>0\text{ for fraction-to-boundary steps, without an unconditional convergence claim.}
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Predictor-Corrector Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual behavior of a common damped step from an infeasible primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the Newton direction satisfy \[A\Delta x=-r_A,\qquad G\Delta x+\Delta s=-r_G,\qquad Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=-r_d.\] For the common update \((x,y,s,z)^+=(x,y,s,z)+\alpha(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s,\Delta z)\), the affine residuals obey \[r_A^+=(1-\alpha)r_A,\qquad r_G^+=(1-\alpha)r_G,\qquad r_d^+=(1-\alpha)r_d.\] This identity does not establish complementarity reduction, step acceptance, or global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common damped Newton step contracts the linear primal and dual residuals exactly when their equations use the full negative residuals.
assumptions_latex: The QP data are fixed during the update.
One common step length \(\alpha\) is used for all displayed variables.

notation.meaning: Equality, slack-form inequality, and stationarity residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Affine-Residual Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of distinct primal and dual step lengths in an infeasible-start Newton update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=-r_d\). Update \((x,s)\) with step \(\alpha_p\) and \((y,z)\) with step \(\alpha_d\). Then \[r_d^+=(1-\alpha_d)r_d+(\alpha_p-\alpha_d)Q\Delta x.\] If also \(A\Delta x=-r_A\) and \(G\Delta x+\Delta s=-r_G\), then \(r_A^+=(1-\alpha_p)r_A\) and \(r_G^+=(1-\alpha_p)r_G\). Thus exact common-step stationarity contraction generally fails when \(\alpha_p\ne\alpha_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate primal and dual steps preserve primal-residual contraction, but stationarity gains a curvature correction unless the steps coincide.
assumptions_latex: The QP data remain fixed during the update.
The displayed full-residual Newton equations are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_d^+=(1-\alpha_d)r_d+(\alpha_p-\alpha_d)Q\Delta x.
knowledge_statements.title: Separate-Step Residual Identity
Infeasible-Start Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-slack initialization permitting nonzero primal and dual residuals before convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose arbitrary \(x^0,y^0\) and strictly positive \(s^0,z^0\), and define \[r_p^0=(Ax^0-b,\,Gx^0+s^0-h),\qquad r_d^0=Qx^0+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^0+G^{\mathsf T}z^0.\] At iteration \(k\), solve a primal-dual Newton system whose right-hand side reduces \(r_p^k\), \(r_d^k\), and \(S_kz^k-\sigma_k\mu_k\mathbf1\). Choose a fraction-to-boundary step maintaining \(s^{k+1},z^{k+1}>0\). Stop only when the primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity satisfy their stated tolerances; positivity of the initial slacks alone is not a feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize positive slacks and multipliers even with nonzero feasibility residuals, then use damped Newton steps to reduce feasibility and complementarity simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: The initial slacks and inequality multipliers satisfy \(s^0,z^0>0\).
Each Newton system admits a direction satisfying the selected residual-reduction equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method permits \(r_p^0\ne0\) or \(r_d^0\ne0\) while preserving positive complementarity variables during the iteration.

notation.meaning: Combined primal equality and slack residual.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical infeasible-start residual formulation for primal-dual interior methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual formulation fits infeasible-start initialization, but the unspecified Newton system and fraction-to-boundary rule do not establish residual convergence. An authoritative algorithm with its regularity and globalization conditions is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General approximate KKT termination belongs to the termination-certificate system, not this initialization leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(Gx+s=h\), a candidate approximate KKT point tests primal residuals, stationarity, signs, and complementarity against declared tolerances; failure of those tests alone does not certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate KKT termination is a general certificate-system claim rather than a defining result about infeasible-start initialization.
assumptions_latex: A fixed QP sign convention and declared norm and scaling conventions are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{This claim should be placed under the primal-dual residual certificate topic.}
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Termination Test

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns positive residual-infeasible initialization and the warning that positivity is not globalization. The proposed residual termination record is deferred as misplaced. Phase-I construction, strictly feasible starts, complete KKT termination, and embedding-based status detection are excluded sibling or adjacent scopes.

children.title: Phase-I Interior Methods
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary interior families for locating strict feasibility.

assumptions_latex: Strict feasibility is tested against the displayed inequality representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ri}(P)\ne\varnothing\ \not\Rightarrow\ \exists x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h\text{ in an unreduced representation}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of identically active or opposing redundant inequalities on a literal strict-feasibility Phase I.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a displayed inequality is an identity on the equality affine space, or opposing redundant inequalities force an equality, no point satisfies every displayed inequality strictly even when the feasible set has nonempty relative interior. Such rows must be recognized as affine-hull equalities or removed before the common-margin Phase I is interpreted as a relative-interior test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant or identically active inequalities can make literal strict feasibility impossible despite a nonempty relative interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Strictness Formulation Boundary

assumptions_latex: The equality affine space \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty.
The auxiliary optimal value is finite, and an approximate sign declaration uses certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*>0\iff\exists x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h;\qquad t^*=0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\text{ and no strict point exists};\qquad t^*<0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact status interpretation of the primal common-margin auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\{x:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\) and a finite optimum \[t^*=\max\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\}.\] Then \(t^*>0\) exactly when a point satisfies \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx<h\). If \(t^*=0\), the original inequalities are feasible but admit no strictly feasible point. If \(t^*<0\), the original affine inequality system is infeasible. When computed approximately, these conclusions require certified lower or upper bounds that determine the relevant sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum common margin is positive exactly for strict feasibility, zero for feasible boundary-only systems, and negative for infeasibility, under the stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Margin Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required branch before interpreting an inequality-margin Phase-I problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before solving a margin problem constrained by \(Ax=b\), either exhibit \(x_e\) with \(Ax_e=b\), or exhibit \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\). The first outcome establishes a nonempty equality affine space; the second certifies that \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent, so no inequality-margin value should be used for status classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I must first establish equality consistency; a left-null-space witness certifies inconsistent equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax_e=b\quad\text{or}\quad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\Rightarrow\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Consistency Precheck

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically certified interpretation of a common-margin Phase-I solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let certified bounds \(L\le t^*\le U\) be available for the finite common-margin optimum. Then \(L>0\) certifies strict feasibility, \(U<0\) certifies infeasibility of the displayed inequalities relative to \(Ax=b\), and \(L=U=0\) certifies boundary-only feasibility. If \(0\in[L,U]\) with \(L<U\), the computation does not distinguish these statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified interval determines the margin sign only when it lies strictly on one side of zero or collapses exactly to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and \(U\) are verified lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L>0\Rightarrow t^*>0;\quad U<0\Rightarrow t^*<0;\quad 0\in[L,U],\ L<U\Rightarrow\text{status unresolved}.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of the optimal common margin.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Margin-Interval Decision

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual formulation and bounds for the finite common-margin auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[t^*=\max_{x,t}\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\},\] a dual is \[\min_{y,z}\ b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{subject to}\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z=1,\quad z\ge0.\] Every dual-feasible \((y,z)\) supplies \(t^*\le b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\). Under the standard finite feasible linear-programming regime, optimal primal and dual values coincide and are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized nonnegative inequality multipliers form the dual margin problem and provide certified upper bounds on the achievable strict-feasibility margin.
assumptions_latex: The primal common-margin problem is feasible and has a finite optimum.
Strong-duality conclusions are invoked only in the standard finite feasible linear-programming regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*\le b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{for every dual-feasible }(y,z).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Automatic Primal-Interior Start for the Margin Auxiliary Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict initialization of the common-margin auxiliary inequalities after equality consistency is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_e\) with \(Ax_e=b\), choose any \[t_0<\min_i\{h_i-(Gx_e)_i\}.\] Then \((x_e,t_0)\) satisfies \(Ax_e=b\) and \(Gx_e+t_0\mathbf1<h\), so it is a strictly inequality-feasible starting point for a primal barrier treatment of the common-margin auxiliary problem. This construction does not itself produce dual feasibility or specify a complete primal-dual path-following method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once an equality-feasible point is known, choosing a sufficiently negative margin variable strictly satisfies every auxiliary inequality.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inequality set is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t_0<\min_i(h_i-(Gx_e)_i)\Rightarrow Gx_e+t_0\mathbf1<h.
knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Primal-Interior Start for the Margin Auxiliary Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession condition under which the common-margin auxiliary problem has no finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(Ax_e=b\) for some \(x_e\). The common-margin problem \[\sup\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\}\] is unbounded above if and only if there exist \(d\) and \(\tau>0\) such that \(Ad=0\) and \(Gd+\tau\mathbf1\le0\). By positive scaling, this is equivalent to the existence of \(d\) with \(Ad=0\) and \(Gd+\mathbf1\le0\). In this regime finite-sign classification of \(t^*\) is inapplicable, although sufficiently large points on the recession path are strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The margin optimum is infinite exactly when an equality-feasible recession direction improves every displayed inequality margin uniformly.
assumptions_latex: The equality affine space is nonempty.
The displayed inequality family is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*=+\infty\iff\exists d:\ Ad=0,\ Gd+\mathbf1\le0.

notation.meaning: Positive uniform margin growth along a recession direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Common-Margin Boundary
Phase-I Interior Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary max-margin phase for finding a strictly feasible point for the QP inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the equality system \(Ax=b\) is feasible. Solve the auxiliary convex problem \[\max_{x,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\] by an interior method, stopping with a certified bound on its optimal value \(t^*\). If a computed feasible pair has \(t>0\), then \(x\) is strictly feasible for \(Gx<h\) and may initialize a primal interior method. If the certified upper bound satisfies \(t^*\le0\), this phase cannot produce strict primal feasibility. A primal-dual feasible-start method additionally requires an analogous dual phase or a joint auxiliary formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a common inequality margin under the equalities; a positive certified margin supplies a strictly feasible primal point, while a nonpositive optimum rules out such a margin.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary optimum is finite and its reported bound is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t>0\) implies \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx<h\); a certified \(t^*\le0\) implies no point has a positive common margin.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: max-margin auxiliary problem characterizes strict primal feasibility under feasible equalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The max-margin implications are mathematically sound under the stated finiteness assumption, but merely directing an interior method to solve the auxiliary problem does not specify how that method itself is initialized. No source supports the Phase-I procedure, certification mechanism, or complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed separate certificate derived directly from the common-margin dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible normalized multiplier with \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\le0\) gives \(t^*\le0\), and a strictly negative bound gives \(t^*<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed certificate is already an immediate instance of the accepted common-margin dual bound.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No separate record is needed.}
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonpositive-Margin Certificate

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory covers equality consistency, exact common-margin classification, certified sign decisions, literal-strictness failure, and the complete normalized dual. The builder's separate nonpositive-margin certificate was deferred because it duplicates the dual bound and classification theorem. Strictly feasible main solves, residual-infeasible initialization, and homogeneous embeddings were excluded as sibling scopes. A fully initialized interior solution procedure and its complexity remain absent.

children.title: Embedding-Based QP Status Methods
children.top_down_role: QP adaptations of embedded formulations for unified status detection.

assumptions_latex: A feasible base point is available when a primal-unboundedness ray is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A verified alternative multiplier certifies infeasibility, and a verified feasible zero-curvature descent ray certifies primal unboundedness.}

notation.meaning: Equality and nonnegative inequality alternative multipliers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-data checks required before interpreting an embedding output as primal infeasibility or primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q\succeq0\): \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\) certify primal infeasibility. Given a feasible \(x_0\), a direction satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) certifies primal unboundedness along \(x_0+td\). An embedding output may claim these statuses only after the original-data conditions are verified to tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embedding status must be checked using original-data Farkas multipliers or a feasible zero-curvature descent ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Data Status Certificates

assumptions_latex: Status recovery uses a solution scale \(\tau\) and certificate scale \(\kappa\).
No independently normalized original-data certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau\to0,\ \kappa\to0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \text{a certified QP status}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status boundary for scale-variable homogeneous embeddings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an embedding iterate approaches \(\tau\to0\) and \(\kappa\to0\), division by \(\tau\) is ill-conditioned and no positive certificate scale remains. Without a separately normalized original-data certificate, this limit establishes neither optimality, infeasibility, nor unboundedness and must be reported as indeterminate or numerical failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both embedding scales vanish, the scales alone supply no certified QP status.
knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Vanishing-Scale Regime

assumptions_latex: The selected embedding residual block satisfies \(R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)=\tau R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)\|\le\tau\varepsilon\Rightarrow\|R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\|\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Embedding residual block and corresponding dehomogenized original-QP residual block.

review_flags: This applies only to residual blocks satisfying the stated degree-one homogeneity relation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition for recovering an original-QP solution from a positive embedding scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an embedding uses homogeneous variables \((u,\tau)\) and a residual block satisfies \(R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)=\tau R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\) for \(\tau>0\). Then \[\|R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\|=\frac{\|R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)\|}{\tau}.\] Hence an absolute embedded tolerance independent of \(\tau\) does not certify an accurate dehomogenized solution when \(\tau\) is small; the sufficient test is \(\|R_{\mathrm{emb}}\|\le\tau\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embedding residuals are amplified by division by the solution scale, so reliable dehomogenization requires residual accuracy proportional to that scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Dehomogenized Residual Reliability Condition
Embedding-Based QP Status Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status interpretation for homogeneous embeddings that couple optimization variables with scale variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An embedding-based convex-QP method augments the primal-dual equations with nonnegative scalars \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\), maintains a homogeneous feasibility system, and drives its embedded complementarity to zero. At a limiting nonzero embedded solution, \(\tau>0\) permits dehomogenization by division by \(\tau\), yielding a primal-dual QP solution. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the remaining normalized variables must instead satisfy explicitly checked Farkas or recession-ray conditions before infeasibility or unboundedness is declared. If both scale variables approach zero without a normalized certificate, the embedding does not by itself determine status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive solution scale yields an optimal QP solution; a positive certificate scale at zero solution scale may yield infeasibility or unboundedness only after certificate checks.
assumptions_latex: The chosen homogeneous embedding is algebraically equivalent to the QP KKT system when \(\tau>0\).
Reported status certificates are normalized and checked against the original QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau>0\) supports optimal-solution recovery, whereas \(\tau=0\), \(\kappa>0\) supports a nonoptimal status only through a valid original-data certificate.

notation.meaning: Homogeneous scale used to recover primal-dual variables.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: homogeneous embeddings distinguish solution recovery from certificate recovery through scale variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The roles of tau and kappa, and the status partition at tau equal to zero, depend on the exact homogeneous QP embedding. Without its equations and an authoritative locator, the generic statement cannot be verified and may blend distinct embedding conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex QP residual certificate with explicit inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c,x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(h,s,z\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx+s=h\), with \(s\ge0\). For a candidate \((x,s,y,z)\) with \(s,z\ge0\), define \(r_p=(Ax-b,Gx+s-h)\), \(r_d=Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz\), and \(r_c=Sz\), where \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). The inequalities \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\|r_c\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\) form a directly checkable approximate KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small primal, stationarity, and complementarity residuals, together with nonnegative slacks and multipliers, certify approximate satisfaction of the convex QP KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\|Sz\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\) certify approximate primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless aggregation of primal, dual, and complementarity residuals using declared positive scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residuals \(r_p,r_d,r_c\), choose declared scales \(d_p,d_d,d_c>0\) and define \[\rho=\max\left\{\frac{\|r_p\|}{d_p},\frac{\|r_d\|}{d_d},\frac{\|r_c\|_\infty}{d_c}\right\}.\] Then \(\rho\leq\varepsilon\) is equivalent to \(\|r_p\|\leq\varepsilon d_p\), \(\|r_d\|\leq\varepsilon d_d\), and \(\|r_c\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon d_c\). The norms and scale formulas are part of the certificate: enlarging freely chosen denominators can make \(\rho\) arbitrarily small without improving the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declared scales combine the KKT residual components into one dimensionless maximum, but arbitrary rescaling cannot itself establish solution quality.
assumptions_latex: Residual norms and scale formulas are fixed and reported
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\leq\varepsilon\) exactly represents the three declared scaled residual inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative slack and multiplier vectors \(s,z\in\mathbb R_+^m\), exact complementary slackness is \(s_i z_i=0\) for every \(i\). An approximate complementarity certificate at tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\) is \(\|s\circ z\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\). Equivalently, every constraint satisfies \(0\le s_i z_i\le\varepsilon_c\). The scalar \(\mu=s^Tz/m\) may additionally report average complementarity, but it does not by itself impose the same componentwise tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative slacks and multipliers certify approximate complementarity when every product of a slack and its corresponding multiplier is small.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\), suppose \(Ax=b\), \(Gx+s=h\), \(s,z\ge0\), and \(Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz=0\). The associated dual value is \(d(x,y,z)=-\tfrac12x^TQx-b^Ty-h^Tz\), and the primal-dual gap satisfies \(f(x)-d(x,y,z)=s^Tz\ge0\). Hence \(s^Tz\le\varepsilon_g\) is a verifiable certificate that the feasible primal objective lies within \(\varepsilon_g\) of the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible stationary primal-dual pair, the duality gap equals total complementarity; a small gap therefore certifies near-optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Certificates

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s\circ z\|_\infty\le s^Tz\le m\|s\circ z\|_\infty\), and the duality gap equals \(s^Tz\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement of componentwise complementarity and gap certificates under exact feasibility and stationarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(s,z\ge0\), all entries of \(s\circ z\) are nonnegative, so \(\|s\circ z\|_\infty\le s^Tz\le m\|s\circ z\|_\infty\). If primal feasibility and dual stationarity are exact, then \(s^Tz\) is also the primal-dual objective gap. Thus a componentwise tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\) implies gap at most \(m\varepsilon_c\), while a gap tolerance \(\varepsilon_g\) implies every complementarity product is at most \(\varepsilon_g\). Without feasibility and stationarity, objective-gap agreement need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under feasibility and stationarity, total complementarity equals the duality gap and bounds maximum componentwise complementarity within a factor equal to the number of inequalities.
