children.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Ray, alternative-system, and embedding evidence for an empty primal feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-aware sufficient validation of an approximate primal-infeasibility ray when a global feasible-point norm bound is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\ge0\), \(\eta=-(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z)>0\), and \(r=A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\). If every putative feasible point is known a priori to satisfy \(\|x\|\le R\) and \(\eta>R\|r\|_*\), then no \(x\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\). Without a verified error bound of this kind, a small cancellation residual and negative right-hand-side pairing do not constitute a rigorous certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Farkas ray is rigorous only when its separation margin dominates a verified worst-case cancellation error.
assumptions_latex: The bound \(\|x\|\le R\) holds for every putative feasible point.
\(\|\cdot\|_*\) is dual to the norm used for \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z)>R\|A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\|_*\Rightarrow\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Approximate Farkas Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Cancellation Residual Alone Is Not a Farkas Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of tolerance-only validation on an unbounded affine domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\delta>0\), the system \(\delta x\le-1\) is feasible, but with \(z=1\) its cancellation residual is \(\|G^{\mathsf T}z\|=\delta\) and its right-hand-side pairing is \(h^{\mathsf T}z=-1<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small cancellation residual plus a negative pairing does not prove infeasibility without a verified bound controlling the residual error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|G^{\mathsf T}z\|\to0,\ h^{\mathsf T}z<0\not\Rightarrow\{x:Gx\le h\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Arbitrarily small constraint coefficient and cancellation residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Cancellation Residual Alone Is Not a Farkas Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization of an Exact Farkas Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale normalization for a strict mixed-affine infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(\beta=b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\), then \[(\widehat y,\widehat z)=\frac{1}{-\beta}(y,z)\] satisfies \(\widehat z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+G^{\mathsf T}\widehat z=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+h^{\mathsf T}\widehat z=-1\). Conversely, every certificate normalized to pairing \(-1\) is an exact unnormalized certificate. This removes arbitrary positive scaling and supplies a fixed separation target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact Farkas ray with negative right-hand-side pairing can be scaled so that the pairing equals minus one.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier pairing is strictly negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+h^{\mathsf T}\widehat z=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization of an Exact Farkas Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact theorem of alternatives for the fixed equality-and-less-than inequality convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite-dimensional real data \(A,b,G,h\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[(i)\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx\le h;\] \[(ii)\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0.\] Equivalently, the strict pairing in (ii) may be normalized to \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed affine system is infeasible exactly when it has a normalized Farkas multiplier ray with zero aggregate normal and negative right-hand-side pairing.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers are unrestricted and inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\iff\exists(y,z):z\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Affine Farkas Alternative

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^Ty+G^Tz=0\) and \(b^Ty+h^Tz<0\) certify that the primal constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of affine equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine constraint system \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a pair \((y,z)\) satisfying \(z\ge0\), \(A^Ty+G^Tz=0\), and \(b^Ty+h^Tz<0\). These conditions are finitely checkable. Indeed, they separate the affine image of every putative feasible point from the prescribed right-hand sides, so their satisfaction certifies that no \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) obeys all primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas multiplier pair with zero aggregated constraint normal and a strictly negative right-hand-side pairing certifies that the primal affine constraints are inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Farkas certificate is consistent with the stated Gx<=h convention, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied. An authoritative alternative-theorem or QP-certificate reference is required.

children.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Status evidence associated with dual inconsistency or primal recession behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status boundary for the displayed convex-QP dual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual infeasibility means that no tuple satisfies the displayed dual feasibility and stationarity conditions. It must not be reported when dual-feasible points or sequences exist but the dual supremum is unattained. A homogeneous recession witness may exclude every dual-feasible tuple, but interpreting it as primal unboundedness additionally requires a primal feasible base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual infeasibility is absence of every dual-feasible point, not failure to attain a feasible dual supremum; primal unboundedness additionally needs primal feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual systems use one fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{dual infeasibility}\ne\text{dual nonattainment},\qquad \text{dual-infeasibility witness alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{primal unboundedness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility versus Dual Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonstrict Recession Pairing Is Not a Dual-Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on the strict cost inequality in a recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\) do not certify dual infeasibility. The unconstrained QP \(\min_x0\) has \(Q=0\), \(c=0\), admits every nonzero \(d\), and has a feasible stationarity system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero cost pairing is compatible with dual feasibility; strict negativity is essential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{\mathsf T}d=0\not\Rightarrow\text{dual infeasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonstrict Recession Pairing Is Not a Dual-Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization of a Dual-Infeasibility Recession Witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale normalization for an exact homogeneous recession certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d\ne0\) satisfies \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then \(\widehat d=d/(-c^{\mathsf T}d)\) satisfies the same homogeneous equalities and inequalities and \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1\). Conversely, every witness normalized by \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\) is an unnormalized witness. The normalization removes arbitrary positive scaling and supplies a fixed validation target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact negative-cost recession witness can be scaled so that its cost pairing equals minus one.
assumptions_latex: The certificate uses the fixed convention \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat d=\frac{d}{-c^{\mathsf T}d},\qquad c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization of a Dual-Infeasibility Recession Witness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Stationarity Alternative for a Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact alternative between feasibility of the convex-QP dual stationarity system and a negative-cost recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[(i)\quad Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\ge0;\] \[(ii)\quad Qd=0,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad Gd\le0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] Equivalently, system (ii) may be normalized by \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\). Thus absence of every dual-feasible stationary tuple is equivalent to existence of a normalized negative-cost recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite QP, the dual stationarity system is infeasible exactly when a normalized zero-curvature negative-cost recession witness exists.
assumptions_latex: The fixed convention is \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), with \(z\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\exists(x,y,z):Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\ z\ge0\iff\exists d:Qd=0,\ Ad=0,\ Gd\le0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Stationarity Alternative for a Convex QP

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^Td<0\) certify infeasibility of the dual KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate excluding dual feasibility for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP with constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a nonzero vector \(d\) satisfying \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^Td<0\) is a certificate of dual infeasibility. If dual KKT multipliers \((y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\) existed, stationarity paired with \(d\) would give \(c^Td=-z^TGd\ge0\), contradicting \(c^Td<0\). The certificate also identifies a decreasing feasible recession direction whenever the primal feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-curvature feasible recession direction with strictly negative linear cost contradicts dual stationarity and therefore certifies dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction conditions do contradict dual stationarity under the stated sign convention, and certificate is an appropriate kind. A source is required to establish the precise QP status terminology and hypotheses.

children.title: Unboundedness Rays
children.top_down_role: Recession evidence supporting an unbounded primal objective status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and interval-validated sufficient conditions for a convex-QP unboundedness ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\) be a verified feasible point and \(\hat d\ne0\). Verify \(A\hat d=0\), \(G\hat d\le0\), \(\hat d^{\mathsf T}Q\hat d=0\), and \((Q\hat x+c)^{\mathsf T}\hat d<0\). Then \(\hat x+t\hat d\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\) and its objective tends to \(-\infty\). With inexact data or arithmetic, interval or backward-error bounds must establish the recession relations, zero curvature, and a strictly negative entire slope enclosure; residual magnitudes without verified signs are insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible base point and a rigorously validated zero-curvature improving recession direction certify primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: Any inexact coefficient enclosures account for data and arithmetic errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat x+t\hat d\text{ is feasible for all }t\ge0\text{ and }f(\hat x+t\hat d)\to-\infty.

notation.meaning: Validated feasible base point and recession direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Aware Ray Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limits of candidate recession-direction evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direction satisfying homogeneous recession and descent conditions does not certify primal unboundedness unless a primal feasible base point is also verified. Conversely, rejection of one candidate direction, or failure of a numerical search to find one, does not certify boundedness below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unboundedness needs both a feasible base point and a valid improving ray; failure to find a ray is not a boundedness certificate.
assumptions_latex: QP status is determined by finite certificate validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\text{ alone}\not\Rightarrow\inf f=-\infty,\qquad \text{rejected or missing }d\not\Rightarrow\inf f> -\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Ray Evidence Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\) and \(f(x_0+td)\to-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive unboundedness certificate for a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\) and \(Gx_0\le h\). If a nonzero \(d\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^Td<0\), then \(x(t)=x_0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\). Because \(Q\succeq0\) and \(Qd=0\), also \(x_0^TQd=0\), and therefore \(f(x(t))=f(x_0)+t c^Td\to-\infty\). Thus \((x_0,d)\) is a directly verifiable unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a zero-curvature feasible recession direction of negative linear cost certifies that the convex QP objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Rays

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-ray calculation and unboundedness conclusion are mathematically coherent, but the record has no supporting source or standard-field rationale. A specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Embedding-Based Status Separation
children.top_down_role: Status distinctions recovered from homogeneous or self-dual embedding outputs.

assumptions_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding is solved to a nonzero limit
The embedding normalization prevents the zero solution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau>0\) selects an optimal-solution regime, whereas \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) select an infeasibility-certificate regime.

notation.meaning: Embedding scale for recovering primal-dual variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract status split for a normalized homogeneous self-dual QP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a normalized homogeneous self-dual embedding, let \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\) be the solution and certificate scalars. If \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\), division of the embedded primal-dual variables by \(\tau\) yields a primal-dual KKT solution. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the embedding cannot be dehomogenized into an optimal solution; instead, its normalized variable blocks must satisfy one of the primal- or dual-infeasibility certificate systems. The unresolved case \(\tau=\kappa=0\) provides no status certificate and must be excluded by normalization or treated as indeterminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogeneous embedding scalars separate recoverable optimal solutions from normalized infeasibility certificates; a doubly zero limit is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Embedding-Based Status Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Status extraction from tau and kappa depends on the exact homogeneous self-dual embedding, normalization, and sign tests. Without those equations and an authoritative locator, the claimed regime split cannot be verified.

children.title: Newton-Outer Accuracy Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination of linear-system accuracy with QP stopping decisions.

children.title: Newton-Solve Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Residual and error regimes for approximate primal-dual Newton directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning-dependent conversion of a Newton linear-system residual into step error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\Delta=-F\), let \(K\) be nonsingular, and define \(e=K\widehat\Delta+F\). Then \(\widehat\Delta-\Delta=K^{-1}e\) and, for any subordinate norm, \[\|\widehat\Delta-\Delta\|\leq\|K^{-1}\|\,\|e\|.\] If \(F\neq0\), then \[\frac{\|\widehat\Delta-\Delta\|}{\|\Delta\|}\leq\kappa(K)\frac{\|e\|}{\|F\|},\qquad \kappa(K)=\|K\|\,\|K^{-1}\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Newton-equation residual controls step error only after amplification by the inverse or condition number of the Newton matrix.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the selected vector norm
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat\Delta-\Delta\|\leq\|K^{-1}\|\|e\|\), with relative amplification bounded by \(\kappa(K)\).

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected subordinate norm

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Step Error Bound

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|K_k\widehat\Delta_k+F_k\|\le\eta_k\|F_k\|\) certifies the requested relative Newton-solve accuracy.

notation.meaning: KKT or Newton matrix at outer iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative residual condition for an inexact primal-dual Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let the exact Newton equation be \(K_k\Delta_k=-F_k\). A computed step \(\widehat\Delta_k\) has relative residual accuracy \(\eta_k\) when its linear residual \(e_k=K_k\widehat\Delta_k+F_k\) satisfies \(\|e_k\|\le\eta_k\|F_k\|\), where \(0\le\eta_k<1\). For a preconditioned iterative solve, the same condition must be evaluated in the explicitly chosen preconditioned norm. This condition is checkable without knowing the exact Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact Newton step meets its requested accuracy when the residual of the linearized KKT equation is at most a prescribed fraction of the outer residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Solve Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative linear-residual condition is standard and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no evidence record or authoritative locator supports it. The norm and preconditioning convention must also be tied to the cited formulation.

children.title: Outer Stopping Reliability
children.top_down_role: Trustworthiness of QP termination decisions under inexact linear solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Way Stopping Decision Under Additive Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe acceptance, safe rejection, and the indeterminate band under a certified additive residual-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\widehat F=F+e\), \(\|e\|\leq\delta\), and \(\varepsilon>\delta\). Then \(\|\widehat F\|\leq\varepsilon-\delta\) guarantees \(\|F\|\leq\varepsilon\), while \(\|\widehat F\|>\varepsilon+\delta\) guarantees \(\|F\|>\varepsilon\). If \(\varepsilon-\delta<\|\widehat F\|\leq\varepsilon+\delta\), the additive bound alone permits exact residuals on both sides of the stopping threshold and therefore supports neither a guaranteed acceptance nor a guaranteed rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified error radius creates safe acceptance and rejection regions separated by an indeterminate stopping band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is safe below \(\varepsilon-\delta\), rejection is safe above \(\varepsilon+\delta\), and the intervening band is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Three-Way Stopping Decision Under Additive Error

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat F\|\le\varepsilon-\delta\) guarantees \(\|F\|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Margin rule preventing inner or evaluation error from causing premature outer termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the computed stopping residual satisfies \(\widehat F=F+e\), where \(F\) is the exact primal-dual residual and \(\|e\|\le\delta\) is a verified bound incorporating linear-solve and residual-evaluation errors. For a desired outer tolerance \(\varepsilon>\delta\), the strengthened test \(\|\widehat F\|\le\varepsilon-\delta\) implies \(\|F\|\le\|\widehat F\|+\delta\le\varepsilon\). Thus the stopping declaration remains reliable despite bounded inner inaccuracies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping is reliable when the computed residual clears the target by a margin at least as large as the certified inner and evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer Stopping Reliability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The margin rule follows correctly from the stated additive error model, and certificate is the proper role. Nevertheless, the nontrivial stopping-reliability claim has neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Accuracy-Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination between inner linear-system tolerances and outer certificate requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near a solution \(w_*\)
\(F'(w_*)\) is nonsingular and \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz
Inexact steps satisfy the relative residual forcing condition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) gives a linear local regime; \(\eta_k\to0\) gives superlinear convergence; \(\eta_k=O(\|F(w_k)\|)\) gives quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inexact-Newton regimes linking inner forcing terms to outer convergence order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(w_*)=0\), suppose \(F'(w_*)\) is nonsingular, and assume \(F'\) is Lipschitz near \(w_*\). Let \(w_{k+1}=w_k+\Delta_k\), where \(\|F'(w_k)\Delta_k+F(w_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(w_k)\|\). For sufficiently close iterates, a uniform bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) yields a linear local convergence regime. If \(\eta_k\to0\), convergence is superlinear. If \(\eta_k=O(\|F(w_k)\|)\), convergence is quadratic. These regimes require the outer stopping tolerance to retain the error margin used by its reliability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed, vanishing, and residual-proportional inner forcing terms respectively support linear, superlinear, and quadratic local outer convergence under regularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Coupling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated local forcing-term regimes are plausible under the listed regularity assumptions, but their precise convergence-rate hypotheses require an authoritative inexact-Newton theorem locator. The record currently provides none.

children.title: Dense Direct Interior-Point QP Solves
children.top_down_role: Dense direct linear algebra for small and medium QPs.

assumptions_latex: The factorization is intended to solve the stated Newton matrix without modifying it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\not\succ0\implies\text{ordinary Cholesky is not a valid factorization of }K.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness boundary separating dense Cholesky solves from full-space symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unregularized full primal-dual KKT matrix is generally symmetric indefinite, so ordinary Cholesky factorization \(K=LL^{\mathsf T}\) is applicable only when the selected reduced or condensed formulation is symmetric positive definite. Encountering a nonpositive pivot means ordinary Cholesky cannot factor the stated matrix without modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary Cholesky is valid for a positive-definite reduced or condensed system, not for a generic indefinite full KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Cholesky Applicability Boundary

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual Newton system is dense of order \(N\)
A backward-stable dense direct factorization is used
A bounded number of triangular solves follows each factorization
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each interior-point iteration requires \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(N^2)\) storage.

notation.meaning: Order of the assembled dense Newton or KKT matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage cost of assembled dense direct KKT solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the assembled dense primal-dual Newton matrix have order \(N\). A dense direct \(LU\), \(LDL^T\), or Cholesky-type factorization, when applicable, uses \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(N^2)\) stored scalars; each subsequent triangular solve costs \(O(N^2)\). Consequently, if one factorization and a bounded number of solves are performed per interior-point iteration, \(k_{\mathrm{IP}}\) iterations cost \(O(k_{\mathrm{IP}}N^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(N^2)\) peak matrix storage, excluding problem assembly and refinement-dependent extra solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring an assembled dense KKT matrix costs cubic arithmetic and quadratic storage per interior-point iteration; triangular solves are quadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Direct Interior-Point QP Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cubic arithmetic and quadratic storage bounds are standard for dense direct factorization and fit this implementation leaf, but the candidate supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale. A dense linear-algebra locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the full KKT matrix with symmetric pivoting and solve by substitutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a multifrontal or supernodal factorization with frontal dimensions \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\), dense elimination within the fronts has structural upper bounds \(O(\sum_{j=1}^m f_j^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(\sum_{j=1}^m f_j^2)\) aggregate frontal storage. Thus cost is governed by the filled elimination structure and can approach dense cost even when the original Newton matrix is sparse.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fill-reducing permutation alone does not guarantee a stable \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization of an indefinite Newton matrix. Singular or small candidate pivots can require delayed or block pivots, a changed numerical permutation, or declared regularization, introducing fill beyond the symbolic prediction. A direction is acceptable only when its residual against the system actually intended by the algorithm meets tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic-pattern reuse across interior-point iterations for a fixed QP formulation and fixed regularization structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k\succ0\) be diagonal, \(H_k=Q+G^{\mathsf T}D_kG\), and \(K_k=\begin{bmatrix}H_k&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\). With fixed operand sparsity and regularization patterns, the symbolic upper-envelope patterns of \(H_k\) and \(K_k\) are independent of the numerical values in \(D_k\). Thus the symbolic ordering and elimination analysis may be reused, while the numerical factors and pivots must be recomputed at each changed scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive barrier scaling changes Newton-matrix values but not the symbolic upper-envelope pattern, permitting symbolic reuse but requiring fresh numerical factors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse-direct alternative when the condensed primal block is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=Q+G^{\mathsf T}DG+R\succ0\). For \(\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}(\Delta x,\Delta y)^{\mathsf T}=(r_x,r_y)^{\mathsf T}\), compute a fill-reducing sparse Cholesky factorization of \(H\), solve \[(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})\Delta y=AH^{-1}r_x-r_y,\] and recover \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(r_x-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y)\). If \(A\) has full row rank, the multiplier Schur complement is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal block is positive definite, sparse Cholesky and an equality-multiplier Schur complement provide an alternative to indefinite KKT factorization.
assumptions_latex: The factor and Schur solves meet their declared residual tolerances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Guided Iterative Refinement for a Sparse Newton Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement and acceptance of a sparse-direct direction for the intended regularized Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_r d=b\) be the regularized Newton system intended by the algorithm, and let the sparse factors produce \(d_0\). At refinement step \(j\), compute \(\rho_j=b-K_r d_j\), approximately solve \(K_r\delta_j=\rho_j\) with the stored factors, and set \(d_{j+1}=d_j+\delta_j\). When \(\|K_r\|\|d_j\|+\|b\|>0\), define \[\eta_j=\frac{\|\rho_j\|}{\|K_r\|\|d_j\|+\|b\|}.\] Accept only when \(\eta_j\le\tau_{\mathrm{res}}\) and the required primal-dual Newton residual tests hold. If regularization changes an original system \(Kd=b\), also test \(b-Kd_j\); a small residual for \(K_r\) does not certify the distinct unregularized equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine a sparse-direct Newton direction by residual correction and accept it using a normalized residual for the intended regularized system, checking the original equations separately when regularization changes them.
assumptions_latex: The intended regularized matrix \(K_r\) and right-hand side \(b\) remain fixed during refinement.
Residuals are evaluated with the intended matrix at accuracy adequate for the requested tolerance.
Correction solves use the computed sparse factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_j\le\tau_{\mathrm{res}}\text{ certifies the declared normalized residual for }K_r d=b\text{, but not for a distinct unregularized system}.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Guided Iterative Refinement for a Sparse Newton Factorization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Bound from an Inexact Sparse Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori residual decomposition for a computed sparse direct solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}+E\), let \(u\) satisfy \((LDL^{\mathsf T})u=P^{\mathsf T}b+q\), and set \(d=Pu\). Then \[b-Kd=-P(q+Eu),\qquad \|b-Kd\|\le\|q\|+\|E\|\,\|u\|.\] Thus the substitution residual \(q\) and factorization defect \(E\) jointly bound the residual of the intended Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton residual is bounded by the factor-substitution residual plus the factorization defect acting on the computed solution.

notation.meaning: Factorization defect relative to the intended permuted matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Detection and Removal of Redundant QP Equality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies when the equality-constraint Jacobian fails the full-row-rank assumption commonly imposed in equality-constrained QP treatments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be the equality-constraint Jacobian. If $\operatorname{rank}(A)<m$, redundant constraints can be detected by an SVD or a rank-revealing QR factorization of $A^T$ and then removed from the formulation. For large sparse $A$, sparse Gaussian elimination applied to $A^T$ is an alternative, but it is less reliable as a rank-detection procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a quadratic program's equality-constraint Jacobian is not full row rank, redundant constraints can be identified using an SVD or rank-revealing QR factorization of its transpose and removed. Sparse Gaussian elimination is an alternative for large matrices, but is less reliable for detecting rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Redundant rows of }A\text{ can be detected by rank-revealing factorization of }A^T\text{ and removed; sparse elimination is a less reliable large-scale alternative.}

children.title: Matrix-Free Newton Operators
children.top_down_role: Implicit products for primal-dual Newton systems without assembled global matrices.

assumptions_latex: The constituent matrix-vector products are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_H=O(T_Q+T_G+T_{G^{\mathsf T}}+n+m_i)\), with no explicit \(G^{\mathsf T}DG\) storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and auxiliary-storage bound expressed through constituent operator costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If applications of \(Q\), \(G\), and \(G^{\mathsf T}\) cost \(T_Q,T_G,T_{G^{\mathsf T}}\), respectively, then one application of \(H=Q+G^{\mathsf T}DG\) costs \[O(T_Q+T_G+T_{G^{\mathsf T}}+n+m_i)\] operations and requires only work vectors of lengths \(n\) and \(m_i\), in addition to the original operators and the diagonal of \(D\). It requires no storage for the generally dense product \(G^{\mathsf T}DG\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced Newton product uses one application of each constituent operator plus diagonal scaling and vector operations, without storing the reduced matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Operator Application Cost

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succeq0\), and \(H\succ0\Longleftrightarrow\ker Q\cap\ker G=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural conditions inherited by the matrix-free reduced primal operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\succ0\) be diagonal, \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), and \(H=Q+G^{\mathsf T}DG\). Then \[v^{\mathsf T}Hv=v^{\mathsf T}Qv+\|D^{1/2}Gv\|_2^2\ge0.\] Hence \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite, and \(H\succ0\) exactly when \(\ker Q\cap\ker G=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced matrix-free Newton operator is symmetric positive semidefinite and is positive definite precisely when the Hessian and constraint term have no common null direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetry and Definiteness of the Reduced Newton Operator
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry and Definiteness of the Reduced Newton Operator

assumptions_latex: The residual is evaluated with the same implemented operator \(\widetilde K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|b-Kv\|_2\le\|b-\widetilde Kv\|_2+\eta_v\).

notation.meaning: Certified operator-application error bound at the trial vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori exact-residual certification for a tolerance-controlled matrix-free Newton application.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the exact Newton operator and \(\widetilde K\) its implemented approximation. If \(\|(\widetilde K-K)v\|_2\le\eta_v\) and \(\widetilde r=b-\widetilde Kv\), then \[\|b-Kv\|_2\le \|\widetilde r\|_2+\eta_v.\] Consequently, \(\|\widetilde r\|_2+\eta_v\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\|b-Kv\|_2\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The computed residual plus a certified operator-application error bounds the exact Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Residual Bound from an Inexact Newton Operator
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Residual Bound from an Inexact Newton Operator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingularity Criterion for the Augmented Newton Operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solvability criterion for the symmetric augmented operator built from a positive-semidefinite primal Newton action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), and \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(A\) has full row rank and \(\ker H\cap\ker A=\{0\}\). The criterion is unchanged when \(K\) is accessed only through operator products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented matrix-free Newton operator is nonsingular exactly when the equality rows are independent and the primal block has no equality-feasible null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular}\iff\operatorname{rank}A=m_e\ \text{and}\ \ker H\cap\ker A=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity Criterion for the Augmented Newton Operator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint-Consistency Boundary for Symmetric Matrix-Free Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry requirement for reduced Newton operators implemented with separately coded forward and transpose products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an implemented reduced action be \(\widetilde H v=Qv+\widetilde G^{\mathsf T}(D(Gv))\). If the routine denoted \(\widetilde G^{\mathsf T}\) is not the Euclidean adjoint of the implemented forward routine \(G\), then \(\widetilde H\) need not be symmetric even when \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) and \(D\succ0\). Consequently, symmetry-dependent Krylov guarantees cannot be invoked without adjoint consistency or an explicitly nonsymmetric solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separately implemented transpose product must be the actual adjoint of the forward product; otherwise the nominally symmetric Newton operator may be nonsymmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde G^{\mathsf T}\ne G^*\ \Longrightarrow\ \widetilde H\text{ need not be symmetric}

notation.meaning: Euclidean adjoint of the implemented forward operator G.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced and Augmented Matrix-Free Newton Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionally explicit operator form for reduced and augmented interior-point Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), and let \(D\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times m_i}\) be diagonal. Define \[Hv=Qv+G^{\mathsf T}(D(Gv)),\qquad \mathcal K\binom{v}{w}=\binom{Hv+A^{\mathsf T}w}{Av},\] for \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(w\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\). These actions require no explicit formation of \(G^{\mathsf T}DG\) or \(\mathcal K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply reduced and augmented Newton matrices using Hessian, constraint, transpose, and diagonal-scaling products, with separate equality and inequality dimensions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any trial vectors \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(w\in\mathbb R^m\), define the matrix-free reduced and augmented Newton actions by \[Hv=Qv+G^T\bigl(D(Gv)\bigr),\qquad \mathcal K\binom{v}{w}=\binom{Hv+A^Tw}{Av}.\] Each action uses only products with \(Q\), \(A\), \(A^T\), \(G\), and \(G^T\), together with componentwise multiplication by \(D\). children.title: Interior-Point Preconditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Preconditioner families adapted to changing barrier scaling and KKT structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(M^{-1/2}H(\mu)M^{-1/2})=\mu^{-1}\to\infty\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional example showing that an unchanging preconditioner need not control barrier-dependent scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(\mu)=\operatorname{Diag}(1,\mu^{-1})\) for \(0<\mu\le1\) and choose \(M=I\). Then \[\kappa\!\left(M^{-1/2}H(\mu)M^{-1/2}\right)=\mu^{-1}\to\infty\quad\text{as }\mu\downarrow0.\] Thus positive definiteness of \(H(\mu)\) and \(M\) alone does not imply a barrier-independent Krylov bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed identity preconditioner can lose spectral robustness when a Newton scaling grows like the inverse barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Preconditioner Barrier Nonrobustness

assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) is the symmetric positive-definite reduced Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform spectral bounds for the preconditioned Newton matrix yield barrier-parameter-independent Krylov convergence bounds.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral admissibility criterion for reduced positive-definite interior-point systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of preconditioners \(M(\mu)\succ0\) is barrier-robust for reduced systems \(H(\mu)\succ0\) if constants \(0<\alpha\leq\beta<\infty\), independent of the barrier parameter \(\mu\), satisfy \[\alpha v^TM(\mu)v\leq v^TH(\mu)v\leq\beta v^TM(\mu)v\qquad\text{for every }v\neq0.\] Equivalently, the spectrum of \(M(\mu)^{-1/2}H(\mu)M(\mu)^{-1/2}\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\). Under this condition, preconditioned conjugate gradients has the standard convergence factor governed by \(\kappa\leq\beta/\alpha\). Diagonal, block, constraint, and Schur-complement regimes differ by how closely and cheaply they enforce these bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioner is barrier-robust when its quadratic form remains uniformly equivalent to the reduced Newton matrix as the barrier parameter vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Preconditioning Regimes

children.title: Structured Condensing
children.top_down_role: Block elimination exploiting repeated, staged, or application-specific QP structure.

assumptions_latex: Eliminated variables are represented through affine equations in the retained variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Free eliminated directions}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{a single-valued affine substitution is not equivalent}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of exact substitution-based condensing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact substitution condensing requires the retained variables and fixed data to determine every eliminated variable uniquely. If the defining affine equations leave free eliminated directions, no single affine map parameterizes all feasible points and direct substitution can discard feasible solutions. The free directions must instead be retained, parameterized, or removed only after an explicitly equivalent reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitution condensing is exact only when retained variables uniquely determine the eliminated variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Elimination Boundary

assumptions_latex: States are affinely determined by the retained variables.
The objective and constraints are substituted exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat H_U=H_U+\Gamma^{\mathsf T}H_X\Gamma+\text{cross-term contributions},\quad\text{which need not be sparse}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparsity and conditioning tradeoff caused by eliminating structured state variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under an affine substitution \(X=\Phi x_0+\Gamma U+\gamma\), a state quadratic contributes \(\Gamma^{\mathsf T}H_X\Gamma\) to the condensed Hessian. Even when the uncondensed stagewise KKT matrix is block banded, propagation through \(\Gamma\) can make the condensed Hessian and constraints dense. Full condensing therefore reduces dimension while potentially increasing storage, fill, and conditioning difficulty; partial condensing interpolates between the sparse and fully condensed regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating states reduces dimension but can turn a sparse stagewise problem into a dense and more difficult condensed problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Condensing Density Tradeoff

assumptions_latex: There are \(T\) stages with uniform control dimension \(n_u\).
The condensed Hessian is explicitly stored and treated as a general dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_u=Tn_u\), \(M=\Theta(T^2n_u^2)\), and \(W=\Theta(T^3n_u^3)\) for dense Hessian storage and factorization.
review_flags: These are worst-case costs for explicitly stored dense condensed-Hessian algebra, not for forming propagation matrices or solving a constrained augmented system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case retained dimension, dense Hessian storage, and dense factorization scaling after eliminating all states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\) control stages with \(n_u\) controls per stage, full condensing retains \(N_u=Tn_u\) control variables. If the condensed Hessian is structurally dense and explicitly treated as a general dense matrix, its storage requires \(\Theta(N_u^2)=\Theta(T^2n_u^2)\) scalars and its dense factorization requires \(\Theta(N_u^3)=\Theta(T^3n_u^3)\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full condensing retains T times the control dimension and can require quadratic dense-Hessian storage and cubic dense factorization work in the horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Condensing Dimension and Dense-Algebra Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retained-variable count for uniform groups of dynamic stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) stages have state dimension \(n_x\) and control dimension \(n_u\), with fixed \(x_0\) excluded and \(L\mid T\). If states strictly inside each group of \(L\) stages are eliminated while every control and each group-end state are retained, then \[N_{\mathrm{pc}}=Tn_u+\frac{T}{L}n_x.\] Thus \(L=1\) gives \(T(n_u+n_x)\), while \(L=T\) retains \(Tn_u+n_x\); additionally eliminating the terminal state gives the fully control-condensed count \(Tn_u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grouping L stages retains all controls and one state per group, interpolating between uncondensed and nearly fully condensed dimensions.
assumptions_latex: Interior group states are uniquely determined by retained boundary states and controls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{pc}}=Tn_u+(T/L)n_x.

notation.meaning: Number of stages per condensing group.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Condensing Retained Dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual correspondence for block-elimination condensing and reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a Newton system as \[\begin{bmatrix}K_{ee}&K_{er}\\K_{re}&K_{rr}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}d_e\\d_r\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}b_e\\b_r\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_{ee}\text{ nonsingular}.\] Set \(S=K_{rr}-K_{re}K_{ee}^{-1}K_{er}\), \(\widehat b=b_r-K_{re}K_{ee}^{-1}b_e\), and reconstruct \(d_e=K_{ee}^{-1}(b_e-K_{er}d_r)\). Then \[b-Kd=\begin{bmatrix}0\\\widehat b-Sd_r\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus a condensed residual is an original-system residual only under exact eliminated-variable reconstruction; otherwise both original residual blocks must be tested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reconstruction lifts the condensed residual to the original Newton residual; approximate reconstruction requires checking both blocks.
assumptions_latex: The Schur complement and reconstruction use the same stabilized Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b-Kd=\begin{bmatrix}0\\\widehat b-Sd_r\end{bmatrix}\quad\text{under exact reconstruction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Condensed-to-Original Residual Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of staged and one-shot affine elimination in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(e_1=F_1(e_2,r)+f_1\) and \(e_2=F_2r+f_2\) are single-valued affine eliminations. Successive exact substitution into every objective and constraint produces the same reduced QP in \(r\) as first composing the affine maps and then substituting once. Thus exact partial-condensing groups may be merged or subdivided without changing the reduced feasible set, objective values, or reconstructed original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive exact affine eliminations and their one-shot composition produce the same reduced QP.
assumptions_latex: Every elimination map is single-valued and affine.
All substitutions use exact arithmetic and consistent variable ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{condense}_{e_2}\!\left(\operatorname{condense}_{e_1}(P)\right)=\operatorname{condense}_{(e_1,e_2)}(P).

notation.meaning: Successively eliminated blocks and final retained block.

knowledge_statements.title: Associativity of Exact Partial Condensing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condensed quadratic coefficients obtained by restricting a quadratic to an affine elimination graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w=(e,r)=Tr+g\), where the feasible elimination equations uniquely give \(e=Fr+f\) and \(T=[F^{\mathsf T},I]^{\mathsf T}\). Substitution into \(q(w)=\tfrac12w^{\mathsf T}Hw+c^{\mathsf T}w\) gives \[\widehat q(r)=\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}(T^{\mathsf T}HT)r+\bigl(T^{\mathsf T}(Hg+c)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}r+\text{constant}.\] Hence \(\widehat H=T^{\mathsf T}HT\); therefore \(H\succeq0\) implies \(\widehat H\succeq0\), and \(H\succ0\) implies \(\widehat H\succ0\) because \(T\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine condensing restricts the Hessian by congruence and preserves positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: The eliminated variables are uniquely represented by \(e=Fr+f\).
All objective terms are substituted exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat H=T^{\mathsf T}HT,\qquad H\succeq0\Rightarrow\widehat H\succeq0.

notation.meaning: Linear part of the affine reconstruction map.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Restriction Congruence Representation

assumptions_latex: The stage dynamics are linear and uniquely determine eliminated states from the initial state and controls.
Substitution preserves all remaining constraints and objective terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condensed QP has the same feasible controls and objective values as the original structured QP.

notation.meaning: State and control at stage t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of linear dynamic states before an interior-point QP solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dynamics \(x_{t+1}=A_tx_t+B_tu_t+a_t\) with fixed \(x_0\), recursively construct \(X=\Phi x_0+\Gamma U+\gamma\), where \(X\) and \(U\) stack the states and controls. Substitute this affine expression into the quadratic objective and every non-dynamic constraint, producing a condensed QP \[\min_U\ \tfrac12U^T\widehat Q U+\widehat c^TU\quad\text{subject to}\quad \widehat G U\leq\widehat h,\quad \widehat A U=\widehat b.\] Solve the condensed primal-dual equations, then recover \(X\) by forward simulation. Partial condensing applies the same operation within groups of consecutive stages and retains their boundary states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate dynamically determined states, solve the resulting control-space QP, and reconstruct the state trajectory by forward simulation.

children.title: Block Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Partitioned Newton-system treatment based on weakly coupled variable or constraint blocks.

assumptions_latex: Local block solves and Schur updates have no dependencies between distinct blocks.
Communication and scheduling overhead are omitted from the ideal span model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{local}}=\sum_i w_i,\qquad S_{\mathrm{local}}=\max_i s_i.

notation.meaning: Work and span of local block i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal concurrency exposed by independent local elimination and recovery phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If local block \(i\) requires work \(w_i\) and span \(s_i\) to form its Schur update and later back-substitute, then with sufficient processors the independent local phases have total work \(\sum_i w_i\) and span \(\max_i s_i\). The coupling-system solve remains a dependent phase, so useful speedup also requires a manageable coupling block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent local blocks can be processed concurrently, but the slowest local block and coupling solve limit speedup.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Local-Elimination Span

assumptions_latex: The Newton matrix has the displayed bordered block form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular}\ \not\Rightarrow\ B_i\text{ nonsingular for every }i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of independent local elimination in a bordered block Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\) with \(B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N)\), the standard local Schur complement requires every \(B_i\) to be nonsingular. The full matrix \(K\) may nevertheless be nonsingular when a proposed \(B_i\) is singular; independent elimination is then invalid and requires a different partition, null-space treatment, cross-boundary pivoting, or declared regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular full Newton matrix does not imply that every proposed local block is independently eliminable.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Local-Block Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det K=-1\ne0\), while \(B^{-1}\) does not exist.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample to inferring independent local eliminability from full-system nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The symmetric matrix \[K=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular, but its proposed local block \(B=[0]\) is singular. Therefore the Schur complement \(C-E^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}E\) is undefined even though the full system has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular two-by-two bordered matrix can have a singular proposed local block, invalidating independent local elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingular Full System with a Singular Local Pivot
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingular Full System with a Singular Local Pivot

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det K=\det B\det S\) and \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(B)+\operatorname{inertia}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact determinant, inertia, and nonsingularity identities for an independently eliminable symmetric bordered system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\) with symmetric nonsingular \(B\), define \(S=C-E^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}E\). Then \[\det K=\det B\,\det S,\qquad \operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(B)+\operatorname{inertia}(S).\] In particular, \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating nonsingular local blocks transfers determinant, inertia, and nonsingularity information exactly to the coupling Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Determinant and Inertia Identities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative bordered-block reduction obtained by eliminating the coupling block first.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\) with nonsingular \(C\), define \(T=B-EC^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[Tp=f-EC^{-1}g,\qquad q=C^{-1}(g-E^{\mathsf T}p).\] Moreover, \(\det K=\det C\det T\), and, for symmetric \(K\), \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(C)+\operatorname{inertia}(T)\). This reduction is exact but generally couples the formerly independent blocks of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible coupling block may be eliminated first, although this generally destroys local block independence.
assumptions_latex: Permutations and regularization are applied consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is nonsingular}\iff T=B-EC^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\text{ is nonsingular}.

notation.meaning: Schur complement after eliminating the coupling block.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Coupling-Block Elimination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Original-Equation Residual Certificate for Block Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori accuracy test for local elimination, coupling solution, and block recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix},\qquad K\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g},\] define \[r_p=f-Bp-Eq,\qquad r_q=g-E^{\mathsf T}p-Cq.\] Then \(r=(r_p,r_q)\) is exactly the residual of the original bordered system, independently of how the local and coupling solves were performed. Thus \(r_p=r_q=0\) if and only if \((p,q)\) solves that system. When the denominator is positive, a normwise acceptance test is \[\frac{\|r\|}{\|K\|\,\|(p,q)\|+\|(f,g)\|}\le\tau.\] Residual assembly must use the same permutation and regularization as the system whose solution is claimed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reassemble the local and coupling residuals in the intended bordered equations; their combined normalized norm certifies the computed block-decomposition solution.
assumptions_latex: The tested matrix, permutation, right-hand side, and regularization are those intended by the Newton step.
All local and coupling products required for residual assembly are available.
\(\|K\|\|(p,q)\|+\|(f,g)\|>0\) when the normalized test is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p=r_q=0\iff K(p,q)^{\mathsf T}=(f,g)^{\mathsf T},\quad\text{and the displayed ratio certifies the declared normalized residual tolerance}.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Equation Residual Certificate for Block Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign and rank structure of coupling updates generated by positive-definite local blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N)\) with \(B_i\succ0\), and partition \(E=(E_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,E_N^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\). Then every local coupling update \(U_i=E_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i\) is positive semidefinite and \[\operatorname{rank}(U_i)\le\operatorname{rank}(E_i).\] Consequently, \(C-S=\sum_iU_i\succeq0\) for \(S=C-E^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating positive-definite local blocks subtracts a sum of positive-semidefinite, rank-limited updates from the coupling block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_i\succeq0,\quad\operatorname{rank}(U_i)\le\operatorname{rank}(E_i),\quad C-S\succeq0

notation.meaning: Schur update contributed by local block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Local Schur Updates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical execution of independent local elimination, coupling solution, and recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g},\qquad B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N),\] with every \(B_i\) nonsingular, independently compute \(u_i=B_i^{-1}f_i\) and the actions needed for \(E_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i\). Assemble \[S=C-\sum_iE_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i,\qquad h=g-\sum_iE_i^{\mathsf T}u_i,\] solve \(Sq=h\), and recover \(p_i=B_i^{-1}(f_i-E_iq)\) independently. Apply permutations and regularization consistently in assembly, recovery, and residual testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate nonsingular local blocks in parallel, assemble and solve the coupling Schur system, then recover and verify every local direction.
assumptions_latex: The assembled Schur complement is nonsingular
Permutations and regularization are applied consistently
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g}\quad\text{for the intended bordered system, up to the declared solve tolerance}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Block-First Schur Decomposition Workflow

assumptions_latex: After permutation, the Newton matrix has block-diagonal local blocks coupled through shared variables or constraints.
Every eliminated local block is nonsingular, possibly after declared regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the Schur complement system and performing independent block back-substitutions exactly solves the original block Newton system.

notation.meaning: Block-diagonal collection of local Newton matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement decomposition of a block-structured interior-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the Newton equation as \[\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^T&C\end{bmatrix}\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g},\qquad B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N).\] Eliminating the local variables gives \[Sq=g-E^TB^{-1}f,\qquad S=C-E^TB^{-1}E.\] After solving this coupling equation, recover each local block independently by \(p_i=B_i^{-1}(f_i-E_iq)\). The products with \(B^{-1}\) consist of independent local solves and therefore admit parallel execution. This representation remains exact provided the block partition, permutation, and any regularization are applied consistently to both the Schur complement and back-substitution.

children.title: Temporal Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Stagewise decomposition for horizon-based or dynamic quadratic programs.

assumptions_latex: At least one Hessian or constraint term couples stages outside the assumed adjacent-stage band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Nonadjacent coupling}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{the simple block-tridiagonal sweep is not an exact factorization}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of a nearest-neighbor block-tridiagonal temporal sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint or Hessian term coupling nonadjacent stages adds off-band blocks to the time-ordered Newton matrix. The nearest-neighbor recursion is then not an exact factorization unless the state is augmented to absorb the coupling or wider fronts are propagated. Increased temporal bandwidth raises per-stage factorization and storage costs, so linear dependence on horizon alone does not imply a small constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlocal temporal couplings require augmented states or wider elimination fronts and invalidate the simple block-tridiagonal recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Long-Range-Coupling Boundary

assumptions_latex: The time-ordered matrix has block half-bandwidth \(w\).
Required pivots are nonsingular and do not force fill outside the stated band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{fact}}=O(Tw^2p^3)\), \(M=O(Twp^2)\), and \(W_{\mathrm{solve}}=O(Twp^2)\).

notation.meaning: Horizon length, block dimension, and block half-bandwidth.

review_flags: Pivoting or regularization that creates fill outside the band invalidates these bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and factor-storage bounds for a band-preserving temporal direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a symmetric block-banded Newton matrix with \(T\) temporal block rows, uniform block size \(p\), and block half-bandwidth \(w\). If elimination proceeds without pivots or regularization that create fill outside this band, dense-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization requires \(O(Tw^2p^3)\) arithmetic and stores \(O(Twp^2)\) factor entries; forward and backward substitutions require \(O(Twp^2)\) arithmetic. Thus the cost is linear in \(T\) for fixed \(p\) and \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A band-preserving temporal factorization is linear in the horizon for fixed stage size and bandwidth, with explicit bandwidth dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Banded Temporal Factorization Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel Cyclic Reduction for Temporal Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel direct variant for block-tridiagonal temporal Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_td_{t-1}+B_td_t+C_td_{t+1}=r_t\), eliminate all odd-indexed stages concurrently using their nonsingular pivots \(B_t\). Their Schur updates produce a block-tridiagonal system on the even stages. Repeat until one block remains, solve it, and recover eliminated stages in reverse levels. With uniform block size \(p\) and dense block arithmetic, the ideal bounds are \(O(Tp^3)\) work and \(O(p^3\log T)\) arithmetic span.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel cyclic reduction recursively eliminates alternating stages while preserving block-tridiagonal structure.
assumptions_latex: The temporal Newton matrix is block tridiagonal.
Every eliminated pivot at every level is nonsingular.
Communication and scheduling costs are excluded from the ideal span.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W=O(Tp^3),\qquad S=O(p^3\log T).
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Cyclic Reduction for Temporal Systems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy test after temporal factorization and recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After recovering \(d_0,\ldots,d_{T-1}\), evaluate the original-order residuals \[\rho_t=r_t-A_td_{t-1}-B_td_t-C_td_{t+1},\] omitting nonexistent endpoint terms. Accept the direction when \[\max_t\|\rho_t\|\le \varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max_t\bigl(\|r_t\|+\|A_td_{t-1}\|+\|B_td_t\|+\|C_td_{t+1}\|\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check every recovered stage against the original temporal equations using a scaled block residual.
assumptions_latex: The residual is evaluated against the original stabilized Newton matrix and right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed inequality certifies the declared normwise Newton-solve tolerance.}
knowledge_statements.title: Recovered Temporal-Direction Residual Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riccati–Temporal Elimination Equivalence for Linear-Quadratic Stages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riccati representation of block elimination for an unconstrained finite-horizon linear-quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{t+1}=A_tx_t+B_tu_t\) with fixed \(x_0\), stage cost \(\tfrac12x_t^{\mathsf T}Q_tx_t+x_t^{\mathsf T}S_tu_t+\tfrac12u_t^{\mathsf T}R_tu_t\), and terminal cost matrix \(P_T\). If \(M_t=R_t+B_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}B_t\succ0\), backward elimination gives \[K_t=M_t^{-1}(S_t^{\mathsf T}+B_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}A_t),\] \[P_t=Q_t+A_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}A_t-(S_t+A_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}B_t)K_t.\] These are the Schur-complement updates of time-ordered block elimination. After the backward Riccati sweep, the unique solution is recovered by the forward rollout \(u_t=-K_tx_t\), \(x_{t+1}=A_tx_t+B_tu_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite control pivots, the backward Riccati recursion is stagewise Schur elimination, followed by forward state-control rollout.
assumptions_latex: The horizon is finite, the initial state is fixed, and the dynamics are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Riccati recursion}=\text{time-ordered block elimination},\qquad u_t=-K_tx_t.

notation.meaning: Quadratic cost-to-go matrix at stage t.

knowledge_statements.title: Riccati–Temporal Elimination Equivalence for Linear-Quadratic Stages

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sequential factorization of a block-tridiagonal temporal Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block equations \(A_td_{t-1}+B_td_t+C_td_{t+1}=r_t\), \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), omit nonexistent endpoint terms and set \(D_0=B_0\), \(g_0=r_0\). For \(t=1,\ldots,T-1\), compute \[L_t=A_tD_{t-1}^{-1},\qquad D_t=B_t-L_tC_{t-1},\qquad g_t=r_t-L_tg_{t-1}.\] Set \(d_{T-1}=D_{T-1}^{-1}g_{T-1}\), then recover \[d_t=D_t^{-1}(g_t-C_td_{t+1}),\qquad t=T-2,\ldots,0.\] If every \(D_t\) is nonsingular, the recovered blocks solve the original system exactly in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward block-Schur sweep followed by backward substitution exactly solves a block-tridiagonal temporal system when every generated pivot is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: The time-ordered Newton matrix is block tridiagonal.
Every generated Schur pivot \(D_t\) is nonsingular.
All declared stabilization is already included in the displayed blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_td_{t-1}+B_td_t+C_td_{t+1}=r_t\quad(t=0,\ldots,T-1).

assumptions_latex: The QP couples variables only within stages and between adjacent stages.

Hence no point satisfies both the equality and \(s>0\), so the logarithmic barrier \(-\mu\log s\) has no feasible domain for this formulation. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Complementarity Without Solution or Multiplier Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of weak complementarity from other degeneracy notions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12x^2\), the unique solution is \(x^*=0\). With stationarity written as \(x-z=0\), the unique multiplier is \(z^*=0\). The bound is therefore weakly complementary although both primal and dual solutions are unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak complementarity does not imply primal or multiplier nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*=z^*=0\text{ uniquely, while strict complementarity fails}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Complementarity Without Solution or Multiplier Nonuniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise degeneracy relevant to central-path limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point with \(s\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(s_i z_i=0\), index \(i\) is weakly complementary when \(s_i=z_i=0\). Strict complementarity holds exactly when no index is weakly complementary, equivalently \(s_i+z_i>0\) for every inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly complementary constraint has both zero slack and zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i\in\mathcal W\iff s_i=z_i=0,\qquad \mathcal W=\varnothing\iff s_i+z_i>0\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Complementary Limiting Index

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification failure at a weakly complementary path limit.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a weakly complementary limit, fixed positive slack or multiplier thresholds cannot guarantee active-set identification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mu_\delta>0:\ 0<\mu<\mu_\delta\Longrightarrow s_i(\mu)<\delta\ \land\ z_i(\mu)<\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Slack-Multiplier Identification Margin

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak complementarity at the limit prevents a positive primal or dual margin from identifying the active constraint and permits perturbation-sensitive selection on the optimal face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete weakly complementary limit with a positive-dimensional optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x_1,x_2}\ \tfrac12x_1^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1\geq0,\quad 0\leq x_2\leq1.\] Its optimal face is \(F^*=\{0\}\times[0,1]\). The logarithmic central point minimizes \(\tfrac12x_1^2-\mu(\log x_1+\log x_2+\log(1-x_2))\), giving \(x_1(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\) and \(x_2(\mu)=\tfrac12\). The lower-bound multiplier satisfies \(z_1(\mu)=\mu/x_1(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\). Thus \(x_1(\mu)\to0\) and \(z_1(\mu)\to0\), violating strict complementarity. Small objective or constraint perturbations can select different points or faces, so active-face prediction lacks a uniform positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central path can converge with both an active slack and its multiplier tending to zero, making the limiting face perturbation-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Central-Path Limits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit spectral divergence caused by an active inequality under logarithmic scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_1,x_2} x_1+\tfrac12x_2^2\) subject to \(x_1\geq0\), with \(x_2\) unconstrained. Along the logarithmic central path, stationarity and complementarity give \(z_1=1\) and \(x_1z_1=\mu\), hence \(x_1=\mu\). Eliminating the complementarity direction contributes \(z_1/x_1=1/\mu\) to the first diagonal entry of the reduced Newton matrix, while the second diagonal entry remains \(1\). Therefore \[H_\mu=\operatorname{diag}(1/\mu,1),\qquad \kappa_2(H_\mu)=1/\mu\quad\text{for }0<\mu\leq1.\] Thus unscaled Newton systems become increasingly ill-conditioned as the solution boundary is approached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-constraint barrier scaling can create a Newton eigenvalue of order inverse barrier parameter, causing unscaled condition numbers to diverge near the boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Induced Ill-Conditioning

children.title: Regularization-Dominated Interior Steps
children.top_down_role: Loss of model fidelity when stabilization dominates the original QP system.

assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the associated vector norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation regime in which stabilization remains quantitatively subordinate to an invertible original Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be nonsingular, \(d=-K^{-1}r\), and \(d_\delta=-(K+\delta R)^{-1}r\). For any subordinate norm, if \(q=\|\delta K^{-1}R\|<1\), then \[\frac{\|d_\delta-d\|}{\|d\|}\le\frac{q}{1-q},\qquad \|Kd_\delta+r\|\le \|K\|\frac{q}{1-q}\|d\|.\] The estimate supplies no small-error guarantee as \(q\) approaches one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If regularization is a small operator perturbation of an invertible Newton matrix, the stabilized direction remains close to the original direction; the guarantee deteriorates as the perturbation measure approaches one.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Regularization Fidelity Bound

assumptions_latex: \(R\succ0\), and \(K+\delta R\) is nonsingular for sufficiently large \(\delta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic loss of Newton-model fidelity under dominant stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the stabilized direction be defined by \[(K+\delta R)d_\delta=-r,\] where \(R\succ0\) and \(\delta>0\). For fixed \(K\), \(R\), and \(r\), the dominant-regularization limit satisfies \[\delta d_\delta\longrightarrow-R^{-1}r,\qquad d_\delta\longrightarrow0,\qquad Kd_\delta+r\longrightarrow r\quad\text{as }\delta\to\infty.\] Consequently, although \(d_\delta\) exactly solves the stabilized equations, it makes asymptotically no progress on the original Newton equation \(Kd=-r\). A practical interior step is regularization-dominated when stabilization controls its scale or direction while the unregularized residual remains above the required inexact-Newton tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Excessive stabilization can make the computed direction solve mainly the regularizer, shrink toward zero, and leave the original Newton residual essentially unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Dominated Interior Steps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision status classification for convex QPs solved by primal-dual interior methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), suppose a solver returns \((x,y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\) and scaled residual \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}\le\varepsilon\). This inequality is only a backward-error test. If \(\kappa_D\varepsilon\) is not small, it need not imply a small forward error or objective error. Moreover, neither primal infeasibility nor dual infeasibility is established without a separately normalized alternative-system certificate, and unboundedness is not established without a feasible recession direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^\top d<0\). Thus the status must remain numerically ambiguous when these discriminating tests fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small scaled KKT residuals can coexist with large solution error. Without separate infeasibility or recession certificates and acceptable conditioning, the solver must report an ambiguous status.

children.title: Small Dense QP Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes dominated by low overhead and dense factorization costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage model for direct dense QP linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense KKT or reduced system of order \(N\), one dense factorization costs \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic and stores \(O(N^2)\) numbers, while each subsequent triangular solve costs \(O(N^2)\). A run using \(k\) factorizations and \(s\) substitutions therefore costs \(O(kN^3+sN^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(N^2)\) storage, up to method-dependent constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense direct QP solves use cubic factorization time, quadratic substitution time, and quadratic memory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dense cost is \(O(kN^3+sN^2)\) arithmetic with \(O(N^2)\) storage.

notation.meaning: Order of the dense KKT or reduced system.
Numbers of factorizations and triangular solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Direct-Solve Cost Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Environment-relative classification of dense QP workloads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP is in a small dense regime relative to a computational environment when its explicit dense matrices and required dense direct factorizations fit the prescribed memory and latency budgets. Thus “small” is workload-relative rather than a fixed dimension threshold. Density and dimension alone do not select a universally fastest QP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense QP is small when dense storage and direct solves fit the actual resource budget; no fixed dimension cutoff or universal solver winner follows.
assumptions_latex: The principal QP linear systems are treated as dense.
Direct dense linear algebra is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regime membership is determined by resource feasibility, not by an intrinsic dimension threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Operational Small Dense QP Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Method Selection Within the Small Dense Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-selection boundary after dense direct treatment is affordable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within the small dense regime, active-set, interior-point, and direct equality-KKT approaches can all be appropriate. Selection depends on factorization count and type, iteration overhead, degeneracy, warm-start availability, accuracy requirements, and numerical stability. Consequently, neither small dimension nor dense storage alone implies that one paradigm dominates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When dense solves are affordable, method choice depends on iterations, stability, degeneracy, reuse, and accuracy—not density alone.
assumptions_latex: Dense storage and factorization already fit the workload budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No solver-family dominance follows solely from membership in the small dense regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Method Selection Within the Small Dense Regime

assumptions_latex: The QP has \(n\) variables and \(m\) linear constraints, with dense numerical data.
A direct dense factorization is used and fits in memory.
Only a small number of solves is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dominant arithmetic cost is dense factorization, while symbolic setup and iteration overhead are lower-order costs.

notation.meaning: dimension of the dense Newton or KKT system
