knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic cost model for small dense QPs using direct linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=n+m\) be the order of a dense KKT system. A method performing \(k\) dense symmetric-indefinite factorizations and \(s\) triangular solves requires \(O(kN^3+sN^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(N^2)\) storage. In a small dense regime, \(N\) is sufficiently small that this storage and factorization cost are acceptable, while symbolic analysis, sparse data structures, and iterative-solver preconditioning would not reduce the stated dense asymptotic cost. Consequently, method selection in this regime is governed chiefly by the number of factorizations, numerical stability, and fixed per-solve overhead, rather than by fill-reducing ordering or matrix-free scalability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For small dense QPs, direct KKT factorization costs cubic time and quadratic memory; low setup overhead and few stable factorizations dominate method selection.
knowledge_statements.title: Small Dense QP Regimes

children.title: Large Sparse QP Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes dominated by sparsity, fill, and iterative-solve scalability.

assumptions_latex: The QP KKT operator is too large for routine dense storage or factorization in the intended environment.
Sparse direct factors or KKT and preconditioner actions are available.
Inner solves are checked against a tolerance compatible with the outer KKT test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_{\mathrm{direct}}=O(F),\qquad W_{\mathrm{iter}}=O\!\left(j(C_K+C_M)\right)\text{ excluding preconditioner construction}.

notation.meaning: Number of stored entries in the computed sparse factors.
Costs of one KKT-operator and preconditioner application.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime-level cost model for sparse direct and matrix-free convex-QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a large sparse QP regime, sparse direct solution is governed by ordering- and pivot-dependent factor fill \(F\), factor arithmetic, and memory, while a matrix-free preconditioned Krylov solve is governed by operator and preconditioner costs and its iteration count \(j\). If one KKT application costs \(C_K\) and one preconditioner application costs \(C_M\), the application work is \(O(j(C_K+C_M))\), excluding construction. Matrix-free access requires that these actions be available without assembling the full KKT matrix. Outer QP iteration counts alone are not a scalability bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large sparse QP scalability is controlled by factor fill or by matrix-free operator, preconditioner, and iteration costs, not by outer iterations alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Sparse Linear-Algebra Regime

assumptions_latex: The symmetric sparsity graph is a star on \(n+1\) vertices.
Symbolic elimination removes the center before the leaves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{nnz}(K)=O(n),\qquad \operatorname{nnz}(L)=\Theta(n^2)\text{ for the stated ordering}.

notation.meaning: Triangular factor pattern generated by elimination.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fill and iteration-count boundaries for claims of sparse scalability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse input need not have sparse factors: a star sparsity graph has \(O(n)\) edges, but eliminating its center first connects all leaves and creates \(\Theta(n^2)\) factor fill. Conversely, matrix-free storage alone supplies no bound on Krylov iterations; such a bound requires spectral, field-of-values, or comparable control of the preconditioned operator. Thus neither input nonzeros nor avoidance of assembly alone guarantees scalable time or memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poor ordering can turn a sparse star pattern into dense factor fill, and matrix-free storage does not by itself control Krylov convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Input Does Not Guarantee Scalable Algebra
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Input Does Not Guarantee Scalable Algebra

assumptions_latex: The QP KKT matrices are sparse and too large for dense storage.
Sparse direct or preconditioned iterative linear solves are available.
The requested accuracy is measured by a scaled KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scalability is controlled by factorization fill or by iteration count and preconditioner cost, not solely by the number of QP iterations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebra cost model for large sparse convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a large sparse KKT system, a sparse direct implementation stores \(O(F)\) factor entries and incurs an ordering-dependent factorization cost that can range from nearly linear to effectively dense. A matrix-free Krylov solve using \(j\) iterations costs \(O(jS)\) for operator products, plus preconditioner construction and application, and must terminate only when its inexactness is compatible with the outer scaled KKT tolerance. Therefore, a QP method is scalable in this regime only if fill \(F\), or alternatively the iteration count \(j\) and preconditioner resources, remain controlled as \(n+m\) grows. Outer iteration counts alone do not constitute a scalability bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large sparse QP performance is determined by elimination fill or preconditioned iteration counts, together with memory and accuracy requirements, rather than outer iterations alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Large Sparse QP Regimes

children.title: Repeated-Parametric QP Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes dominated by warm starts, persistent faces, and factorization reuse.

children.title: Repeated-QP Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior iterates or faces across a sequence of related QP instances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-family variants of state transfer for compatible repeated QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active-set method, transfer the prior primal point and working set, restore primal feasibility when required, remove constraints that are no longer active or make the working-set equations inconsistent, and complete an admissible working set before invoking the ordinary transition algorithm. For a primal-dual interior method, transfer primal-dual variables only after restoring the method's strict sign domain and acceptable residual conditions. In either variant, fall back to the ordinary initializer when repair fails or is more costly than reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set warm starts repair feasibility and working-set validity; interior warm starts repair positivity and residual admissibility, with fallback to a cold start.
assumptions_latex: The selected base method permits initialization from the repaired state.
All repairs are checked against the new QP rather than the preceding one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred state is used only if it satisfies the chosen method's ordinary initialization requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set and Interior Warm-Start Variants

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Meaning and solver-independent guarantee boundary of repeated-QP warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A repeated-QP warm start transfers compatible parts of the preceding solver state—such as a primal point, multipliers, slacks, a working set, or algorithmic parameters—to initialize the next QP. Components violating the new problem's equations, bounds, signs, independence requirements, or method domain must be repaired or discarded. Once the resulting state satisfies the base solver's ordinary initialization assumptions, that solver's guarantees apply. Warm starting alone gives no unconditional improvement in iterations or work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse compatible prior solver state, repair or discard invalid components, and then rely on the base solver; reuse does not guarantee a speedup.
assumptions_latex: Consecutive QPs have identified variable and constraint correspondences.
The base solver has explicit admissibility conditions for its initial state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A repaired admissible warm start inherits the base solver's guarantees but no universal complexity improvement.

notation.meaning: Retained state from the preceding QP.
Admissible state for the new QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start State and Guarantee Boundary

assumptions_latex: A sequence of convex QPs has compatible variables and constraint indexing.
A previous primal-dual solution estimate is available.
The new iterate must satisfy the interior method's domain requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repaired previous solution is a valid initializer for the next QP, but it carries no unconditional iteration-count improvement guarantee.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: warm starting reuses a prior iterate after restoring positivity and acceptable feasibility
source_gap: no supplied locator directly supports repeated-QP warm starts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual warm start for a compatible sequence of convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the previous estimate \((x^-,y^-,z^-,s^-)\), initialize \(x^0=x^-\) and \(y^0=y^-\), then restore strict positivity by \(z_i^0=\max\{z_i^-,\delta\}\) and \(s_i^0=\max\{h_i-G_i x^-,\delta\}\). If required by the chosen interior method, apply a bounded least-squares correction to \((x^0,y^0)\) to reduce the new primal and dual residuals while retaining \(z^0,s^0>0\). Run the primal-dual method from this repaired point and stop under the ordinary scaled KKT criterion. Output the new primal-dual estimate and retain it for the next problem. Warm starting is beneficial only when the data change is sufficiently small relative to the local solution sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the preceding primal-dual solution, repair positivity and residuals for the new data, then apply the ordinary solver and stopping test.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-QP Warm Starts

children.title: Parametric QP Tracking
children.top_down_role: Solver behavior across QPs governed by an explicit changing parameter.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tracking along a parameter path while a nonsingular active-set formula remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a path \(\theta(t)\), retain the current affine KKT formula while all inactive slacks and active multipliers remain nonnegative. Advance to the first parameter value at which an inactive slack or active multiplier reaches zero, update the candidate active set, and solve the new fixed-active-set KKT system. Simultaneous zero events require an explicit degeneracy rule; an arbitrary single update need not identify a valid adjacent region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Follow one affine solution formula to the next slack or multiplier event, then update the active set; simultaneous events require a degeneracy rule.
assumptions_latex: A continuous parameter path \(\theta(t)\) is specified.
The current active-set KKT system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The current affine formula remains valid up to its first sign-feasibility event; tied events are an algorithmic ambiguity boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-to-Event Parametric Tracking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-inclusive representation of a strictly convex affine multiparametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+C\theta)^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b+B\theta\) and \(Gx\le h+H\theta\), with \(Q\succ0\). For an active set \(I\) whose KKT matrix is nonsingular, its KKT solution \((x_I(\theta),y_I(\theta),\lambda_I(\theta))\) is affine. Its closed validity region is \[\mathcal R_I=\{\theta:G_{I^c}x_I(\theta)\le h_{I^c}+H_{I^c}\theta,\ \lambda_I(\theta)\ge0\}.\] The valid regions are polyhedral and cover the feasible parameter domain. They may overlap at degenerate boundaries, but all valid formulas have the same primal component there; hence the unique optimizer \(x^*(\theta)\) is continuous and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex affine parametric QP has a continuous piecewise-affine optimizer on closed polyhedral validity regions that may overlap at degenerate boundaries.
assumptions_latex: All problem data depend affinely on \(\theta\).
The fixed-active-set KKT system used for each formula is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible parameter domain is covered by closed polyhedral validity regions, and \(x^*(\theta)\) is continuous and piecewise affine.

notation.meaning: Closed validity region for active set I.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Critical-Region Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy-safe continuation across a tied boundary of a parameter path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a parameter \(\theta_0\), let \(E_s\) contain inactive constraints whose slacks vanish simultaneously and let \(E_\lambda\) contain active constraints whose multipliers vanish simultaneously. Form candidate outgoing active sets by adding subsets of \(E_s\) and deleting subsets of \(E_\lambda\). Retain only candidates whose KKT equations admit the required local solution and whose inactive slacks and active multipliers have the correct signs on a one-sided neighborhood in the path direction. Continue with a validated candidate; if no candidate can be validated, report tracking failure rather than applying an arbitrary single pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a tied event, test the relevant add-drop combinations and continue only with an active-set formula valid on the outgoing side.
assumptions_latex: A continuous parameter path and its outgoing direction at \(\theta_0\) are specified.
The tied event sets are finite.
Candidate formulas are accepted only after one-sided primal and dual sign validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Continuation uses a locally valid outgoing KKT regime, or tracking failure is reported.}
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Branching at Simultaneous Events

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of single-valued affine tracking when singular curvature permits multiple optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite affine-parametric convex QP with \(Q\succeq0\) singular, the fixed-active-set KKT equations may be singular and may describe an affine set of primal-dual solutions rather than one affine function of \(\theta\). The optimizer correspondence \(X^*(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin} f_\theta\) can therefore be multivalued. The unique continuous piecewise-affine optimizer conclusion valid under \(Q\succ0\) no longer follows, and an arbitrary optimizer selection need not preserve continuity or piecewise affinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular curvature can make the optimizer correspondence set-valued, so unique continuous piecewise-affine tracking is no longer guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: The constraint system and objective data depend affinely on \(\theta\).
Only parameter values with a nonempty attained solution set are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succeq0\text{ alone does not guarantee a unique continuous piecewise-affine optimizer map.}

notation.meaning: Set of primal optimizers at parameter theta.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Boundary Without Strict Convexity

assumptions_latex: The parametric QP has \(Q\succ0\) and affine dependence on \(\theta\).
On each considered region, the active constraint gradients are linearly independent.
The active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On every region with a fixed valid active set, the optimizer and associated multipliers are affine functions of the parameter.

notation.meaning: active index set on a critical region

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solving a nonsingular fixed-active-set KKT system with affine right-hand side gives an affine solution
source_gap: no supplied locator directly treats multiparametric QPs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-active-set representation for strictly convex multiparametric QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+C\theta)^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b+B\theta\) and \(Gx\le h+H\theta\). For a candidate active set \(I\), solve the equality-constrained KKT equations using \(G_Ix=h_I+H_I\theta\). Nonsingularity gives \(x^*(\theta)=X_I\theta+x_I\) and affine multipliers. The parameter set on which this formula is valid is determined by the linear inequalities \(G_{I^c}x^*(\theta)<h_{I^c}+H_{I^c}\theta\) and \(z_I^*(\theta)\ge0\). Hence the feasible parameter domain is partitioned into polyhedral critical regions, and tracking consists of following the affine formula until one defining inequality becomes tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex parametric QP has an affine optimizer on each polyhedral region where the valid active set remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric QP Tracking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A relevant multiparametric-QP source is required. Moreover, strict inactive inequalities describe region interiors, so they do not by themselves establish a partition of the entire feasible parameter domain, including boundaries.

children.title: Persistent-Face Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance sequences where active-face structure changes slowly or predictably.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondegenerate Sufficient Condition for Face Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local active-pattern stability under continuous QP perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar\theta\), suppose the selected KKT point is locally unique, the active gradients are linearly independent, the active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and every inactive slack is strictly positive. If the QP data vary continuously, then these signs persist in a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood, so the maximal active pattern remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingularity, strict active multipliers, and strict inactive slacks ensure local persistence of the active face.
assumptions_latex: The QP data vary continuously with \(\theta\).
LICQ and active-set KKT nonsingularity hold at \(\bar\theta\).
Active multipliers and inactive slacks have positive margins at \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\rho>0\) such that the maximal active pattern is unchanged whenever \(\|\theta-\bar\theta\|<\rho\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Sufficient Condition for Face Persistence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity Does Not Imply Face Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional convex-QP boundary example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2\), the unique optimizer is \(x^*(\theta)=\max\{\theta,0\}\), which is continuous. The bound is active for \(\theta<0\) and inactive for \(\theta>0\), while at \(\theta=0\) its multiplier is zero. Thus continuity of the optimizer does not imply a persistent active face, and loss of strict complementarity permits a face transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous solution max(theta,0) changes from the bound face to the interior at theta zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimizer continuity is insufficient for active-face persistence.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuity Does Not Imply Face Persistence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial persistence of an optimal face across related QPs in a fixed constraint indexing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP family has a persistent active-face regime at \(\bar\theta\) if there is a neighborhood \(U\) and an index set \(I\) such that a selected optimizer \(x^*(\theta)\) lies in the relative interior of the face described by exactly the maximal active pattern \(I\) for every \(\theta\in U\). This active-pattern formulation remains meaningful when the affine constraint right-hand sides vary. Continuity of \(x^*(\theta)\) alone does not imply persistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face persists when the optimizer retains the same maximal active pattern throughout a parameter neighborhood; continuity alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The QP family uses a fixed constraint indexing and representation.
A selected optimizer exists throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Face persistence is local constancy of the maximal active pattern, not merely continuity of the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Active-Face Regime

assumptions_latex: At parameter \(\bar\theta\), the QP has a unique KKT point.
LICQ and strict complementarity hold at \(\bar\theta\).
The active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular and the data vary continuously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same active face remains optimal throughout a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood.

notation.meaning: active set at the reference parameter

review_flags: source_scope_indirect: locator supports faces but not parametric active-set stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local persistence of an optimal polyhedral face under parameter perturbations.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be the active inequalities at \(x^*(\bar\theta)\). Suppose there is \(\gamma>0\) such that \(z_i^*(\bar\theta)\ge\gamma\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(h_i(\bar\theta)-G_i(\bar\theta)x^*(\bar\theta)\ge\gamma\) for every \(i\notin I\). If the active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular, its local solution depends continuously on \(\theta\). Consequently, there exists \(\rho>0\) such that, whenever \(\|\theta-\bar\theta\|<\rho\), all active multipliers remain positive and all inactive slacks remain positive. The optimal face therefore retains exactly the index set \(I\) throughout that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive active multipliers, strictly positive inactive slacks, and a nonsingular active KKT system ensure that the optimal face persists under small parameter changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Face Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited face definition does not support parametric active-set stability. The statement also needs an explicit convex parametric-QP setting and sufficiently regular parameter dependence.

children.title: Factorization-Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sequences supporting reuse or low-rank modification of numerical factorizations.

assumptions_latex: T\ge1\text{ systems share the same nonsingular coefficient matrix }K.
C_f>0\text{ is the numerical-factorization cost and }C_s\ge0\text{ is one stored-factor solve cost}.
Stored factors remain available and numerically admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{\mathrm{reuse}}=C_f+TC_s,\quad C_{\mathrm{fresh}}=T(C_f+C_s),\quad C_{\mathrm{fresh}}-C_{\mathrm{reuse}}=(T-1)C_f.

notation.meaning: Numerical factorization and stored-factor solve costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized method-selection condition for repeated QPs with reusable factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(T\) repeated QP linear systems share one nonsingular KKT matrix and only their right-hand sides change, factor once and apply the stored factors to every right-hand side. Relative to refactoring for every system, exact reuse saves \((T-1)C_f\). If matrices instead change by structured modifications, an update belongs in the reuse regime only when its construction, application, storage, and validation cost is preferable to refactorization; otherwise refactorization is the applicable route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact same-matrix reuse amortizes one factorization across all repeated solves; changed matrices use this regime only when a validated update is cheaper than refactorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Reuse Regime

assumptions_latex: K\text{ is the matrix represented by the stored numerical factors}.
K_t\text{ is the current repeated-QP KKT matrix}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_t=K\Rightarrow\text{exact numerical reuse};\qquad K_t\ne K\Rightarrow\text{reuse requires a validated update or refactorization}.

notation.meaning: Residual evaluated with the current matrix.
Candidate computed using stored or updated factors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact numerical reuse and symbolic or updated reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unchanged numerical factors are exact for new right-hand sides only while the coefficient matrix remains \(K\). If the current matrix is \(K_t\ne K\), even an unchanged sparsity pattern does not make the old numerical factors valid; applying them generally produces \(r_t=b_t-K_t\hat w_t\ne0\). A changed matrix therefore requires refactorization or a separately validated update. Pattern equality may justify symbolic reuse, but every returned solution is checked using the current matrix and the original QP stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: New right-hand sides permit exact numerical reuse; changed coefficients require a validated update or refactorization, even when the sparsity pattern is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Current-Matrix Validation Boundary

assumptions_latex: Successive QPs have the same KKT coefficient matrix or differ only in identified low-rank blocks.
A numerically stable factorization or update is available.
Residuals are checked against the current QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact matrix reuse reduces each subsequent linear solve to triangular substitutions; low-rank reuse adds update work but still requires stability checks.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unchanged coefficient matrices permit reuse of direct factors across multiple right-hand sides
source_gap: no supplied locator directly treats factorization reuse
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated QPs sharing a KKT matrix or admitting stable low-rank updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every repeated QP produces the same nonsingular KKT matrix \(K\) and only the right-hand side changes, compute one factorization of \(K\); each later dense solve then costs \(O(N^2)\) arithmetic rather than another \(O(N^3)\) factorization. For sparse factors, replace these bounds by costs determined by stored factor nonzeros. If \(K\) changes by rank \(r\), a stable rank-update scheme may be used when its update cost is lower than refactorization. Reuse is admissible only while pivot quality and the residual for the current matrix remain within prescribed tolerances; otherwise the algorithm must refactorize. Thus reuse changes linear-algebra cost, not the KKT stopping requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When repeated QPs share a KKT matrix, one factorization serves many right-hand sides; changed matrices require stable updates or refactorization after residual and pivot checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Reuse Regimes

children.title: Explicit Face Recovery
children.top_down_role: Identification of a final active face from approximate primal-dual information.

assumptions_latex: An approximate primal-dual point and declared prediction tolerances are available.
A candidate-face equality-constrained KKT system can be solved or diagnosed as singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A predicted face is accepted only after the resulting primal-dual point passes the full QP KKT verifier.}

notation.meaning: Inequality rows selected as face equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prediction and validation contract for explicit recovery of an optimal active face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Predict \(I\) from small slacks and multiplier information, solve the QP restricted by \(Ax=b\) and \(G_Ix=h_I\), and accept the face only if the refined point satisfies every original inequality, stationarity, complementarity, and nonnegativity of the selected multipliers within declared tolerances. Otherwise revise \(I\) using violated inactive constraints or invalid selected multipliers, or report that face recovery was not certified. Positive-multiplier thresholding alone is not generally exact: in \(\min\{x^2:x\ge0\}\), the unique solution has an active bound with zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict a face, solve on it, and accept it only after full-QP validation; degeneracy can make multiplier-threshold prediction miss truly active constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Explicit Face Recovery

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\tau>0,\exists k_0:\ \forall k\ge k_0,\ I^*=\{i:s_i^k<\tau,\ z_i^k>\tau\}.

notation.meaning: Active inequality set at the limiting KKT point.
Slack and multiplier estimate for inequality i at iterate k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient local condition for eventual exact active-set recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,z^k)\to(x^*,z^*)\) for a polyhedrally constrained convex QP and let \(s^k=h-Gx^k\). If the limiting KKT pair is strictly complementary, so each inequality has either \(s_i^*>0\) or \(z_i^*>0\), then some fixed \(\tau>0\) and index \(k_0\) satisfy \(I^*=\{i:s_i^*=0\}=\{i:s_i^k<\tau\text{ and }z_i^k>\tau\}\) for all \(k\ge k_0\). Thus the active set is identified after finitely many terms of the convergent sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence to a strictly complementary KKT point eventually separates active and inactive constraints by fixed slack and multiplier thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Threshold Identification under Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Threshold Identification under Strict Complementarity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicted face is accepted only when the refined point satisfies all inequalities and has nonnegative active multipliers within tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((\hat x,\hat z)\), predict \(I=\{i:h_i-G_i\hat x\le\tau\ \text{and}\ \hat z_i\ge\tau\}\). Solve the equality-constrained QP obtained by imposing \(G_Ix=h_I\), together with \(Ax=b\), and compute its multipliers. Accept the recovered face only if the refined point satisfies \(G_{I^c}x<h_{I^c}+\tau\), the active multipliers satisfy \(z_I\ge-\tau\), and the full scaled KKT residual is within the requested tolerance. Otherwise add a violated inactive constraint, remove an active constraint with a sufficiently negative multiplier, and resolve. Stop with a validated face and refined solution, or report that face recovery was not certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict active constraints from small slacks and positive multipliers, solve on that face, and accept it only after primal, dual, and KKT validation.

children.title: Solution-Polishing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Refinement on a recovered face to improve solution and certificate quality.

assumptions_latex: An approximate solution and a predicted active set \(I\) are available.
The unpolished solver result remains available if polishing is rejected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal X^*\cap\{x:G_Ix=h_I\}=\varnothing\implies x^p\notin\mathcal X^*\text{ for every fixed-face polished }x^p.

notation.meaning: Optimal solution set of the original QP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and failure semantics for post-solve fixed-face refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the equality-constrained KKT system for the predicted face and solve it, optionally using iterative refinement or higher precision. Accept the polished point only if its full scaled KKT evidence improves to the requested tolerance and all original inequalities and multiplier signs remain valid; otherwise retain the unpolished result and report polishing failure. If the imposed face is disjoint from \(\mathcal X^*\), greater arithmetic precision can reduce the linear-system residual but cannot recover an original optimizer without changing the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve accurately on the predicted face and retain the result only after full-QP validation; precision cannot repair a face that excludes every true optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Fixed-Face Polishing

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{bmatrix}Q&A^\top&G_I^\top\\A&0&0\\G_I&0&0\end{bmatrix}\text{ is nonsingular, and a fully validated solution is globally optimal}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-face polishing regime for a nondegenerate convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(I\) is the active set of an optimizer, the rows of \([A;G_I]\) are linearly independent, and \(Q\) is positive definite on \(\ker[A;G_I]\), then the fixed-face KKT matrix is nonsingular. Its solution gives the unique primal minimizer on that face and unique associated multipliers. If the result also satisfies every inactive inequality and has nonnegative active multipliers, it satisfies the full convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a correct, full-rank face with positive reduced curvature, one fixed-face KKT solve yields a unique primal-dual result whose full-QP validation certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Polishing on a Correct Nondegenerate Face
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Polishing on a Correct Nondegenerate Face

The prediction is validated after refinement.

Solve the equality-constrained KKT equations with \(Ax=b\) and \(G_Ix=h_I\), using iterative refinement or higher precision when required, to obtain \((x^p,y^p,z_I^p)\); set \(z_{I^c}^p=0\). Accept the polished point only if \(Gx^p\le h\), \(z_I^p\ge0\), and its scaled full KKT residual and complementarity gap improve to the requested tolerance. If validation fails, modify \(I\) and repeat for a bounded number of trials, or return the unpolished solution together with a polishing-failure status.

children.title: Interior-to-Active-Set Crossover
children.top_down_role: Transitions from interior iterates to explicit working faces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local one-solve crossover at a regular strictly complementary convex-QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let interior iterates converge to a KKT point \((x^*,y^*,z^*)\). If LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive definiteness of the Hessian on the tangent space of the active face hold, and the prediction thresholds separate positive limiting active multipliers from positive limiting inactive slacks, then \(I_k=\mathcal A(x^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). The KKT matrix on this face is nonsingular, and its exact solve returns \(x^*\); no face correction is then required in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular strictly complementary solution, crossover eventually predicts the exact face and completes with one face KKT solve.
assumptions_latex: Interior iterates converge to a convex-QP KKT point \((x^*,y^*,z^*)\).
The reduced Hessian on the active-face tangent space is positive definite.
Prediction thresholds eventually separate positive active multipliers from positive inactive slacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_k=\mathcal A(x^*)\) eventually, and the exact face KKT solve returns \(x^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid transition from a near-central iterate to an explicit working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior iterate satisfying the crossover trigger, form \(I_k=\{i:s_i^k\le\tau_k\ \text{and}\ z_i^k\ge\tau_k\}\). Solve the QP restricted by \(G_{I_k}x=h_{I_k}\), using a rank-revealing solve if the predicted face is degenerate. Validate primal feasibility for every inactive inequality, nonnegativity of active multipliers, and the full scaled KKT residual. If an inactive inequality is violated, add it; if an active multiplier is sufficiently negative, remove its constraint; then resolve. Stop when validation succeeds and output the explicit working face and solution. If bounded corrections do not succeed, reject crossover and continue the interior method from its retained iterate.

children.title: Active-Set Solution Polishing
children.top_down_role: Face-restricted refinement after an approximate interior solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of accepting a face-restricted solve without original-QP validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12(x-1)^2\) subject to \(x\ge0\), the predicted face \(x=0\) has exact face solution \(x^p=0\), whereas the original QP has unique solution \(x^*=1\). With stationarity \(x-1-\lambda=0\), the face solution requires \(\lambda=-1\), violating dual feasibility. Hence a zero face-system residual does not certify a polished solution of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly solved but incorrectly predicted face can be nonoptimal for the original QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^p=0\) solves the face problem exactly but is not a KKT point of the original QP.

notation.meaning: solution of the fixed-face polishing problem

assumptions_latex: An approximate convex-QP solution and a candidate working set are supplied.
The working-set KKT equations admit a stable solution or least-norm solution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated face-restricted solve yields the polished solution; failure of validation leaves the original approximate solution unchanged.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set refinement after an approximate interior-point solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(W\) from the supplied working-set prediction. Solve the equality-constrained QP with \(Ax=b\) and \(G_Wx=h_W\), preferably using residual refinement, to obtain \(x^p\) and working-set multipliers. If some inactive constraint is violated, add a maximally violated index to \(W\); if some working-set multiplier is negative beyond tolerance, remove such an index. Repeat until the original inequalities, multiplier signs, stationarity, and complementarity satisfy the requested tolerances, or until a prescribed correction limit is reached. Return \(x^p\) only after successful validation; otherwise return \(\hat x\) and a polishing-failure flag. This procedure refines a candidate face but does not independently globalize an incorrect starting face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a predicted working set, repeatedly solve the face-restricted QP and correct violated constraints or multiplier signs, accepting only a fully validated refinement.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Solution Polishing

children.title: Interior-Based Active-Face Prediction
children.top_down_role: Prediction of a terminal working set from interior primal-dual information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of positive-multiplier face prediction at weakly active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((s^k,z^k)\to(s^*,z^*)\) and index \(i\) is weakly active, so \(s_i^*=z_i^*=0\). For every fixed \(\tau_z>0\), eventually \(z_i^k<\tau_z\); hence the rule \(s_i^k\le\tau_s^k\) and \(z_i^k\ge\tau_z\) eventually excludes \(i\). For example, the barrier points of \(\min\tfrac12x^2\) subject to \(x\ge0\) satisfy \(x(\mu)=s(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\) and \(z(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\), converging to the active constraint with zero multiplier. Exact full-active-set identification by a fixed positive multiplier threshold therefore requires a separation condition such as strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active constraint has limiting slack and multiplier zero, so a fixed positive multiplier threshold eventually misses it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\notin\{j:s_j^k\le\tau_s^k,\ z_j^k\ge\tau_z\}\) eventually for every fixed \(\tau_z>0\).

notation.meaning: primal slack and dual multiplier sequences

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Activity Identification Boundary

assumptions_latex: The convex QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le b\), with \(Q\succeq0\).
An interior primal-dual iterate satisfies \(s=b-Ax>0\), \(z>0\), and approximate complementarity \(s_i z_i\approx\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicted terminal face is \(F(\widehat{\mathcal A})=\{x:Ax\le b,\ A_i x=b_i\ \text{for all }i\in\widehat{\mathcal A}\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based face prediction for convex inequality-constrained QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\tau_s,\tau_z>0\), form \(\widehat{\mathcal A}=\{i:s_i\le\tau_s\ \text{and}\ z_i\ge\tau_z\}\). Optionally reject an index if adding its row makes \(A_{\widehat{\mathcal A}}\) numerically rank deficient. Initialize a crossover or active-set phase on the face \(F(\widehat{\mathcal A})\). Stop prediction when the set is unchanged on two successive interior iterations, and output \(\widehat{\mathcal A}\). Under strict complementarity and convergence of \((x,s,z)\) to a primal-dual solution, sufficiently separated thresholds identify the terminal active set locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify constraints with small slack and substantial multipliers as active, remove numerically dependent rows, and pass the resulting face to crossover or an active-set solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Based Active-Face Prediction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the threshold rule, rank-repair step, stopping rule, or local active-set identification claim. “Sufficiently separated thresholds” must be quantified relative to limiting active multipliers and inactive slacks. The plain statement also omits the stopping rule and identification guarantee.

children.title: Primal-Dual Iterate Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of approximate primal and multiplier solutions.

assumptions_latex: The new convex QP has the same variable and constraint dimensions as a previously solved instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized point satisfies \(s_i^{\mathrm{init}}>0\), \(z_i^{\mathrm{init}}>0\), and \(s_i^{\mathrm{init}}z_i^{\mathrm{init}}\ge\sigma\mu_0\) for every inequality index \(i\).

notation.meaning: prior primal, equality-dual, slack, and inequality-dual values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positivity-restored reuse of a previous primal-dual QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map the previous iterate into the new problem and set \(s^{\mathrm{init}}=\max\{b-Ax^0,\delta\mathbf1\}\) and \(z^{\mathrm{init}}=\max\{z^0,\delta\mathbf1\}\), componentwise. Retain \(x^0\) and \(y^0\) when dimensions agree, then apply a feasibility-restoration Newton step for the new primal and dual residuals. If necessary, increase selected slack or multiplier components so that \(s_i^{\mathrm{init}}z_i^{\mathrm{init}}\ge\sigma\mu_0\), where \(\delta,\sigma,\mu_0>0\). Use the restored tuple as the first interior-point iterate and terminate initialization after positivity and residual checks pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the previous primal and multiplier estimates, floor slacks and inequality multipliers away from zero, and restore feasibility and complementarity before interior iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Iterate Warm Starts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positivity floors are clear, but the feasibility-restoration Newton step, component adjustments, residual checks, and claimed complementarity bound lack a cited, fully specified method. The record cannot be assessed as a reproducible warm-start algorithm without a source.

children.title: Working-Face Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse or prediction of active-set structure.

assumptions_latex: A nearby QP and a prior or predicted active set \(\mathcal A_0\) are available.
The rows selected for the initial face are required to be numerically independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The warm start supplies an independent working set \(\mathcal W_0\) and a face-feasible initial point whenever the face projection is consistent.

notation.meaning: candidate active set inherited from the nearby problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set initialization from a nearby problem's working face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order indices in \(\mathcal A_0\) by decreasing multiplier magnitude or prediction score. Scan this order and retain an index only when its row increases the numerical rank, producing \(\mathcal W_0\). Project the prior primal estimate onto \(A_{\mathcal W_0}x=b_{\mathcal W_0}\) while enforcing the remaining inequalities. If the projection is inconsistent, remove the lowest-ranked retained constraint and repeat. Initialize the active-set QP method with the resulting point and \(\mathcal W_0\); stop initialization when the face equations and primal feasibility satisfy their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse a predicted active set, discard dependent or inconsistent constraints, project the prior point onto the repaired face, and initialize the active-set method there.
knowledge_statements.title: Working-Face Warm Starts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the ranking, numerical-rank test, constraint-removal policy, or feasibility-preserving projection. The projection objective and tolerances are unspecified, so the claimed face-feasible output is not reliably defined.

children.title: Factorization-Cache Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of symbolic and numerical factorization state across nearby QPs.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{back}}\Rightarrow\widehat w\text{ passes the declared normwise backward-residual test}.

notation.meaning: scaled normwise residual used as a backward-error acceptance measure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori validation independent of whether factors were fresh, reused, or updated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_{\mathrm{new}}w=q\), define \(\eta=\|q-K_{\mathrm{new}}\widehat w\|/(\|K_{\mathrm{new}}\|\,\|\widehat w\|+\|q\|)\) in a declared consistent norm. Cache reuse may be accepted when \(\eta\) meets its backward-error tolerance. A small \(\eta\) does not by itself certify small forward error when \(K_{\mathrm{new}}\) is ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate a reused solve against the current matrix using a scaled backward residual; this does not guarantee forward accuracy for an ill-conditioned system.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backward-Residual Validation of a Reused Solve
knowledge_statements.title: Backward-Residual Validation of a Reused Solve

assumptions_latex: k\text{ is the rank of a supported update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Reuse cost depends on the cache mode: triangular solves for unchanged }K,\text{ numerical refactorization for changed values, and symbolic reanalysis when structural compatibility fails.}

notation.meaning: rank of a supported low-rank coefficient update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost hierarchy for symbolic, numerical, and supported low-rank cache reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With unchanged \(K\), each new right-hand side requires only application of the cached factors. With unchanged compatible sparsity but changed coefficients, symbolic analysis may be reused but numerical factorization is generally repeated. A supported rank-\(k\) update typically requires cached solves involving the update columns and a dense \(k\times k\) correction solve; otherwise refactorization is required. Exact costs depend on fill, pivoting, and factor structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right-hand-side reuse is cheapest; changed values usually require numerical refactorization, while supported low-rank changes add cached solves and a small dense correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Cache Cost Hierarchy

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\mathrm{new}}=K\Rightarrow LDL^T(Pw)=Pq_{\mathrm{new}}\text{ is valid};\qquad K_{\mathrm{new}}\ne K\Rightarrow\text{unchanged-factor reuse is not exact in general}.

notation.meaning: cached permutation and block LDL-transpose factors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for reusing cached numerical factors without modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cached factors of \(PKP^T=LDL^T\) may be reused unchanged for a new right-hand side when the coefficient matrix and factor semantics are unchanged. If any coefficient changes, the cached factors still represent the old matrix unless a mathematically valid update or numerical refactorization is performed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical factors can be reused unchanged across right-hand sides, but coefficient changes require a validated update or refactorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Numerical-Factor Reuse Criterion

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pattern}(K_1)=\operatorname{pattern}(K_2)\nRightarrow\operatorname{factors}(K_1)=\operatorname{factors}(K_2).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cache invalidation boundary beyond the visible sparsity pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality of sparsity patterns is insufficient for numerical-factor reuse. Numerical cache identity must distinguish coefficient values and the scaling, ordering, pivoting policy, regularization, dimensions, formulation, and arithmetic conventions determining factor semantics. Pattern compatibility alone supports only the applicable symbolic analysis, subject to value-dependent pivoting boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matching sparsity pattern may permit symbolic reuse, but numerical reuse also requires matching values and solver conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Identity Includes Numerical Conventions

assumptions_latex: Successive QPs produce KKT matrices with unchanged or closely related sparsity patterns.
A cached permutation and factorization state are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is accepted only if the updated factors pass stability and residual tests; otherwise a fresh symbolic analysis or numerical factorization is performed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarded symbolic and numerical KKT-factorization reuse across nearby QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compare the structural signature of the current KKT matrix \(K\) with the cached signature. If it matches, reuse the permutation \(P\) and elimination tree. When the numerical change is represented by a supported low-rank or diagonal modification, update the cached factors in \(PKP^T=LDL^T\); otherwise refactor numerically with the cached symbolic analysis. Accept the factors only when pivot-growth, inertia, and linear-solve residual tests meet prescribed tolerances. On failure, recompute the numerical factorization, and recompute symbolic analysis whenever the sparsity pattern has changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse ordering and elimination data when sparsity is unchanged, update numerical factors for supported changes, and refactor whenever stability, inertia, or residual checks fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Cache Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The topic and algorithm content kind fit, but no source supports the proposed cache-update workflow or its pivot-growth, inertia, and residual acceptance tests. Their applicability depends on the KKT formulation and factorization method, neither of which is fixed.

children.title: Interior-Point Warm-Start Limitations
children.top_down_role: Centrality and positivity difficulties when reusing boundary-near solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strictly Positive Stationary Restoration Can Be Arbitrarily Noncentral
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional QP family separating positivity and stationarity from central-neighborhood membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\ge1\), minimize \(Mx\) over \(0\le x\le1\), with slacks \(s_1=x\), \(s_2=1-x\) and lower- and upper-bound multipliers \(z_1,z_2\ge0\). The optimum is \((x,s,z)=(0,(0,1),(M,0))\). For \(0<\delta<1\), set \(x_\delta=\delta\), \(s_\delta=(\delta,1-\delta)\), and \(z_\delta=(M+\delta,\delta)\). This point is strictly primal-dual positive, primal feasible, and satisfies stationarity \(M-z_{1,\delta}+z_{2,\delta}=0\). Its complementarity products are \(\delta(M+\delta)\) and \(\delta(1-\delta)\), while \(\mu_\delta=s_\delta^{\mathsf T}z_\delta/2=\delta(M+1)/2\). Hence \[\frac{\min_i s_{i,\delta}z_{i,\delta}}{\mu_\delta}=\frac{2(1-\delta)}{M+1}\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }M\to\infty.\] Thus positivity, primal feasibility, and stationarity do not uniformly restore centrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repaired boundary solution can be strictly positive, feasible, and stationary yet arbitrarily far from every fixed lower-product central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{M\ge1}\frac{\min_i s_{i,\delta}z_{i,\delta}}{\mu_\delta}=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Positive Stationary Restoration Can Be Arbitrarily Noncentral

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Positivity Floors Do Not Preserve Primal-Dual Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual obstruction when boundary slacks and multipliers are independently floored while other warm-start variables are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write inequality feasibility as \(Gx+s=h\) and stationarity as \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y-G^{\mathsf T}z=0\). From a feasible point, retain \(x,y\) and replace \(s,z\) by \(s+\Delta s,z+\Delta z\). The resulting residual changes are \(r_p^+=\Delta s\) and \(r_d^+=-G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z\). Thus independent positive floors generally destroy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flooring zero slacks and multipliers while retaining the other variables generally destroys primal or dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p^+=\Delta s,\qquad r_d^+=-G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Positivity Floors Do Not Preserve Primal-Dual Feasibility

assumptions_latex: A previous solution lies on or near the boundary, so some prior slacks or inequality multipliers are zero or extremely small.
The new problem is to be solved by a strictly feasible primal-dual interior-point method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct reuse can violate positivity or yield \(\min_i s_i z_i/\mu\approx0\); restoration is therefore required and may erase the anticipated warm-start benefit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary and centrality obstruction for primal-dual interior-point warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strictly feasible primal-dual initialization requires \(s>0\) and \(z>0\), while a central-neighborhood condition additionally bounds every product \(s_i z_i\) relative to \(\mu=s^Tz/m\). A boundary-near prior solution commonly has active indices with \(s_i\approx0\) and inactive indices with \(z_i\approx0\). Reusing it unchanged violates strict positivity in the limit and can place the iterate arbitrarily far from the central path. Positive shifts and feasibility restoration repair admissibility, but sufficiently large shifts discard local information and provide no uniform iteration reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prior boundary solution is neither strictly positive nor central. Repairing its tiny slacks and multipliers may require shifts large enough to destroy the warm-start advantage.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Warm-Start Limitations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positivity and centrality obstruction is plausible, but the assertion that restoration may erase warm-start benefit and provides no uniform iteration reduction is nontrivial and uncited. A source must specify the central neighborhood and the scope of the limitation.

children.title: QP Solver Reliability System
children.top_down_role: Cross-paradigm mechanisms governing numerical trustworthiness and reproducible status reporting.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Sections 13.7 and 16.8, Presolving, Perspectives, and Software

children.title: Scaling-Equilibration Methods
children.top_down_role: Transformations supporting stable activity decisions and linear solves.

children.title: Variable Scaling
children.top_down_role: Transformations applied to primal variables to improve numerical balance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(D^TQD)\text{ need not be less than }\kappa_2(Q).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of diagonal coordinate scaling as a numerical heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(D^TQD\) is congruent to \(Q\) and preserves inertia, diagonal scaling need not reduce \(\kappa_2(Q)\), a KKT condition number, or factorization error. Poor scale choices can enlarge coefficient ranges and worsen conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact variable reparameterization can improve or worsen numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variable Scaling Does Not Monotonically Improve Conditioning
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling Does Not Monotonically Improve Conditioning

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde g_L=D^Tg_L,\qquad \widetilde g_L=0\iff g_L=0.

notation.meaning: original and scaled stationarity residual vectors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping of stationarity residuals between original and scaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(g_L(x,y)=Qx+c+A^Ty\), then under \(x=D\widetilde x\) the scaled-coordinate Lagrangian gradient is \(\widetilde g_L(\widetilde x,y)=D^Tg_L(D\widetilde x,y)\). Exact stationarity is invariant, but unweighted componentwise or Euclidean stationarity tolerances generally are not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact stationarity survives an invertible coordinate change, while numerical stationarity norms transform by the transpose scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Covariance Under Variable Scaling

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in[\ell,u]\iff\widetilde x\in[D^{-1}\ell,D^{-1}u].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate mapping for bound-constrained QPs under positive diagonal variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=D\widetilde x\) with \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_j)\) and \(d_j>0\). Bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\) become \(D^{-1}\ell\le\widetilde x\le D^{-1}u\). A linear residual \(Ax-b\) becomes \((AD)\widetilde x-b\) with the same value at corresponding points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal variable scaling transforms bounds componentwise and preserves constraint residual values at corresponding points.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transformation of Variable Bounds and Primal Residuals
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation of Variable Bounds and Primal Residuals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and inertia covariance of an equality or fixed-active-set KKT matrix under an invertible variable change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix}\), let \(x=D\widetilde x\) with nonsingular \(D\), and set \(T=\operatorname{diag}(D,I)\). Then \[\widetilde K=\begin{bmatrix}D^{\mathsf T}QD&D^{\mathsf T}A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_WD&0\end{bmatrix}=T^{\mathsf T}KT.\] Thus rank, nullity, inertia, and nonsingularity are invariant, although numerical condition numbers need not be.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable scaling transforms a fixed-face KKT matrix by congruence, preserving exact rank and inertia but not conditioning.
assumptions_latex: A_W\text{ is an equality or fixed-active-set matrix}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde K=T^{\mathsf T}KT,\quad\operatorname{rank}\widetilde K=\operatorname{rank}K,\quad\operatorname{inertia}\widetilde K=\operatorname{inertia}K.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Congruence Under Variable Scaling

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le b\).
The diagonal scaling matrix \(D\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution is bijective, preserves feasibility and objective values, and maps solutions by \(x^\star=D\tilde x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of variables for a quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(x=D\tilde x\). The original QP is equivalently represented as \[\min_{\tilde x}\ \tfrac12\tilde x^T(D^TQD)\tilde x+(D^Tc)^T\tilde x\quad\text{subject to}\quad (AD)\tilde x\le b.\] Because \(D\) is nonsingular, \(\tilde x\mapsto x\) is bijective, so feasibility and objective values correspond exactly. If \(Q\succeq0\), then \(D^TQD\succeq0\). Primal solutions reconstruct as \(x^\star=D\tilde x^\star\), while constraint multipliers are unchanged because the constraint functions themselves are only reparameterized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular diagonal substitution rescales variables, transforms the Hessian, linear term, and constraint columns, and preserves the QP and its convexity exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal change-of-variables representation is mathematically precise and appropriate for Variable Scaling, but the record supplies only a standard-field rationale and no inspectable authoritative citation. Candidate-review acceptance requires a source with a specific locator.

children.title: Constraint Scaling
children.top_down_role: Row transformations supporting stable feasibility and activity assessment.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |q_i|\le\varepsilon_i\iff|r_iq_i|\le r_i\varepsilon_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation required for absolute row-residual and activity tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q_i=a_i^Tx-b_i\), then the scaled residual is \(\widetilde q_i=r_iq_i\). The test \(|\widetilde q_i|\le\widetilde\varepsilon_i\) represents \(|q_i|\le\varepsilon_i\) exactly when \(\widetilde\varepsilon_i=r_i\varepsilon_i\). Reusing an untransformed absolute tolerance can change feasibility or activity classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute feasibility and activity tolerances must scale with their constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Residual Tests Are Not Row-Scaling Invariant
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Residual Tests Are Not Row-Scaling Invariant

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r(a^Tx-b)\le0\iff a^Tx-b\le0\text{ for all values exactly when }r>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp preservation boundary for componentwise affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplication of an inequality row by a positive scalar preserves it. Multiplication by a negative scalar reverses its direction, multiplication by zero destroys it, and general nonsingular mixing of inequality rows need not preserve the componentwise feasible set. Nonsingular mixing of equality rows has different semantics and is outside this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only positive independent row scalings automatically preserve componentwise inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Inequality Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F(A,b)=\mathcal F(RA,Rb),\qquad\mathcal A_{A,b}(x)=\mathcal A_{RA,Rb}(x).

notation.meaning: active inequality index set at a feasible point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric quantities preserved by positive diagonal constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) with \(r_i>0\), every feasible side and every zero residual is unchanged. Consequently the feasible set, active index set, faces, tangent cones, and exact row rank are unchanged, although row norms and numerical conditioning may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves feasibility, activity, faces, tangent geometry, and exact rank while changing numerical magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scaling Invariance of Active Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT-Certificate Covariance under Positive Row Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between original and scaled inequality KKT certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=b-Ax\), \(\widetilde s=R(b-Ax)=Rs\), and \(z=R\widetilde z\), where \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) and \(r_i>0\). Then \[s\ge0\iff\widetilde s\ge0,\qquad z\ge0\iff\widetilde z\ge0,\qquad A^Tz=(RA)^T\widetilde z,\] and \[\widetilde z_i\widetilde s_i=z_is_i\quad\forall i.\] Thus primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and componentwise complementarity hold for one formulation exactly when they hold for the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled slacks and inversely scaled multiplier coordinates give a bijection between complete KKT certificates of the original and positively row-scaled inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{KKT}(x,s,z)\iff\operatorname{KKT}(x,\widetilde s,\widetilde z).
knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Certificate Covariance under Positive Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Reparameterization under Positive Constraint Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance of the inequality-constrained Lagrange dual under positive diagonal row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax\le b\), define \[L(x,z)=f(x)+z^T(Ax-b),\qquad \widetilde L(x,\widetilde z)=f(x)+\widetilde z^TR(Ax-b).\] The bijection \(z=R\widetilde z\) maps \(\widetilde z\ge0\) onto \(z\ge0\) and gives \(\widetilde L(x,\widetilde z)=L(x,z)\). Consequently \(\widetilde g(\widetilde z)=g(R\widetilde z)\), the dual optimal values agree, and dual optimizers correspond by \(\widetilde z=R^{-1}z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling reparameterizes inequality multipliers without changing the Lagrangian or dual optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde g(\widetilde z)=g(R\widetilde z),\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}_{\widetilde z\ge0}\widetilde g=R^{-1}\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\ge0}g.

notation.meaning: Dual function for the scaled inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Reparameterization under Positive Constraint Scaling

assumptions_latex: The diagonal row-scaling matrix \(R\) has strictly positive diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The systems \(Ax\le b\) and \(RAx\le Rb\) define the same feasible set, with multipliers related by \(z=R\tilde z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal rescaling of QP constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(Ax\le b\) by \(RAx\le Rb\), where \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) and every \(r_i>0\). Positivity preserves each inequality direction, hence the feasible set is unchanged. With original slack \(s=b-Ax\), the scaled slack is \(\tilde s=R(b-Ax)=Rs\). If \(\tilde z\ge0\) is the multiplier for the scaled system, equality of Lagrangian stationarity terms requires \(A^Tz=A^TR^T\tilde z\), so \(z=R\tilde z\). Complementarity is preserved componentwise up to the positive row factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying each inequality by a positive scale preserves feasibility; slacks scale with the rows, and multipliers transform inversely when reconstructing the original KKT system.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive row-scaling formulas, including scaled slacks and the multiplier relation, are internally consistent and appropriate for Constraint Scaling. However, no source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Matrix Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing regimes for Hessian, Jacobian, or KKT matrix blocks.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(RMC)=\operatorname{rank}(M).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic limitation of nonsingular diagonal equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular diagonal \(R,C\), \(\operatorname{rank}(RMC)=\operatorname{rank}(M)\) and \(\ker(RMC)=C^{-1}\ker(M)\). Equilibration therefore cannot remove exact rank deficiency or make a singular system nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal equilibration can rebalance a matrix but cannot repair exact singularity or rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.title: Equilibration Cannot Repair Structural Singularity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{row/column norm balance}\nRightarrow\kappa_2(\widehat M)\le\kappa_2(M).

notation.meaning: spectral condition number of a nonsingular matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance boundary for norm-based equilibration objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equal or nearly equal row and column norms do not imply a smaller spectral condition number, bounded pivot growth, or stable factorization. Those properties also depend on angles, signs, rank structure, pivoting, and the selected norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced row and column norms are not a certificate of good conditioning or stable factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Norms Do Not Guarantee Improved Conditioning
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Norms Do Not Guarantee Improved Conditioning

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: DKD=(DKD)^T,\qquad\operatorname{inertia}(DKD)=\operatorname{inertia}(K).

notation.meaning: numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equilibration form appropriate for symmetric Hessian or KKT matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(K\), \(\widehat K=DKD\) is symmetric and congruent to \(K\). Sylvester's law of inertia gives \(\operatorname{inertia}(\widehat K)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)\), and rank is preserved. Independent left and right scalings generally destroy symmetry unless chosen compatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix should be equilibrated by congruence when symmetry and inertia must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Preserving Congruence Equilibration

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat M=RMC\text{ is returned after at most }K\text{ sweeps, each costing }O(\operatorname{nnz}(M)+m+n).

notation.meaning: accumulated positive diagonal row and column scalings
projection of a positive factor onto the interval from l to u

review_flags: No asymptotic convergence claim is made when clipping remains active; the sweep cap is an explicit termination safeguard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fully specified alternating row-column maximum-norm equilibration variant for a general sparse solver matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R=I\), \(C=I\), and \(B=RMC\). In each sweep, for every structurally nonzero row set \(u_i=\max_j|B_{ij}|\) and update \(R\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{clip}(u_i^{-1},\ell,u))R\). Recompute \(B=RMC\); for every structurally nonzero column set \(v_j=\max_i|B_{ij}|\) and update \(C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{clip}(v_j^{-1},\ell,u))\). Leave zero rows and columns unchanged and report them. Stop after a full sweep when every scalable row and column norm \(q\) satisfies \(|\log q|\le\tau\), or after \(K\) sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately normalize nonzero row and column maximum norms toward one, clip each factor, report structural zeros, and stop at logarithmic balance or a sweep limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Infinity-Norm Equilibration

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_j|(M_\varepsilon)_{ij}|=\max_i|(M_\varepsilon)_{ij}|=1,\qquad \kappa_2(M_\varepsilon)=\frac{2-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of balanced row and column norms to certify spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&1-\varepsilon\\1-\varepsilon&1\end{bmatrix}\), every row and column infinity norm equals one. Its eigenvalues are \(2-\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon\), so \(\kappa_2(M_\varepsilon)=(2-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon\). Hence exactly equilibrated matrices can be arbitrarily ill conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix family has perfectly balanced row and column maximum norms while its spectral condition number diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Matrices Can Be Arbitrarily Ill Conditioned
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Matrices Can Be Arbitrarily Ill Conditioned

assumptions_latex: M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has no zero row or zero column}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e_i^TRMC\|_\infty=1\ \forall i,\qquad \|RMCe_j\|_\infty=1\ \forall j.

notation.meaning: unclipped inverse row-maximum scaling followed by inverse column-maximum scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite behavior of the unclipped alternating infinity-norm variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First scale every row of \(M\) by the reciprocal of its nonzero maximum absolute entry, obtaining \(B\). Then scale every column of \(B\) by the reciprocal of its maximum absolute entry. The resulting matrix \(RMC\) has every row and every column infinity norm equal to one. Thus the unclipped max-norm variant reaches exact balance in one row pass followed by one column pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no row or column is zero and clipping is inactive, one row-normalization pass followed by one column-normalization pass exactly balances all maximum norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Max-Norm Equilibration

assumptions_latex: A matrix \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) represents a QP linear system or KKT block.
Only positive diagonal row and column scalings are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\widehat M=RMC\) has approximately balanced nonzero row and column norms, subject to clipping and structural-zero limitations.

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scalings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative diagonal balancing of solver-system row and column magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R=I\) and \(C=I\). At each sweep, compute nonzero row norms of \(RMC\) and multiply \(R\) by diagonal inverse norm factors; then compute nonzero column norms and update \(C\) analogously. Clip every factor to prescribed positive bounds to avoid overflow and underflow. Leave structurally zero rows or columns unchanged and report them separately. Stop when all scalable row and column norms lie within a chosen multiplicative tolerance of their target, or when a sweep limit is reached. Output \(\widehat M=RMC\) together with \(R\) and \(C\) for postsolve reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately rescale nonzero rows and columns toward common norms, clip extreme factors, stop at balance or an iteration limit, and retain the transformations for reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Equilibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the norm choice, target norms, update factors, clipping bounds, convergence criterion, and treatment of KKT structure define materially different equilibration variants. No citation identifies or supports the stated variant.

children.title: Presolve Redundancy-Reduction Methods
children.top_down_role: Structural simplification and rank cleanup before QP iterations.

children.title: Structural Presolve
children.top_down_role: QP simplifications based on fixed variables, bounds, singleton structure, or removable blocks.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(a)\le b\Rightarrow a^Tx\le b\ \forall x\in[\ell,u];\qquad L(a)>b\Rightarrow[\ell,u]\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum row activities over the current box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural certificate for a linear row over current variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell\le x\le u\), define \(U(a)=\sum_{a_j>0}a_ju_j+\sum_{a_j<0}a_j\ell_j\) and \(L(a)=\sum_{a_j>0}a_j\ell_j+\sum_{a_j<0}a_ju_j\), using consistent extended-real arithmetic. If \(U(a)\le b\), then \(a^Tx\le b\) is redundant over the current box. If \(L(a)>b\), the row and bounds are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval activities can certify that a row is always satisfied or impossible under the current variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interval Certificates for Bound-Redundant and Impossible Rows
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Certificates for Bound-Redundant and Impossible Rows

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha>0\Rightarrow u_j\leftarrow\min(u_j,\beta/\alpha),\qquad \alpha<0\Rightarrow\ell_j\leftarrow\max(\ell_j,\beta/\alpha).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound tightening from a constraint containing one unfixed variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After fixed variables are substituted, a singleton inequality \(\alpha x_j\le\beta\) with \(\alpha\ne0\) implies \(x_j\le\beta/\alpha\) for \(\alpha>0\) and \(x_j\ge\beta/\alpha\) for \(\alpha<0\). Intersecting the implication with the current bound interval is feasibility preserving; an empty intersection certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton row directly tightens one variable bound, with the direction determined by the coefficient sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton-Row Bound Implication

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(v,x_R)=\tfrac12x_R^TQ_{RR}x_R+(c_R+Q_{RF}v)^Tx_R+\kappa.

notation.meaning: fixed and retained variable index sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective and constraint transformation when structural presolve fixes variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(x=(x_F,x_R)\) and fix \(x_F=v\). With \(Q=\begin{bmatrix}Q_{FF}&Q_{FR}\\Q_{RF}&Q_{RR}\end{bmatrix}\), the reduced objective is \(\tfrac12x_R^TQ_{RR}x_R+(c_R+Q_{RF}v)^Tx_R+\kappa\), where \(\kappa=\tfrac12v^TQ_{FF}v+c_F^Tv\). A row \(A_Fx_F+A_Rx_R\le b\) becomes \(A_Rx_R\le b-A_Fv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting fixed variables gives an exactly equivalent smaller QP when the induced linear term, right-hand sides, and objective offset are retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Fixed-Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative repeated application of elementary structural QP reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a queue of rows and variables affected by each accepted change. In a declared deterministic order, test contradictory bounds; classify empty rows; substitute fixed variables with the exact induced objective and right-hand-side updates; propagate singleton-row bounds; recompute interval row activities using exact arithmetic or conservative outward rounding; delete only rows certified redundant by those activities; and enqueue every affected neighbor. Retain infinite bounds symbolically. Any indeterminate floating-point comparison causes retention rather than deletion or an infeasibility declaration. Record every accepted transformation for reverse postsolve.
